Many German consumers have been spooked and unsettled by government attempts to reform the welfare state and corporate environment. While the growth prospects for Liberia are promising, challenges still remain. The country continues to face significant hurdles such as unemployment, poverty, and inadequate infrastructure. Internet search engine users are an odd mix of naive and sophisticated, suggests a report into search habits.
The report by the US Pew Research Center reveals that 87% of searchers usually find what they were looking for when using a search engine. It also shows that few can spot the difference between paid-for results and organic ones. The report reveals that 84% of net users say they regularly use Google, Ask Jeeves, MSN and Yahoo when online.
Almost 50% of those questioned said they would trust search engines much less, if they knew information about who paid for results was being hidden. According to figures gathered by the Pew researchers the average users spends about 43 minutes per month carrying out 34 separate searches and looks at 1.9 webpages for each hunt. A significant chunk of net users, 36%, carry out a search at least weekly and 29% of those asked only look every few weeks. For 44% of those questioned, the information they are looking for is critical to what they are doing and is information they simply have to find.
Search engine users also tend to be very loyal and once they have found a site they feel they can trust tend to stick with it. According to Pew Research 44% of searchers use just a single search engine, 48% use two or three and a small number, 7%, consult more than three sites. Tony Macklin, spokesman for Ask Jeeves, said the results reflected its own research which showed that people use different search engines because the way the sites gather information means they can provide different results for the same query. Despite this liking for search sites half of those questioned said they could get the same information via other routes. A small number, 17%, said they wouldn't really miss search engines if they did not exist. The remaining 33% said they could not live without search sites. More than two-thirds of those questioned, 68%, said they thought that the results they were presented with were a fair and unbiased selection of the information on a topic that can be found on the net. Alongside the growing sophistication of net users is a lack of awareness about paid-for results that many search engines provide alongside lists of websites found by indexing the web. Of those asked, 62% were unaware that someone has paid for some of the results they see when they carry out a search. Only 18% of all searchers say they can tell which results are paid for and which are not. Said the Pew report: "This finding is ironic, since nearly half of all users say they would stop using search engines if they thought engines were not being clear about how they presented paid results." Commenting Mr Macklin said sponsored results must be clearly marked and though they might help with some queries user testing showed that people need to be able to spot the difference.

Following a fruitless 90-minute meeting, negotiations between the government and five public sector unions regarding proposed pension reforms concluded without a resolution. These unions, including Unison, seek the withdrawal of upcoming regulations increasing the retirement age for council employees from 60 to 65, potentially impacting 1.4 million workers who may strike on March 23rd. Despite ongoing discussions slated to restart next week, a Unison spokesperson stated that “at least we are still talking.” With a ballot of 800,000 local government workers beginning soon, and other unions poised to join, the aim is to avert a significant conflict before the general election. Ministers privately view withdrawing the regulations as the more palatable approach, though officials insist the changes will proceed in April. A PCS spokesperson emphasized the potential for further action if the government doesn’t reconsider, criticizing the lack of options presented to workers, highlighting the requirement of working an additional five years to receive their originally promised pension. Unions representing approximately 800,000 members, along with those from the Transport and General Workers’ Union and Amicus, are involved.

A month’s postponement has been announced for incorporating downloads into the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart. Originally slated for March 20th, the change will occur on April 17th to address concerns about fair representation for independent record labels. The British Phonographic Industry (BPI) believes independent music isn’t sufficiently showcased online and aimed to correct this imbalance. Chairman Peter Jamieson emphasized the significance of this move, stating it’s the biggest update to the charts in two decades. Despite the importance of including downloads – overseen by The Official UK Charts Company (OCC), a partnership between the BPI and British Association of Record Dealers (BARD) – the chart launch was delayed after BPI members requested a revised timeline. Downloads will debut in the chart covering the week starting April 10th, mirroring the approach taken by the U.S.’s Billboard Hot 100.

In this paper, we propose opportunistic jammer selection in a wireless
security system for increasing the secure degrees of freedom (DoF) between a
transmitter and a legitimate receiver (say, Alice and Bob). There is a jammer
group consisting of $S$ jammers among which Bob selects $K$ jammers. The
selected jammers transmit independent and identically distributed Gaussian
signals to hinder the eavesdropper (Eve). Since the channels of Bob and Eve are
independent, we can select the jammers whose jamming channels are aligned at
Bob, but not at Eve. As a result, Eve cannot obtain any DoF unless it has more
than $KN_j$ receive antennas, where $N_j$ is the number of jammer's transmit
antenna each, and hence $KN_j$ can be regarded as defensible dimensions against
Eve. For the jamming signal alignment at Bob, we propose two opportunistic
jammer selection schemes and find the scaling law of the required number of
jammers for target secure DoF by a geometrical interpretation of the received
signals.

"Re-Make/Re-Model" is a song written by Bryan Ferry that appears as the opening track on Roxy Music's eponymous debut album.  The recording starts with some brief background ambiance of a cocktail party, before launching into the song. Whilst the basic backing track of guitar, acoustic piano, bass guitar, tenor saxophone and drums is relatively straightforward and traditional in form, other elements of the arrangement are quite bizarre and futuristic: Eno plays continual squalls of atonal oscillator noise using Andy MacKay's VCS3 synthesizer, whilst Ferry's lead vocal style is strikingly distraught and anguished in tone. The lead guitar and saxophone solos in the middle of the song also tend to cacophony. In the song, each instrument is allowed a short solo break in turn; the sax mimics the trumpets from Richard Wagner's opera "the Valkyrie" and the bass guitar solo mimics the riff from the Beatles song "Day Tripper". Phil Manzanera's guitar part reverses the usual guitar pattern: he plays single-note lead guitar all through the song, with no chords, but his solo break consists only of chords.

The impact of radiation damping (RD) on T1 relaxation times observed during inversion recovery experiments was investigated. Our research demonstrates that the magnitude of RD varies based on the sample’s T1 value. Radiation damping difference spectroscopy (RADDSY) helped quantify the severity of RD, alongside gradient inversion recovery (GIR) which was employed for RD suppression in T1 measurements. At 9.4 T, with an RD characteristic time (Trd) of 50 ms, significant RD effects were detected for T1 values exceeding Trd, exhibiting substantial distortions when T1 exceeded approximately 150 ms – results consistent with expected Trd predictions. Furthermore, inconsistencies were noted in previously published calculations of the characteristic RD time.

Line 2 large baking sheets with parchment. In a bowl, combine cheese, herbs and cayenne. Season with salt. On a lightly floured surface, roll out a sheet of pastry to a 16-by-9 1/2-inch rectangle. With the short side facing you, spread half of cheese mixture over bottom half of pastry sheet. Fold top half of pastry toward you over bottom half, enclosing cheese mixture (into 8-by-9 1/2-inch rectangle). Press pastry down to help dough layers adhere and force out air pockets. Roll pastry into a 8-by-16-inch rectangle. Transfer to baking sheet; chill for 20 minutes. Repeat with remaining pastry sheet and cheese mixture. Refrigerate for 20 minutes. Preheat oven to 425°F. Remove 1 pastry sheet from refrigerator and place on a lightly floured cutting board. Place a fresh sheet of parchment on the baking sheet. With a sharp knife, trim uneven edges from pastry, then cut pastry into 32 1/2-by-8-inch strips. Holding 1 end in each hand, twist each strip 3 or 4 times and place 1 inch apart on lined baking sheet, pressing ends down. (You'll fit 10 to 12 twists on each sheet.) Bake twists for 12 to 14 minutes, until golden brown. Transfer twists to wire racks to cool. Repeat with remaining pastry. Serve at room temperature.

To prepare this recipe, begin by combining 7 grams of dry yeast, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and 125 milliliters of warm water in a bowl; cover and let stand in a warm spot for about 10 minutes, or until it becomes foamy. In another bowl, sift together 4 cups (600g) of all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon of salt. Create a well in the center, then incorporate the foamy yeast mixture, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, and an additional 250 milliliters of warm water. Combine these ingredients until a soft dough forms and pull it together into a ball. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover loosely with oiled plastic wrap and allow it to rise for 1 hour. While the dough rises, pulse olives, 50 grams of Parmesan cheese, and 3 chopped garlic cloves in a food processor until finely chopped. Add 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the processor while the motor is running and continue processing until a smooth paste forms. Gently punch down the dough and knead briefly for 1 minute. Roll the dough into a 42 x 35 centimeter rectangle, spreading evenly with the olive paste except for a border along one long edge. Roll the dough up tightly along its length, finishing with the uncovered strip. Slice the rolled dough into 12 pieces and arrange them closely on a greased baking sheet. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes, or until they have risen. Preheat your oven to 200 degrees Celsius and bake for 30 minutes, or until the pastries are golden brown.

“Vibration Cooking: Or, the Travel Notes of a Geechee Girl,” Vertamae Smart-Grosvenor’s 1970 debut cookbook blending recipes and personal narratives, was initially released by Doubleday. Subsequent editions followed in 1986 and 1992, alongside a 2011 publication from the University of Georgia. Following its success, Smart-Grosvenor authored further cookbooks. This work significantly highlighted Gullah culture. Critic Anne E. Goldman noted similarities between “Vibration Cooking” and Jessica Harris’ “Iron Pots and Wooden Spoons,” suggesting both books utilize the individual’s history shaped by colonial influences. Food scholar Lewis V. Baldwin praised the book for its perceptive observations regarding food’s social importance and connection to Southern identity. Notably, it influenced filmmaker Julie Dash to create “Daughters of the Dust,” a critically acclaimed film showcased at the Sundance Film Festival.

We propose and study a task we name panoptic segmentation (PS). Panoptic
segmentation unifies the typically distinct tasks of semantic segmentation
(assign a class label to each pixel) and instance segmentation (detect and
segment each object instance). The proposed task requires generating a coherent
scene segmentation that is rich and complete, an important step toward
real-world vision systems. While early work in computer vision addressed
related image/scene parsing tasks, these are not currently popular, possibly
due to lack of appropriate metrics or associated recognition challenges. To
address this, we propose a novel panoptic quality (PQ) metric that captures
performance for all classes (stuff and things) in an interpretable and unified
manner. Using the proposed metric, we perform a rigorous study of both human
and machine performance for PS on three existing datasets, revealing
interesting insights about the task. The aim of our work is to revive the
interest of the community in a more unified view of image segmentation.

Iconic filmmaker Spike Lee has announced his decision to support up-and-ohming student directors as part of his commitment to fostering new talent in the film industry. Known for his groundbreaking works such as 'Do the Right Thing' and 'BlacKkKlansman', Lee recognizes the importance of educating the next generation of filmmakers.

In a statement released yesterday, Lee revealed his plans to initiate a mentorship program within his production company, 40 Acres and A Mule Filmworks. The program aims to provide aspiring student directors with firsthand industry experience and constructive feedback on their projects, giving them a significant career head start.

The film titan has always been a vocal advocate of diversity in Hollywood and this initiative is no exception. The mentorship program will especially focus on students from underrepresented demographics to ensure the broader cultural perspectives that inform his own work are maintained and expanded upon in the industry.

"Great narrative comes from great diversity and it is important to nurture these varying viewpoints through direct student engagement," Lee said. " I want to provide them the tools and inspiration to create without barriers and ensure that our industry continues its slow but undeniable progression towards true inclusivity."

Lee's decision has been widely celebrated by the industry and educational institutions alike. Many believe that the move will encourage other accomplished filmmakers to follow suit in mentoring the next generation. Some universities have also expressed their interests in collaborating with Lee's program, stating that such initiatives align well with their own mission to equip students with practical skills and experience.

Renowned for his ground-breaking and political storytelling style, the Oscar-nominated director understands that a new narrative can only be brought forth by new voices. Lee's plan not only will boost aspiring filmmakers' careers but also promises to disrupt the conventional storytelling by embracing the wider dimensions of cultural perspectives through film.

The mentorship program is likely to begin in the fall of this year and will cover different aspects of filmmaking – from scripting to post-production. Further details will be announced by Lee himself in due course.

This latest move firmly places Spike Lee as a torchbearer for diversity and equality, actively reaching out to the next generation of storytellers, helping them to voice their experiences and narratives, while challenging the status quo in Hollywood. It emphasizes his dedication to bringing about tangible changes in an industry often criticized for its lack of diverse representation.

On the seventeenth day of the eighth month of the lunar calendar, 1781, an officer named Chutu Wang from Mianchi county, Fujian province, a former Confucian literatus, was on patrol duty during the evening near the Shifang Bridge. An angry mob of people, armed with knives, scythes, and other farming implements, assaulted him after they had surrounded his military wagon. Two of the peasants jumped on top of the wagon and pulled Chutu off the back. They proceeded to beat and stab him to death.
According to an account of the event given by John Dardess, the first scholar to study the incident, Chutu was an important figure in the local administration of Mianchi county, a Confucian scholar who was known to have been a "strait-laced, austere man dedicated to his moral ideals." Chutu's murder was a sign that much of the countryside in late-Ming China had fallen into chaos, so much so that "the death of the local official was not worth a public announcement."
Chutu Wang, after all, had been a Confucian gentry who had received his education in accordance with the principles of Confucius. At the age of seven or eight (in the year 1764) he would have been given the "Three Teachings, Three Obediences" (sanjiao, sanzun) education, where he would have studied, among others, the Confucian classics. He would also have participated in the ritual of rites for dead relatives, and would have prepared for a career in government service and local administration. Furthermore, Chutu would also have been given the Chinese equivalent of an SAT exam, which would have been administered by the Chinese Educational Commission in Beijing. Chutu was appointed to provincial office in Fujian, and by the time of his murder in 1781 had earned the distinction of second-class juren. His murder led to an outcry from high Confucian officials. Some of China's leading Confucians, who gathered in Yangzhou after Chutu's death, demanded the punishment of the four or five ringleaders.

George Steadman Holden (September 29, 1868 – July 9, 1935) was an American football player and manufacturer.  Holden was born in Middlefield, Massachusetts, in 1868.  He was the son of Henry Parker and Mary A. (Holmes) Holden.  He moved to Palmer, Massachusetts, in 1871 when his father purchased interests in several local businesses.  Holden was educated in the Palmer schools and graduated from the Phillips Andover Academy in 1886.  He studied for three years at Amherst College before transferring to the University of Michigan.  He played college football and was the starting quarterback for the 1890 Michigan Wolverines football team.  Holden was a member of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity while attending both Amherst and Michigan.  He graduated from Michigan in 1891.  In March 1896, he married Katherine Cramer of Ann Arbor, Michigan.  They had three children, Roger Cramer Holden, Philip Holmes Holden, and Henry Parker Holden.  He worked in the woolen business in Palmer, Massachusetts, and became the superintendent of the Palmer Woolen Mill in 1895 and the financial manager starting in 1900.  In July 1935, Holden died at his home in Palmer.

Leonora Eyre, an attractive and elegant, but essentially selfish, middle-aged woman, becomes friendly with antique dealer Humphrey Boyce and his nephew James. Both men are attracted to Leonora, but Leonora prefers the young, good-looking James to the more "suitable" Humphrey. While James is away on a buying trip, Leonora discovers to her annoyance that he has been seeing Phoebe, a girl of his own age. Leonora makes use of Humphrey to humiliate Phoebe, and turns out a sitting tenant in order that James can take up a flat in her own house. She does this in an apparent attempt to control his life. While abroad, the bisexual James has begun a relationship with an American, the amoral Ned, who later follows him to London. Ned prises James out of Leonora's grasp, only to reject him for another lover. James attempts a reconciliation with Leonora, but she refuses to give him a second opportunity to hurt her, and settles for the admiration of the less attractive Humphrey. As with all Pym's fiction, the novel contains many literary references, notably to works by Keats, John Milton and Henry James.

Roast one medium, firm eggplant by preheating your oven to its highest setting (at least 500°F). Make two or three slits in the whole eggplant and place it directly on the oven rack for approximately 20 minutes, ensuring the slits face upwards to prevent liquid loss. Combine the cooked eggplant and its juices with garlic, allspice, salt, pepper, and chopped parsley in a food processor; pulse until a smooth paste forms, then drizzle in some extra-virgin olive oil. This creates a “poor man’s caviar” due to the visible eggplant seeds. Serve the eggplant spread alongside slices of a whole grain baguette or similar crusty bread, and consider adding mixed olives and Italian sheep’s milk cheeses nearby for complementary flavors.

To prepare these scones, you’ll need 2 cups of all-purpose flour (about 9 ounces), 1 tablespoon of baking powder, 4 tablespoons of sugar, ½ teaspoon of salt, and 4 tablespoons of cold, cubed butter. Combine the dry ingredients in a food processor, pulsing for 3 seconds until they resemble coarse crumbs (or mix manually with two knives, a pastry blender, or your fingers until similar). In a large bowl, combine this mixture with ¾ cup of heavy cream, 1 beaten egg, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Mix by hand until a smooth, slightly moist dough forms – a stand mixer with the dough hook works well too. Divide the dough into four equal parts; shape each part into a disc about 3/4 inch thick. Gently flatten each disc, creating a slight indentation in the center, then brush with 1/2 teaspoon of milk or cream and sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of sparkling sugar. Cut each disc into quarters. Bake on an ungreased sheet pan or a parchment-lined one at 400°F (200°C) for 15 minutes, or until lightly browned. Transfer the scones to a wire rack to cool, and serve with butter and jam.

Deep learning techniques for image segmentation now deliver near-instant results matching human precision. Despite these improvements, current systems can falter due to poor image quality, distortions, or unpredictable algorithm behavior. Predicting segmentation reliability without reference labels is crucial for both clinical workflows and extensive research to filter out flawed data. Here, we introduce two real-time automated quality control methods specifically designed for cardiovascular MRI segmentations leveraging deep learning. Initially, we trained a neural network on 12,880 images to forecast Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSCs) individually; achieving a mean average error (MAE) of 0.03 on 1,610 test cases and 97% accuracy in identifying low versus high-quality segmentations. Additionally, when ground truth annotations aren't present, we developed a network to estimate DSC scores based on assessed image quality through a novel testing approach, yielding an MAE of 0.14 and 91% accuracy. These predictions provide immediate feedback during scans, allowing clinicians to determine analyzability instantly – facilitating optimized image acquisition strategies for superior outcomes.

Having taught a college course on World War II and having studied extensively with leading historians and interviewed countless survivors representing both sides of the conflict, I believe this film stands as arguably the best depiction of the war yet—rivaled only by “Come and See” and “Schindler’s List.” Last night, I screened it alongside two veterans: a U.S. soldier who battled from Omaha to Czechoslovakia and a German infantry officer who served on the Eastern Front for four years. The German, who encountered Hitler multiple times, immediately praised its meticulous historical detail, noting even Hitler’s distinctly working-class Munich dialect – something unlikely for an American viewer to detect.  My German companion, stationed in East Prussia during the desperate attempt to evacuate over a million civilians before the Soviet advance, was deeply moved, describing the film’s harrowing depictions of hospitals, chaos, violence, and the shocking sight of twelve-year-old children engaged in combat as undeniably authentic. He confessed to being surprised by how much worse the final state of Berlin resembled the devastation he experienced along the Baltic coast, and remains profoundly affected by those memories. The film powerfully illustrates the complete collapse of Germany ("Gotterdammerung") and effectively conveys its grim reality. For parents of young children, the horrifying conclusion concerning Goebbels’ offspring is particularly disturbing.  The film’s central strength lies in its nuanced portrayal of Hitler—avoiding simplistic portrayals of a stereotypical madman; instead, presenting him as a surprisingly complex figure.  I’ve spoken with individuals who knew Hitler personally, including a childhood acquaintance of Goebbels’ eldest daughter, and they consistently describe him as capable of charm, attentiveness, and even courtly behavior, despite his chilling capacity for issuing commands through a deceptively gentle voice.

Max Ferdinand Perutz  (19 May 1914 – 6 February 2002) was an Austrian-born British molecular biologist, who shared the 1962 Nobel Prize for Chemistry with John Kendrew, for their studies of the structures of haemoglobin and myoglobin. He went on to win the Royal Medal of the Royal Society in 1971 and the Copley Medal in 1979.  At Cambridge he founded and chaired (1962–79) The Medical Research Council (MRC) Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB), fourteen of whose scientists have won Nobel Prizes. Perutz's contributions to molecular biology in Cambridge are documented in The History of the University of Cambridge: Volume 4 (1870 to 1990) published by the Cambridge University Press in 1992. Early life and education
Perutz was born in Vienna, the son of Adele "Dely" (Goldschmidt) and Hugo Perutz, a textile manufacturer. His parents were Jewish by ancestry, but had baptised Perutz in the Catholic religion. Although Perutz rejected religion and was an atheist in his later years, he was against offending others for their religious beliefs.

Mountview House is a heritage-listed detached house at 37 Leichhardt Street, Spring Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was originally built in the 1860s with a new wing added in 1882 designed by Andrea Stombuco. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 13 May 2004. History 
The earliest section of Mountview House, a two-storeyed stone residence, is believed to have been erected in the 1860s for Brisbane foreman carpenter Daniel McNaught. A two-storeyed brick wing designed by architect Andrea Stombuco was added in 1882, when the house was converted into a preparatory school for boys. This part of Spring Hill was surveyed officially into suburban allotments in 1856, but was soon subdivided for closer residential settlement by speculative landowners. Along with Kangaroo Point and Petrie Terrace, Spring Hill was among the earliest of Brisbane's dormitory suburbs, attracting wealthier residents to the high land along the ridges, and the less affluent to the hollows in between: Hanly's Hollow (between Wickham Terrace and Leichhardt Street), Spring Hollow (between Leichhardt Street and Gregory Terrace), and York's Hollow (to the north of Gregory Terrace - an area occupied by a number of brick-makers in the 1850s and 1860s, now Victoria Park).

Surface segmentation tackles the task of grouping adjacent pixels into distinct categories using both local characteristics and the shape of the underlying 3D surface. This issue is crucial across fields like hydrology, planetary science, and biochemistry, yet it’s difficult due to two key factors. Firstly, segment boundaries follow surface contours in a topological sense, irrespective of their precise location or orientation. Secondly, the surface's topology varies significantly depending on the level of detail considered. Traditional deep learning approaches, reliant on convolutions and pooling, struggle with this because they focus on regular grid patterns. Therefore, we introduce a method utilizing a contour tree skeleton—a polytree representing the development of surface outlines across various elevations—and employ a graph neural network built upon this hierarchical structure to capture topological variations at different scales. Testing with real hydrological data demonstrates that our model achieves superior classification performance compared to existing techniques.

For this coconut ice cream, you’ll need two 14-ounce cans of light coconut milk, two tablespoons of coconut cream, six tablespoons of pure maple syrup, two tablespoons of rum, one teaspoon of vanilla extract, and one teaspoon of sea salt. Also, gather 25 raw almonds and 1 ½ cups of unsweetened shredded coconut. Ensure your ice cream bowl has been consistently frozen for at least 48 hours. Roughly chop the almonds – I prefer using a nut slapper. Spread the almonds and coconut on a baking sheet and toast them in a hot oven (broiler recommended) for approximately 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until fragrant. Resist the urge to eat the toasted nuts and coconut. In a large bowl, combine the coconut milk, coconut cream, maple syrup (adjusting to your preference—I used eight tablespoons initially, adding two more for sweetness), rum, and vanilla. Taste and adjust the sweetener if necessary. Incorporate the salt, ideally pink Himalayan sea salt. Let the nuts cool completely; don't indulge! Refrigerating the liquid mixture for a few hours is beneficial, though optional. Transfer the mixture to an ice cream maker and follow the manufacturer's instructions. Don't add the nuts or coconut yet; this usually takes around 30 minutes to reach a frozen consistency. Once nearly ready, fold in most of the nuts and coconut, reserving some for garnish. Continue freezing for another couple of hours, or overnight. Before serving, let the ice cream sit for 10 minutes to soften slightly.

She also finds herself confronted by past regrets and realizes the power of forgiving oneself. Ultimately, through these encounters with strangers turned friends, Sarah begins to see her own journey in a new light, and gains clarity on what matters most.

As the characters part ways, they reconnect on a deeper level and continue to inspire each other. The reader leaves with the impression that although they may have started off as strangers seated next to one another at breakfast, their paths are now forever changed - bound together by fate, friendship, and a chance meeting over coffee and a muffin.

The Ambedkar cartoon is an issue that rocked the Parliament of India on 11 May 2012. Both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha were adjourned on that day due to the ruckus created by the opposing parties. The issue was taken up by Thirumavalavan, an MP from the state of Tamil Nadu. He put the issue to parliament (Lok Sabha), but was at first denied permission to speak about it. He then showed a copy of the controversial cartoon that allegedly insulted the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.  In the cartoon, the former Prime Minister of India (Congress), Jawaharlal Nehru, holds a whip and along with Ambedkar is driving a snail, which represents the Indian Constitution. The Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes considered the cartoon to be insulting. The book it appeared in was published by NCERT under the guidance of the Ministry of Human Resources in 2006 under the UPA government headed by Sonia Gandhi (Indian National Congress). Later the HRD Minister Kapil Sibal apologised to the nation with regards to the cartoon. NCERT was also asked to remove the cartoon from their textbooks.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art
performance in many different 2D medical image analysis tasks. In clinical
practice, however, a large part of the medical imaging data available is in 3D.
This has motivated the development of 3D CNNs for volumetric image segmentation
in order to benefit from more spatial context. Due to GPU memory restrictions
caused by moving to fully 3D, state-of-the-art methods depend on
subvolume/patch processing and the size of the input patch is usually small,
limiting the incorporation of larger context information for a better
performance. In this paper, we propose a novel Holistic Decomposition
Convolution (HDC), for an effective and efficient semantic segmentation of
volumetric images. HDC consists of a periodic down-shuffling operation followed
by a conventional 3D convolution. HDC has the advantage of significantly
reducing the size of the data for sub-sequential processing while using all the
information available in the input irrespective of the down-shuffling factors.
Results obtained from comprehensive experiments conducted on hip T1 MR images
and intervertebral disc T2 MR images demonstrate the efficacy of the present
approach.

Kennekuk (approximately 1790–1852), nicknamed the “Kickapoo Prophet,” served as a respected medicine man and spiritual guide for the Vermilion division of the Kickapoo tribe. Primarily residing in East Central Illinois near the Vermilion River, his name is sometimes translated as “the drunkard’s son.” Early in life, he tragically killed his uncle during a drunken outburst, resulting in his exile from the tribe. Wandering through Indiana and Illinois, he sought assistance as a beggar before being accepted by a Catholic priest who instructed him in Christianity. Kennekuk subsequently abandoned alcohol and began advocating for its cessation amongst his people. Eventually, he was reinstated into his tribe, and by 1816, at age twenty-five, he rose to become a prominent chief. Quickly, alcohol consumption within his group decreased, fostering greater unity and productivity.

Throughout his life from 1833 until his passing in 1852, Kennekuk guided a community emphasizing non-violence, abstaining from alcohol, meditative practices, and peaceful coexistence with settlers. He championed a quiet, accommodating approach to westward expansion alongside agriculture. This philosophy led to criticism and separation from other Kickapoo groups. His community’s faith incorporated elements of Christian outreach and attracted converts from the Potawatomi tribe. Kennekuk ultimately succumbed to illness on the Kansas reservation in 1852.

For this recipe, you’ll need 2 pounds of lean beef stew meat or wild game, plus 1/2 pound of suet and 1/2 pound of chopped, candied citron. Combine 3 pounds of Granny Smith apples, 2 pounds of brown sugar, and 4 cups of apple juice or cider. Season with 1 tablespoon each of salt, nutmeg, allspice, cinnamon, and cloves, along with 1 cup of molasses and 1 cup of light corn syrup. Also include 2 pounds of dried currants, 1 pound of golden raisins, and 1 pound of seedless raisins. Add 2 cups of brandy. First, simmer the meat in water until incredibly tender – approximately 1 to 1 ½ hours, then cool and grind it using a food processor or grinder, aiming for around 4-5 cups. Process the suet and citron similarly, adding them to the ground meat. Chop the apples finely and incorporate them into the mixture. In another saucepan, dissolve the sugar in the apple juice or cider over medium heat, then simmer for 5 minutes. Return the meat mixture to the syrup and cook for an additional 10 minutes before stirring in the salt, spices, molasses, corn syrup, fruits, and brandy. Allow to cool, and serve as pie filling or freeze in portions for future meals. This recipe yields roughly 4 quarts, enough for four pies.

7 g dried yeast
1 teaspoon sugar
4 cups plain flour (600g)
1 teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons olive oil
2 cups pitted black olives (250g)
12 cup finely grated parmesan cheese (50g)
3 garlic cloves, chopped
375 ml warm water
1 tablespoon olive oil
Mix yeast, sugar& 125ml warm water in a bowl. Cover and set aside in a warm place for 10 minutes, or until frothy. Sift the flour and salt into a bowl and make a well in the centre. Add frothy yeast, oil and 250ml of warm water. Mix to a soft dough and gather into a ball. Turn out on a floured surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover loosely with greased plastic wrap and set aside for 1 hour until well risen. Process the olives, parmesan and garlic in a food processor until chopped. With motor running add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and process to a paste. Punch down the dough and knead for 1 minute. Roll out to a rectangle 42 x 35 cm. Spread with olive paste leaving a plain strip along one of the long sides. Roll up lengthwise, ending with the plain long side. Cut into 12 slices and place close together on a greased baking tray. To prepare these rolls, begin by combining 1/3 cup of dried minced onion with 1/3 cup of water and letting it sit for 10 minutes until softened. Next, dissolve 1 package (1/4 ounce) of active dry yeast in 2 tablespoons of warm water (between 110° and 115°). In a large bowl, blend together 1 cup of warm 2% milk (also between 110° and 115°), 1/4 cup of toasted wheat germ, 1 tablespoon of canola oil, 1 tablespoon of honey, 1 teaspoon of garlic powder, and 3/4 teaspoon of salt. Add the softened onion mixture and the yeast solution along with 1-1/2 cups of flour, beating until a smooth, slightly sticky dough forms. Gradually add more flour until the dough reaches a stiff consistency. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for 6-8 minutes until it’s smooth and elastic. Grease a bowl, place the dough inside, turn to coat, cover, and let rise in a warm spot for approximately 1 hour, or until doubled. After rising, punch down the dough, divide it into 20 equal portions, shape them into balls, and arrange them in a greased baking dish. Cover with a towel and let rise again for 45 minutes, or until nearly doubled. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until lightly browned. Brush the rolls with melted butter and sprinkle generously with shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese. Continue baking for an additional 5-7 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and the rolls are golden brown. Garnish with minced fresh parsley if desired, and serve warm.

Characterising tractable fragments of the constraint satisfaction problem
(CSP) is an important challenge in theoretical computer science and artificial
intelligence. Forbidding patterns (generic sub-instances) provides a means of
defining CSP fragments which are neither exclusively language-based nor
exclusively structure-based. It is known that the class of binary CSP instances
in which the broken-triangle pattern (BTP) does not occur, a class which
includes all tree-structured instances, are decided by arc consistency (AC), a
ubiquitous reduction operation in constraint solvers. We provide a
characterisation of simple partially-ordered forbidden patterns which have this
AC-solvability property. It turns out that BTP is just one of five such
AC-solvable patterns. The four other patterns allow us to exhibit new tractable
classes.

Manual tumor detection through biomedical imaging can be slow and prone to inaccuracies, leading researchers to explore automated approaches using diverse mathematical algorithms – including statistical analysis, variational methods, and machine learning. This paper introduces a semi-automated liver segmentation technique for 2D CT scans, classifying tissues as healthy, vessels, or tumor via graph cuts. Our method generates pixel features from 59 time-series intensity values and utilizes a streamlined perimeter cost within an energy function. Data and perimeter terms are normalized to accelerate the graph cut computation, eliminating the need for parameter tuning. Instead of requiring training, we leverage pre-defined tissue mean values established by experienced radiologists.  The approach offers computational simplicity and demonstrated strong performance on a clinical dataset of 10 tumors, achieving a mean Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.77 and a mean Volume Overlap Error (VOE) of 36.7%, with an average processing time of 1.25 minutes per slice.

New rules on marriage for foreign nationals living in the UK are coming into force.
From Tuesday, most non-EU citizens will need Home Office approval to marry. The Home Office says the new rules are aimed at reducing the number of sham marriages, of which there are estimated to be up to 15,000 a year. But immigrants' group the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants (JCWI) says the rules breach human rights law and it may mount a legal challenge. When the changes were unveiled last year, immigration minister Des Browne said: "Our aim is to avoid unnecessary disruption of genuine marriages, while providing firm controls to prevent abuse." Under the previous regulations anybody wishing to get married in the UK only had to produce evidence they had been resident in the country for a week and give 15 days notice of the wedding at the local register office.
But from Tuesday all non-EU nationals, apart from citizens of Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Iceland or Norway, intending to wed in the UK must either obtain a visa allowing them to get married before they enter the country or apply for a Home Office 'certificate of marriage approval'. To get a certificate, costing £135, applicants will have to send proof that they have a legal right to be in the UK. Those without a settled status, such as asylum seekers awaiting a decision on their application, will have no right to marry in the UK.
Once they have the necessary documentation, those subject to immigration controls wishing to get married in England or Wales must register their intention to marry at one of 76 specially-designated register offices. They can, however, marry at the register office or church of their choice. Rhian Beynon of the JCWI said the new rules were "not proportionate" and "discriminatory".
"These rules means in some cases the Home Secretary is going to be a marriage registrar of last resort. "We're currently taking a legal opinion on this. We'll be looking for people whose right to marry is breached and we'll be looking at taking a case on this to the Human Rights Court," Ms Beynon said. The new rules have also been called into question by the parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights. In a report published last July the cross-party committee stated there was a "significant risk" the new procedures were incompatible with the right to marry because they introduced restrictions which were "disproportionate". The committee believed the new laws might be incompatible with the Human Rights Act on the grounds of religion, belief and nationality, the report added.
Over the last year immigration service operations against marriages of convenience have been stepped up resulting in a growing number of convictions. In January 25 people who took part in a sham marriage network based in Leicester were jailed for a total of 35 years. And last November Samuel Amoah, a Belgian national who set up two sham weddings for couples who wanted to remain in the UK, was jailed for three years. Several other cases are currently going through the courts. The role of registrars who under the Asylum and Immigration Act 1999 were obliged to report suspected sham marriages to the Home Office, has been key in many prosecutions. Registrars' spokesman, Mark Rimmer, said they welcomed the new marriage regulations and believed they would be an significant deterrent. "They will effectively remove most of the blatant cases. Certainly those who are illegals in this country, of which we had quite a few, will no longer be getting married," Mr Rimmer said. Mr Rimmer, the service director for registrations of marriages at Brent Council in north-west London, said he did not consider the new law to be an infringement of civil liberties. "It may be seen to be far more draconian than it has been but certainly it's still not as difficult to marry in the UK than it is to marry, for example, in Holland, Germany or France. "I think it's a proportionate response by government to what was a very large problem," Mr Rimmer said.

To prepare this dish, you’ll need 6 boneless, skinless chicken thighs alongside either 6 Toulouse or 6 chipolata sausages – adjust based on your chicken’s size. Also include 250g of streaky bacon (or 250g of pancetta), cut into 6 or 12 rashers according to their shape. You'll also require 200g of orange duck pate. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Flatten one chicken thigh using cling film, aiming for roughly the same width as your sausage. Lay a strip of bacon or pancetta on a cutting board; if using streaky bacon, gently widen it with a knife. Use two rashers per thigh if needed. Place the flattened thigh on top of the bacon, skin-side up. Spread a small amount of pate onto the center portion of the thigh. Wrap a sausage around the pate, rolling it tightly and overlapping the bacon ends at the seam (toothpicks might be helpful to hold it together). Repeat this process for all six thighs. Arrange the rolled dishes on a baking tray and bake for 20-30 minutes, or until golden brown and the juices run clear. Sure! Here's a recipe for Simple Cinnamon Raisin Apple Strudel:

Ingredients:

* 1 package of puff pastry, thawed
* 2-3 apples, peeled and sliced
* 1/4 cup brown sugar
* 2 tbsp granulated sugar
* 1 tsp cinnamon
* 1/4 cup raisins
* 1/4 cup chopped walnuts (optional)
* 1 egg, beaten (for brushing pastry)
* Powdered sugar, for dusting

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix together the brown sugar, granulated sugar, and cinnamon.
3. Add the sliced apples to the bowl and toss until they are evenly coated with the sugar mixture.
4. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
5. Spoon the apple mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
6. Sprinkle the raisins and chopped walnuts (if using) over the top of the apple mixture.
7. Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling, pressing the edges to seal. Use a fork to crimp the edges and create a decorative pattern.
8. Brush the top of the strudel with the beaten egg and cut a few small slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
9. Place the strudel on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
10. Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm. Enjoy!

Note: You can also add a drizzle of honey or maple syrup over the top of the strudel before baking for an extra touch of sweetness.

This paper presents an enhanced graphical interface for Linear Temporal Logic (LTL), designed for the Android platform. This sketch-based interface simplifies LTL control design for users without specialized knowledge. It allows rapid generation of plans fulfilling complex goals through predefined areas of interest. Users can further tailor these plans by sketching reference trajectories, and the system then creates a balanced plan incorporating both the custom paths and the initial LTL specification, alongside demonstrating experimental validation.

The soaring cost of oil has hit global economic growth, although world's major economies should weather the storm of price rises, according to the OECD.
In its latest bi-annual report, the OECD cut its growth predictions for the world's main industrialised regions. US growth would reach 4.4% in 2004, but fall to 3.3% next year from a previous estimate of 3.7%, the OECD said. However, the Paris-based economics think tank said it believed the global economy could still regain momentum.
Forecasts for Japanese growth were also scaled back to 4.0% from 4.4% this year and 2.1% from 2.8% in 2005. But the outlook was worst for the 12-member eurozone bloc, with already sluggish growth forecasts slipping to 1.8% from 2.0% this year and 1.9% from 2.4% in 2005, the OECD said. Overall, the report forecast total growth of 3.6% in 2004 for the 30 member countries of the OECD, slipping to 2.9% next year before recovering to 3.1% in 2006. "There are nonetheless good reasons to believe that despite recent oil price turbulence the world economy will regain momentum in a not-too-distant future," said Jean-Philippe Cotis, the OECD's chief economist. The price of crude is about 50% higher than it was at the start of 2004, but down on the record high of $55.67 set in late October.
A dip in oil prices and improving jobs prospects would improve consumer confidence and spending, the OECD said. "The oil shock is not enormous by historical standards - we have seen worse in the seventies. If the oil price does not rise any further, then we think the shock can be absorbed within the next few quarters," Vincent Koen, a senior economist with the OECD, told the BBC's World Business Report. "The recovery that was underway, and has been interrupted a bit by the oil shock this year, would then regain momentum in the course of 2005." China's booming economy and a "spectacular comeback" in Japan - albeit one that has faltered in recent months - would help world economic recovery, the OECD said. "Supported by strong balance sheets and high profits, the recovery of business investment should continue in North America and start in earnest in Europe," it added. However, the report warned: "It remains to be seen whether continental Europe will play a strong supportive role through a marked upswing of final domestic demand." The OECD highlighted current depressed household expenditure in Germany and the eurozone's over-reliance on export-led growth.

To prepare this meatloaf, you’ll need 1 pound of extra lean ground beef and 12 pounds of ground turkey breast, plus 1 egg, 2 tablespoons of ketchup, 2 tablespoons of barbecue sauce, 1 teaspoon of liquid smoke, 1/4 teaspoon dried parsley, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 cup of oatmeal, 1 cup of crushed tomatoes, 12 medium diced white onions, 12 large diced green bell peppers, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 3 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, 1/4 tablespoon yellow mustard, 2 tablespoons of brown sugar, 1 tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon of liquid smoke, 1/2 cup of ketchup, 1/2 cup of barbecue sauce. A Pitcher of Bloodies
1/2 cup celery leaves
1 clove garlic, peeled and gently crushed
Coarse sea salt
12 ounces vodka
24 ounces tomato passata, or best quality tomato juice
2 ounces freshly squeezed lemon juice
1 ounce freshly squeezed lime juice
3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
2 teaspoons hot sauce, or to taste
2 tablespoons freshly grated horseradish, or best quality prepared horseradish
freshly ground black pepper
The Garnish Bar
Add the celery leaves, garlic, and a pinch of salt to a large measuring cup. Muddle gently, then add the vodka. Continue muddling until the celery leaves release their aroma. Strain, discarding the solids. Pour the passata (or juice, if using) into a pitcher. Pour the infused vodka into the empty bottle, shaking to loosen any passata that is clinging to the inside, then pour it into the pitcher. Add the lemon and lime juices, the balsamic vinegar, the hot sauce, and the horseradish. Stir well, and add another pinch of salt and plenty of fresh black pepper, stirring again to incorporate. Chill for at least 30 minutes, and serve over ice with your favorite garnish(es). I like to give my fellow revelers options, so I set out a variety of garnishes: lemon and lime wedges, fat green olives, tart cornichons, celery stalks, pickled green tomatoes, pickled green beans, cocktail onions, pickled green chile peppers, plus additional hot sauce for those who like a little extra kick in their drink.

In this paper, a new approach for sign language recognition system using image segmentation is presented. The proposed method utilizes a topological derivative based approach combined with an isotropic filter to segment the sign language images. The isotropic filter is used to enhance the image quality and remove noise, while the topological derivative is used to identify the boundaries of the sign language gestures. The segmentation results are then used as input for a sign language recognition system, which can accurately recognize and interpret different sign language gestures. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Health Secretary Alan Milburn has defended his decision to launch an advertising campaign featuring posters showing graphic images of smoking-related illnesses, saying it is necessary to shock people into quitting.
The controversial posters show rotting teeth, cancerous lungs and amputated limbs in an effort to discourage smokers from lighting up. Critics have argued that they are too gruesome but Mr Milburn insists that tough measures are needed to reduce Britain's high smoking rates.
"We know these images can be disturbing," he said, "but we also know that sometimes it takes something shocking to make people take notice."
According to government figures, around 80% of lung cancer cases and 90% of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) cases could be prevented if everyone quit smoking. The new ad campaign forms part of a £20 million initiative aimed at encouraging more people to give up cigarettes.
Mr Milburn acknowledged that some individuals may find the imagery offensive but stressed that ultimately the aim was to save lives. "I understand why some people might think this approach goes too far," he added, "But when you consider what smoking does to your health – and worse still, the impact on those closest to you - I believe there is no such thing as going too far when it comes to protecting people's wellbeing."

A prescription cannabis drug made by UK biotech firm GW Pharmaceuticals is set to be approved in Canada.
The drug is used to treat the central nervous system and alleviate the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS). A few weeks ago, shares in GW Pharma lost a third of their value after UK regulators said they wanted more evidence about the drug's benefits. But now Canadian authorities have said the Sativex drug will be considered for approval.
Approximately 50,000 people in Canada have been diagnosed with MS and 85,000 people are suffering from the condition in the UK. Many patients already smoke cannabis to relieve their symptoms.
Now, GW Pharma's Sativex mouth spray could be legally available to MS sufferers in Canada within the next few months. This will be the first time a cannabis-based drug has been approved anywhere in the world, representing a landmark for GW Pharma and for patients with MS. Final approval in Canada should now be little more than a formality, analysts said, and the company expects full approval for Sativex early in 2005. "We are delighted to receive this qualifying notice from Health Canada and look forward to receiving regulatory approval for Sativex in Canada in the early part of 2005," said GW Pharma executive chairman Dr Geoffrey Guy.
The UK government granted GW Pharma a licence to grow the cannabis plant for medical research purposes. Satifex consists of a cannabis extract containing tetrahydrocannabinol and cannabidiol, a cocktail that has also proved effective in treating patients with arthritis. Thousands of plants are grown at a secret location somewhere in the English countryside. Despite hopes of regulatory approval last year, a series of delays has put back Sativex's launch in the UK. The latest news sent shares in GW Pharma up 8.5p, or 8.1%, to 113.5p.

Deep learning’s popularity in biomedical image segmentation faces a significant hurdle due to domain shift—the difference between datasets can drastically reduce model accuracy when applied to new data with varied characteristics.  To combat this, we introduce a unique unsupervised domain adaptation network designed to transfer knowledge from labeled source domains to unlabeled target domains for cross-modal biomedical image segmentation. Our system utilizes two core components: a conditional domain discriminator (CDD), inspired by conditional domain adversarial networks, which effectively handles intricate cross-modality imagery, and a category-centric prototype aligner (CCPA), enhanced from graph-induced prototype alignment techniques used in object detection. This aligns instances based on detailed feature representations and mitigates class imbalance using an entropy-based loss function. Experiments on a standard cardiac substructure segmentation dataset show substantial improvements in performance on the target domain using our proposed method.

He returned to Romania and founded a series of companies, including a pharmaceutical company, a construction company, and an investment company.

In 2012, Gruia was elected to the Romanian Senate as a member of the Democratic Liberal Party. He served as the party's leader from 2014 to 2015 and has been the president of the National Liberal Party since 2021.

Gruia has also been involved in charitable work, founding the Gruia Family Foundation in 2009. The foundation works to improve the education and health care of Romanian children.

Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 medium beets, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 4 cups arugula, washed and dried
- 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 1/4 cup chopped walnuts
- 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion

For the blue cheese dressing:
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Toss the beets with olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
3. Spread the beets out on a baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
4. In a large bowl, combine the roasted beets, arugula, blue cheese, walnuts, and red onion.
5. To make the blue cheese dressing, whisk together mayonnaise, blue cheese, apple cider vinegar, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until smooth.
6. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy your delicious and healthy Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing!

Incorporating multi-scale features in fully convolutional neural networks
(FCNs) has been a key element to achieving state-of-the-art performance on
semantic image segmentation. One common way to extract multi-scale features is
to feed multiple resized input images to a shared deep network and then merge
the resulting features for pixelwise classification. In this work, we propose
an attention mechanism that learns to softly weight the multi-scale features at
each pixel location. We adapt a state-of-the-art semantic image segmentation
model, which we jointly train with multi-scale input images and the attention
model. The proposed attention model not only outperforms average- and
max-pooling, but allows us to diagnostically visualize the importance of
features at different positions and scales. Moreover, we show that adding extra
supervision to the output at each scale is essential to achieving excellent
performance when merging multi-scale features. We demonstrate the effectiveness
of our model with extensive experiments on three challenging datasets,
including PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012 and a subset of MS-COCO 2014.

Nasdaq, the operator of the influential Nasdaq stock index, intends to offer shares to the public and become publicly traded on its own exchange.  A filing with the SEC indicates they aim to generate $100 million (£52 million) through this offering. While some analysts believe this signals a move toward a complete IPO, Nasdaq previously dampened speculation about a full public listing. Initially, Nasdaq conducted private share sales in 2000 and 2001, achieving a limited public debut in 2002 via the OTC Bulletin Board. Importantly, the company won't receive proceeds from the current sale; instead, profits will accrue solely to existing shareholders from earlier private placements. As an index comprising technology and rapidly expanding businesses, Nasdaq became synonymous with the late 1990s’ technological surge before experiencing a significant decline following the dot-com crash. Recent gains among major tech companies like Intel and resilient firms like Amazon have contributed to its recent resurgence.

Wander not dear- blow with the fair breeze & fly the high seas,
All the fretting & sulking stoked, to find an enduring harmony in me,
Wander not into sounds that trick, with their spirited agonies,
Come seize the day, for we shall speak in the melody, God meant for you & me.
Look into my eyes; you shall reach the end of all your journeys,
Place your hand over my beating heart, & find it surpass yours in all degrees,
Like the butterfly, in a God endowed span, enjoys itself thoroughly,
Seeking nothing from flower to flower, save the sweetest of honey,
Live the joy & exuberance as God meant it, rest all must be memory,
Like the sweetness cast by the meekest flower, on a winter day, on a bended knee.
*             *             *
Let the cuckoos sing their sweetest,
Where lovers with a heavy heart rest,
Let the winds blow their trumpets
Where a lone candle burns in earnest.
Let the stars burn their brightest,
Let the darkest hour put them through the harshest test,
Let the coy flowers wistful in sobs of dew throw a riot,
In half shut eye, in half a dream reach their height.
Let the sunbeams open vaults of lit treasures,
And from each casement poet’s thought & sigh come together,
Let the moon in amorous pursuits,
In dew locks of the night, break into cold sweat.
With too great a capacity for joy,
When the world has little occasion for it.
Tarry not- for here I stand in abated breath,
Patient as the ants in your spell, I lie sedate,
When each moment pricks, like a thorn-embedded & plucked,
Before, in brooding fears & doubts, I drown,
Release me from this anguish, gently, to be reborn.
*                   *                   *
When the river persists the hills bow,
When the fruits heave the branches bestow,
Come monsoons the wind must with all his might blow,
Out on errands, the waning moon must return in her full halo.
Come the season, every tree pledges to burst into her splendor,
All entrusted with a purpose, a task to accomplish,
A soul to save, a heart to give away, a time to grant a wish,
For what do you wait- when God’s work lies incomplete at your door?
My time stands encased in a dew dropp in mid-air,
Holding my share of turmoil’s in sighs & cares,
While I knit verses in the trails of the birds & the bees,
Impart some sustaining truths that good things
come to those who wait on destiny, in a fighting frenzy.
Let's lend our heart's and spirits to light a hearth
And thereon, find new ways to measure our heart's girth.
6th Nov-2010

All ye good people, afar and near,
To my request pray lend an ear;
I advise you all without delay to go
And see the Fair Maid's House - it is a rare show.
Some of the chairs there are very grand,
They have been cut and carved by a skilful hand;
And kings, perchance, if fhe truth were told,
Have sat on them in days of old.
King James the First of Scotland was murdered there,
And his cries for mercy rent the air.
But the Highland robbers only laughed at him,
And murdered him in the dungeon and thought if no sin.
Then there's an ancient shrine upstairs,
Where the Monks and Saints said their prayers,
To the Holy Virgin, be it told;
And the house, it is said, is six hundred years old.
The old cruisie lamps are there to be seen,
Which let the monks see to write from their sheen,
Arld if the walls could speak, they could tell a fearful tale,
Which would make the people's cheeks turn pale.
Then there's an old claymore dug up from Culloden Moor,
Which in its time shed innocent blood, I am sure,
If not at Culloden Moor, some other place,
Which no doubt the truth of it history might trace.
The interior of the house is magnificent to be seen,
And the wood panelling, I'm sure, would please the Queen;
And the old fire-place, with its big fire,
Is all that visitors could desire.
Then there's a ring in a big stone near by the door,
Where gentlemen tethered their horses in days of yore;
And on the staircase door there's a firling pin
For making a rattling noise when anyone wanted in.
The mistress of the house is very kind,
A more affable woman would be herd to find;
And to visitors she is very good,
And well versed in history, be it understood.

There are many examples in biological domains where there is insufficient information to estimate the uncertainty associated with a single observation, such as the mean or standard deviation of an observational dataset. This makes it hard for these datasets to be used on their own, and most researchers would rather obtain statistics of the entire dataset than simply the average values. There has been, however, some recent work which addresses this problem by using knowledge of the variance associated with different observations [1]. We present a framework for training hierarchical models to approximate certain aspects or facets of the true structure of a dataset. By defining the extent over which the model will estimate individual variability, the strength of its approximations and how much additional data must be provided before a given approximation can yield new information about the real structure of the raw data, we have gained experimental success at estimating the uncertainties associated with arbitrary features. Our analysis also demonstrates that the algorithm can improve upon known robustness bounds while substantially reducing training time and thus increasing accuracy.


[1] S. Wang, P. E. Cukierman, D. Dutta, J. M. Chan, S.-P. Chung, G. R. Veenstra and A. I. Hinton, Sparse Learning through Partition Tables, Neural Computation Letters (2015) 6(1): 933–939

Consider a bridgeless cubic graph $G$ and a collection of $k$ 1-factors within $G$. Define $E_i$ to be the set of edges appearing in exactly $i$ of these 1-factors. Let $\mu_k(G)$ represent the minimum size of $E_0$ across all possible selections of $k$ 1-factors. If $G$ cannot be 3-edge-colored, then $\mu_3(G) \geq 3$. As demonstrated by [E. Steffen, 2015], when $\mu_3(G) > 0$, twice its value provides an upper limit on $G$'s girth. We demonstrate that $\mu_3(G)$ also restricts the oddness $\omega(G)$ of $G$, proving that $\omega(G) \leq \frac{2}{3}\mu_3(G)$. When $\mu_3(G) = \frac{2}{3}\mu_3(G)$, specific core structures emerge, termed Petersen cores. For any specified oddness, we can construct a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph $G$ where $\omega(G) = \frac{2}{3}\mu_3(G)$. However, this difference between $\omega(G)$ and $\frac{2}{3}\mu_3(G)$ can vary greatly, even with fixed oddness. Moreover, for any $k \geq 3$, a bridless cubic graph $G$ exists such that $\mu_3(G) = k$.

1 large whole chicken (About 5 1/2 pounds)
8 medium cloves garlic, crushed
3 medium onions, halved
2 lemons, halved
1 1/2 pounds assorted fingerling potatoes
1/4 cup assorted chopped herbs (rosemary, thyme, parsley, or sage)
Olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Preheat oven to 425°. Rinse chicken well and pat dry, remove bag of giblets and discard or save for another use. Trim excess fat from opening of chicken cavity if necessary. Arrange halved onions in center of 9X13 inch pyrex dish to act as a base for chicken to sit on. Place chicken on top of onions. Squeeze halved lemon onto chicken body and legs, then place lemons in chicken cavity, repeat with all halved lemons. Place crushed garlic in cavity as well then tie chicken legs together with kitchen twine. Season chicken liberally with salt and cracked black pepper. Wash fingerling potatoes and slice largest fingerlings in half lengthwise. Toss potatoes with olive oil, half the chopped herbs and season with salt and pepper. Place in roasting baking dish around chicken. Roast until temperature taken in the thickest part of breast registers 150°F and thighs registers at least 165°F, about an hour. Remove from oven and allow chicken to rest for 15 minutes. Remove potatoes and toss with remaining chopped herbs. Carve chicken and serve immediately.

Controversial new EU rules for the patenting of computer-based inventions have been put on hold due to a last minute intervention from Poland.
Poland - a large and therefore crucial EU member - has requested more time to consider the issue, especially as it relates to the patenting of software. Critics say the law would favour large companies over small, innovative ones. They say it could have massive ramifications for developments such as open source software.
Polish ministers want to see the phrasing of the text of the Directive on the Patentability of Computer-Implemented Inventions changed so that it excludes the patenting of software. The planned law has ignited angry debate about whether the EU should allow the patenting of computer programs and internet business methods as currently happens in the US. So, for instance, US-based Amazon.com holds a patent on 'one-click shopping'. Critics claim the law, which the EU says is needed to harmonise with the US, is little more than a law on ideas. "Patent rights, it is claimed, protect inventors but in this case it is exclusively the interests of the big companies that are protected," Eva Lichtenberg, a Austrian Green member of the European Parliament said in a statement. "Smaller, innovative firms cannot afford the patenting and legal costs that the directive would inflict on them," she added. The European Parliament has already clashed with the European Union on the issue and there have been accusations that the process to decide the issue has been undemocratic. The directive has been subject to several previous delays.

Tarzan and the Ant Men is a thrilling adventure novel written by Edgar Rice Burroughs. It follows the story of Tarzan, the lord of the jungle, as he embarks on a treacherous journey through a mysterious land inhabited by savage, ant-sized humanoids. 

The novel begins with Tarzan's day-to-day life in the African jungle, where he spends his time swinging through the trees, hunting for food, and protecting his animal friends. However, his peaceful existence is shattered when he comes across a race of minuscule warriors known as the Ant Men. 

Intrigued by these tiny beings with their intricate society, Tarzan decides to investigate further and discovers that they are at war with a neighboring tribe, the Waziri. Determined to assist the Ant Men, Tarzan offers his assistance and the strength of his superior physique. 

As the story progresses, Tarzan finds himself immersed in the complex politics and battles between the Ant Men and the Waziri, showcasing his leadership and strategic skills. Along the way, he learns more about their customs, traditions, and their reverence for the giant ants that inhabit their underground realm. 

With his unwavering loyalty, Tarzan forms valuable alliances and becomes a pivotal figure in the war between the Ant Men and the Waziri. As he fights alongside them, Tarzan begins to question his own identity and where he truly belongs. Is he more human or animal? Can he bridge the gap between his jungle upbringing and the civilized world?

Throughout the novel, Tarzan faces numerous challenges, from hostile wildlife to fierce warriors, and even the treacherous terrain of the underground ant kingdom. With his strength, intelligence, and resourcefulness, Tarzan must overcome these obstacles to help the Ant Men protect their land and defeat their enemy.

Tarzan and the Ant Men is a thrilling and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the balance between civilization and the wild. Burroughs' vivid storytelling and his ability to transport readers into the heart of the jungle make this novel a captivating read for both fans of the Tarzan series and new readers alike.

We propose an improved workflow for unsupervised multiphase image segmentation. Our method consists of four steps: (1) construction of an initial multiphase segmentation, (2) identification of oversegmentation artifacts, (3) correction of oversegmentation artifacts, and (4) refinement of the segmentation. We evaluate our method on two publicly available datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

When performing high-dimensional regression with many predictors relative to the data amount, identifying key variables impacting the target outcome becomes crucial. Variable selection and managing multiple testing are common approaches to this challenge; however, their relationship isn't thoroughly explored. If the signal is sufficiently powerful, selection consistency can be achieved, making false discovery rate control redundant. This work examines situations where signals are simultaneously infrequent and faint, preventing selection consistency and introduces a technique controlling the false discovery rate as it approaches infinity. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the false non-discovery rate of this method converges to zero at its best possible speed, supported by numerical examples showcasing its superior performance.

In a landmark ruling, renowned athlete, James Collins, has been handed a ban from all professional sports activities. The decision comes after a lengthy investigation into allegations of doping, marking a significant turning point in the fight against performance-enhancing drugs in sports.

Collins, a decorated sprinter with multiple national and international titles to his name, was found guilty of using prohibited substances to enhance his performance. The ban, effective immediately, will last for four years, effectively ruling him out of the next Olympic Games.

The case against Collins was brought by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), following irregularities in his drug test results. The agency's investigation revealed the use of anabolic steroids, a substance banned in professional sports due to its performance-enhancing effects.

The ruling was delivered by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), the highest court for sports-related disputes. In their statement, the CAS panel said, "The athlete has been found guilty of violating anti-doping rules. The panel believes that a four-year ban is appropriate considering the severity of the violation."

The decision has sent shockwaves through the sporting world, with many expressing their disappointment and shock at the news. Collins, who has always maintained his innocence, expressed his devastation at the ruling. "I am deeply saddened and shocked by this decision. I have always competed clean, and I will continue to fight to clear my name," he said in a statement.

The ban on Collins is seen as a landmark case in the fight against doping in sports. It sends a strong message to athletes worldwide about the severe consequences of using performance-enhancing drugs. The World Athletics President, Sebastian Coe, said, "This ruling is a significant step in our fight against doping. It shows that no athlete, no matter how successful, is above the rules."

The case has also sparked a debate about the effectiveness of current anti-doping measures and the need for more stringent controls. As the sporting world grapples with the fallout from this decision, it is clear that the fight against doping is far from over.

Rediffusion Singapore was a cable television provider in Singapore. It was previously a subsidiary of Rediffusion Industries, which originated from Radio Rediffusion, the first radio broadcaster in Singapore.

Radio Rediffusion began broadcasting in June 1949 and continued for 35 years until September 1984. At its peak, it reached 900,000 listeners, unparalleled by any other local radio station. However, with the emergence of television, Radio Rediffusion began to decline in popularity. On September 1, 1984, the radio station broadcast its last signal, thus ending its era.

In November 1989, Rediffusion acquired a 20-year franchise to operate a cable television service in Singapore. Installation works began in March 1990, and the service was launched on June 11, 1990, costing subscribers S$15.20 per month. In 1997, it increased its coverage area from 85 to 98 percent of Singapore, with an additional 84,000 homes able to receive the service. In March 1998, Rediffusion accelerated its expansion program to reach all households by end 1999.

On May 1, 2001, Singapore's then Minister for Information and the Arts Lee Yock Suan announced that the franchise for the cable television service would not be renewed, and that it would expire on August 31, 2001. The service would be replaced by StarHub CableTV, which began on December 29, 2001. In 2002, Rediffusion's cable television business was sold to Singapore Cable Vision (SCV), a subsidiary of StarHub.

On April 1, 2003, SCV merged with Singapore Digital Media Pte Ltd (SDM), a subsidiary of StarHub, and became StarHub Cable TV.

For Rare Lamb: Have the lamb at room temperature. Heat the oven to 400 degrees. Using a paring knife poke 6 small holes in the fat side of the roast and insert the garlic cloves. Rub the roast all over with salt and pepper and a little bit of oil. Insert a meat thermometer in the thickest part of the leg, being careful not to touch the bone. Place in a pan with a roasting rack and roast at 400 degrees for 40 min, so which the meat can brown. Turn down the oven to 325 degrees and roast for an additional 40 to 50 min or possibly till the meat thermometer registers 140 degrees. For Medium Lamb: Follow the above instructions but cook a bit longer so the thermometer registers 145 to 150 degrees. Remove the meat from the oven and allow it to sit 1/2 hour before slicing. After thirty years away, writer Fernando returns to Medellín, now described as Colombia’s “capital of hate.” He encounters Alexis, a sixteen-year-old male prostitute and hitman – a product of Medellín’s violent youth – and develops a passionate, yet ultimately tragic, love affair with him. Their relationship is shadowed by violence; Alexis readily kills anyone who offends him, functioning almost as an Angel of Death. As they move through the city, marked by murder and church visits, Alexis imparts knowledge about the underworld of Medellín’s gun culture, while Fernando shares memories of his own lost childhood in a vastly different city. Following Alexis’s death at the hands of two motorbike riders, Fernando hunts down his killers and discovers Wilmar, a boy strikingly similar to Alexis in appearance and demeanor. Learning that Wilmar is dating the man responsible for Alexis’s death—having previously killed Wilmar’s brother—Fernando urges him to flee the country, which he does. However, upon returning to say goodbye to his mother, Wilmar is murdered. Fernando is left isolated within a city where genuine connection appears unattainable.

Having contributed to Great Britain’s bronze medal performance at the World Cross Country Championships, she pulled ahead of Ines Monteiro around the midpoint of the 6.6km event before comfortably overtaking her Portuguese competitor in 20 minutes and 38 seconds.
