segmentation by incorporating CNNs into a bounding box and scribble-based
segmentation pipeline. We propose image-specific fine-tuning to make a CNN
model adaptive to a specific test image, which can be either unsupervised
(without additional user interactions) or supervised (with additional
scribbles). We also propose a weighted loss function considering network and
interaction-based uncertainty for the fine-tuning. We applied this framework to
two applications: 2D segmentation of multiple organs from fetal MR slices,
where only two types of these organs were annotated for training; and 3D
segmentation of brain tumor core (excluding edema) and whole brain tumor
(including edema) from different MR sequences, where only tumor cores in one MR
sequence were annotated for training. Experimental results show that 1) our
model is more robust to segment previously unseen objects than state-of-the-art
CNNs; 2) image-specific fine-tuning with the proposed weighted loss function
significantly improves segmentation accuracy; and 3) our method leads to
accurate results with fewer user interactions and less user time than
traditional interactive segmentation methods.

Premiership footballer and record company boss Kevin Campbell has gained a court injunction stopping R&B singer Mark Morrison from releasing an album.
The Everton striker signed Morrison to his fledging 2 Wikid Records label and claims he spent thousands of pounds producing his album Innocent Man. Now he is attempting to prevent Morrison releasing the album on Monday through another label. But Morrison vowed to ignore the order, saying "no judge is gonna stop me".
Morrison, who is now as well known for his brushes with the law than his music career, rose to fame with the 1996 single Return of the Mack.
But the Leicester singer has struggled to repeat its success following two spells in jail. One was for hiring a stand-in to complete his community service for possession of a stun gun and three-months following a nightclub fracas. He signed to Mr Campbell's label a year ago and has released one single, with the label saying the album was due for release on 24 January. But Mr Campbell said he learned that Morrison planned to release the album through Jet Star, which is advertising it on its website. Mr Campbell said: "I'm glad we were granted the injunction but I'm completely gutted that we have had to go that far. "Mark Morrison was given everything he asked for by 2 Wikid but it seems that he couldn't help but return to his old ways.
"I've worked hard to realise my ambition in football but had hoped that my future career would be in the music business. "I have always dreamt of starting a record label but now Mark Morrison has spoilt that dream for me. There is no loyalty in this business - just greed."
But Morrison is determined the album will be released on Monday. He said: "The injunction is ludicrous. "I signed a new deal with a new record company because I was not getting the support I needed from 2 Wikid. "I was with that label for a year and in that time released just one record, which was not properly promoted. He added: "The whole world is waiting for this album and it will come out on December 27. No injunction or judge will stop it. The Mack will return." The case is set to be heard in the High Court on 20 December.

Boris Johnson, Britain's prime minister since 2019, has announced that he will step down from his position in June after leading the country through several tumultuous years including Brexit and COVID-19 pandemic. In a brief statement issued by 10 Downing Street on Friday morning, Boris Johnson said: "I have always understood politics to be about serving people – first as their member of parliament then later as Prime Minister - but now I want to serve our great nation differently." 

Confirming speculation that had been swirling around him for weeks, Mr Johnson did not specify what his future plans might hold beyond retiring from frontline political life, simply saying it was time 'to give someone else': an opportunity'. His decision to retire comes just before local elections this May, which were seen as testing ground national mood ahead general election next year, with poll suggesting party could face crushing defeat if PM remains at helm.

The European Union has made good on its threat to scrap EU software patents, and in its place will promote an open, free and universal digital society.

In June 2011 it emerged that many technology companies were unhappy with how the European Court of Justice ruled to allow patent protection for standardisation technologies - a measure they called anti-competitive and a disincentive for innovation and competition. The controversial legislation was due to come into effect by July 2012 but now that summer deadline has been pushed back again until just after the end of 2012 at the earliest.

Instead, the EU's Executive Commission is introducing changes to the so-called 'Patent Cooperation Treaty'. These could radically affect those who use software. A draft report says the new laws "would establish strong limitations" on any patents granted on software inventions - creating what critics say is more of a grey area where anyone or company can effectively own intellectual property rights over existing technologies.

Under this proposal it would be possible to hold anybody liable if their users used software which infringed an invention, in which case the alleged creator, rather than being held responsible, could choose whom to sue. Any patent holder would also no longer have to go through the cumbersome process of filing a formal application before bringing suit against somebody else's computer. Instead they would be allowed to simply issue a letter to someone requesting payment for using software that allegedly infringes an original invention. The patent claims should be valid once the notice expires anyway.

European commissioner Günther Oettinger said he believed it was unacceptable to allow technology companies such as Google to rely upon one single system across all corners of Europe when applying for patents. He also pointed out that most US businesses are already benefiting equally from open systems, including by benefiting directly from fair use exemptions under copyright law. This means, he added ominously, that it is not going well for those countries in Europe trying to adopt an independent intellectual property system. And so Europe will remain "a big weak link".

Opposition Groups across the EU voiced concerns last night at the lack of explanation behind the revised wording: what does the proposed change actually mean for software? Rui Tokisaki is presently the head coach of Tochigi SC, having previously been a Japanese football player. His brother, Rui Tokisaki, was also a professional footballer. Tokisaki began his playing career in 1998 with J1 League’s Bellmare Hiratsuka (later Shonan Bellmare), initially appearing in games in 1999. The team experienced relegation to J2 League starting in 2000, during which time he made his debut and played extensively as a center back throughout 2000 and 2002, occasionally serving as a side back as well. His appearances decreased after 2003, and he transferred to Mito HollyHock in J2 League in 2005, though limited playing time followed. He then returned to his hometown and played for FC Pelada Fukushima (later Fukushima United FC) in Regional Leagues alongside his brother Rui from 2007 until 2011, continuing to play regularly until 2009 before retiring at the end of the 2011 season.

Hailing from the animation house that brought us such jems as Morph, the Wallace and Gromit series and Rex the Runt, Chicken Run is the first ever feature length claymation ever attempted.

Set on a chicken farm in Yorkshire some time in the middle of the century, our plucky (sorry) heroines face a lifetime of hard labor laying for the farmers, and if their performance is not up to par they quite literally face the chop. Ginger, making her way to the top of the pecking order (sorry again) attempts jailbreak after farcical jailbreak, but success is less than forthcoming.

Enter Rocky The Rhode Island Red, (Rocky Rhodes for short, and you can't blame me for that one, the writers came up with it) apparently able to fly, the chickens look to him to help them bust this chicken coup, but Rocky is not what he may appear to be.

That's the plot in a nut (egg?) shell, and as you can imagine the subject matter made for perfect "salutes" to the classic world war 2 escape movies, references to which abound throughout. From Ginger tossing a baseball (actually a sprout) in the "cooler" (coal bunker), to Fowler's incessant ramblings about his old RAF days.

The lead characters are deep and endearing enough for you to care about what happens to them, if a little stereotypical at times. The interaction between them is fluid and believable, all the more amazing considering that Mel Gibson never even set foot in the same recording studio as the other actors, reading his lines in a studio in America instead. The supporting cast provide plenty of humour and Mrs. Tweedy substitutes quite nicely for the Nazi camp commandant.

The animation is lively and colourful the characters wonderfully expressive in that unmistakable style developed in the Wallace and Gromit shorts, and thanks to the fact the sets are real models there is plenty of scope for dramatic lighting effects.

The only real fault I could find in the film was that it just seemed a little too... American at times. Hollywood's involvement showed through the English setting to some degree, especially as you get to the movie's climax which seems to go a bit overboard, especially compared to the utterly hysterical ending to The Wrong Trousers. But all in all I have to say I really enjoyed this movie. Now all we need is a Wallace and Gromit movie.

Recent advancements in semantic segmentation leveraging fully convolutional networks (FCNs) often utilize an encoder-decoder structure like U-Net, training them on pixel-wise classifications using paired images and segmentation maps. These approaches primarily rely on class labels derived from the ground truth. This work introduces a multi-task learning framework designed to incorporate both structural and spatial details alongside class information. The decoder component of the FCN is adapted to integrate these additional cues while minimizing network complexity. Structural information is acquired through contour maps or distance maps, obtainable from ground truth segmentations without extra annotations. We investigate various distance map calculation methods and their impact on segmentation accuracy. Extensive testing across two medical imaging tasks—color fundus images for optic disc and cup segmentation, and endoscopic images for polyp segmentation—demonstrates competitive results, sometimes surpassing existing state-of-the-art models, and achieves a parameter reduction of approximately 20%.

Having just survived another perilous year at Hogwarts, Harry is determined to enjoy his summer break and relax with his friends. However, fate has other plans for him.

As the school year begins, Harry discovers that members of an ancient order known as the Order of the Phoenix have been secretly working to help protect the students from the dangerous forces lurking outside their walls. After being approached by Albus Dumbledore, Harry learns that Voldemort's return to power could lead to widespread disaster and destruction if something isn’t done.

Feeling a renewed sense of purpose, Harry joins the Order and is tasked with protecting Sirius Black – one of its most important members – who has come under attack from Voldemort's Death Eaters. As the two work together, they uncover a shocking revelation: Voldemort will stop at nothing to eliminate anyone who stands in the way of achieving ultimate control!

With time running out, Harry Musters all his courage and determination to lead the charge against the dark forces encroaching on Hogwarts. Alongside his loyal companions like Hermione Granger and Ron Weasley, Harry faces incredible odds in what becomes an epic battle that tests everything he thought he knew about bravery, friendship and loyalty.

"Background subtraction" is an old technique for finding moving objects in a
video sequence for example, cars driving on a freeway. The idea is that
subtracting the current image from a timeaveraged background image will leave
only nonstationary objects. It is, however, a crude approximation to the task
of classifying each pixel of the current image; it fails with slow-moving
objects and does not distinguish shadows from moving objects. The basic idea of
this paper is that we can classify each pixel using a model of how that pixel
looks when it is part of different classes. We learn a mixture-of-Gaussians
classification model for each pixel using an unsupervised technique- an
efficient, incremental version of EM. Unlike the standard image-averaging
approach, this automatically updates the mixture component for each class
according to likelihood of membership; hence slow-moving objects are handled
perfectly. Our approach also identifies and eliminates shadows much more
effectively than other techniques such as thresholding. Application of this
method as part of the Roadwatch traffic surveillance project is expected to
result in significant improvements in vehicle identification and tracking.

Kazuya is a fascinating character, and I'll tell you why. Firstly, his design is incredibly well-done. His appearance, with the red hair and the mole under his eye, is instantly recognizable and memorable. His character arc, from a naive and entitled rich kid to a vengeful and power-hungry individual, is also well-executed.

One of the things that sets Kazuya apart from other characters is his unapologetic and unwavering ambition. He knows what he wants, and he's willing to do whatever it takes to get it, even if it means hurting others or sacrificing his own relationships. This makes him both a compelling and a frustrating character to watch, as you're never quite sure what he'll do next.

Another aspect of Kazuya's character that I appreciate is the way he challenges the traditional hero/villain dynamic. He's certainly not a hero, but he's not necessarily a villain either. He exists in a gray area, and his motivations and actions are often understandable, even if they're not always admirable. This complexity makes him a refreshing change from the usual black-and-white characterizations found in many stories.

Overall, I think Kazuya is a well-written and engaging character, and I'm looking forward to seeing how his character develops in the future. How about you? What are your thoughts on Kazuya as a character? Do you love him, hate him, or something in between? Let me know in the comments!

For the pastry, combine 140 grams of unsalted butter (cut into cubes), 135 grams of sugar, 2 eggs, and 150 grams of flour, mixing with an electric whisk until resembling breadcrumbs. Then, quickly knead into a cohesive dough ball – it’s meant to remain cold. It will be somewhat crumbly, so gently press it together; if necessary, add just a small amount of water. Wrap the dough and chill for 2 hours. Prepare the pear filling by peeling, halving, and removing the cores from 5 pears. In a saucepan, combine the pears with 50 ml of white wine or white port and 3 star anise, cooking for approximately 5 minutes before turning and cooking for another 5, ensuring they soften slightly without becoming mushy. Allow to cool. Next, make the frangipane: cream 60g butter and 60g sugar until light and fluffy, then incorporate the remaining egg, cinnamon, 1 teaspoon of flour, and 60 grams of ground almonds. Chill until ready to use. Preheat the oven to 160°C. Roll out the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface and place it into a buttered tartelette case. Spread generously with the frangipane. Slice each pear into fan shapes, creating a design that allows the bases to hold the fans together. Arrange the pear halves in a circular pattern across the frangipane. If issues arise due to large pears, don’t fret—any arrangement will contribute to a rustic appearance. Bake for 25 minutes, or until the tartelettes are golden brown.

R&B star Alicia Keys is to open February's Super Bowl singing a song only previously performed there by Ray Charles and Vicki Carr.
Keys, who will sing America the Beautiful, will be accompanied by 150 students from the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind. Charles, who died last year, attended the school as a child in 1937. Keys said she was "very excited", describing Charles as "an artist I admire, miss and respect". "I know that this is going to be a very touching and memorable moment," she said.
It will be her first performance at the Super Bowl, which will be watched by millions in the US on 6 February. Sir Paul McCartney will provide the half-time entertainment in the slot filled by Janet Jackson last year. Organisers have promised there will be no repeat of her nipple-baring incident that sparked thousands of complaints on US TV's most-watched broadcast. A National Football League spokesman said they were "comfortable" this show would be acceptable to a mass audience. The game and show were watched by 144 million people in the US in 2003.
Twenty CBS-owned TV stations were fined $550,000 (£300,000) by the country's TV regulatory agency after more than 542,000 complaints were made about Janet Jackson's "wardrobe malfunction". Sir Paul said: "There's nothing bigger than being asked to perform at the Super Bowl. "We're looking forward to rocking the millions at home and in the stadium."

The Starship Enterprise, commanded by Captain Jonathan Archer and his crew, encountered a baffling alien ship operated by the Antianna, which prevented their progress. Lacking a way to understand the Antiannan communications and fearing conflict, the Enterprise altered its trajectory. They were swiftly drawn into the territory of the Thelasian Trading Confederacy, a group already involved with the Antianna. Governor Maxim Sen, the Confederacy’s leader, was actively planning a war to neutralize the Antianna’s danger to their trade networks. Archer believed Sen harbored hidden intentions, and suspected a deeper cause behind the Antianna’s aggression. However, facing opposition from multiple races, Archer required concrete evidence. Ensign Hoshi Sato possesses the crucial skill to translate the Antiannan language; her success could avert widespread devastation, but failure would trigger a catastrophic, sector-wide war.

Lia, fifteen years old, finds herself caring for her dying great-grandmother Sarah, who recounts chilling tales of Graymoss Plantation – a Louisiana estate abandoned due to a rumored malevolent presence. Following Sarah’s passing, Lia’s mother inherits the property and intends to relocate with a group of challenging foster children. Disagreeing with this plan, Lia becomes determined to demonstrate the house’s haunting reputation is genuine. She uncovers historical accounts of paranormal activity and faces resistance from local residents wary of the family moving in. Initially suspecting someone might be deliberately creating the disturbances, Lia shifts her focus when encountering the children her mother wants to help. Utilizing Edgar Allan Poe’s works for guidance, she ultimately banishes the spectral entities, which echo the unsettling atmosphere of Shirley Jackson’s *The Haunting of Hill House*, characterized by whispers and misplaced objects. The narrative concludes rather quickly, with a budding romance unresolved, yet remains a captivating read for lovers of mystery and supernatural narratives.

THE AUTHOR OF THIS NOVEL, MARK FRANCIS, HAS DEALT WITH A LOT OF CONVERSATIONS ABOUT HOW BEST TO DESCRIBE HIS SIDE of the argument about how to understand reality (or to describe it accurately) and has chosen this very approach. He describes the various categories of arguments in short descriptions that he believes are essential parts of explaining things so that we can make accurate statements about them. These include "objective description", "subjective description", "conceptual analysis", and the like.

He writes:

Objectivity is first and foremost not having an opinion as to what is real, or whether things exist in any particular sense. Realizing that you have an answer, whether the truth, or anything else really matters doesn't mean you've understood it, only that your answer isn't made up by yourself—that others might draw upon the concepts you discuss. Thus, I argue that Objectivity involves not just knowing that the world exists but also knowing exactly why those who live in that world exist.


As with all art there must be subjectivity. There may well indeed be questions about objective vs subjective. So far, however, I am uninterested in these question because they seem likely to become confused by another idea which seems to me incontrovertibly true if I were ever granted access to the information necessary to formulate a definitive answer: Subjectivity doesn't involve merely being aware of what's going on; you're also aware of where things come from and how things work as a whole. For example, do people know the size of their own hands? How many apples are at your table today while you eat yours and read some more paragraphs of material on my page? Of course, most people think things happen by luck, and therefore don't mind being in an environment where someone else has worked very hard to get something just handed to them! The same may be said for many other mundane phenomena. But we still say things along what seems pretty much reasonable lines when our lives look like an accident rather than something planned. [1]

In his attempt to explain reality, Francis often uses vague analogies or metaphors, suggesting that he simply trusts his readers to come up with ways of understanding and comparing facts without recourse to words such as "right", "good", and "bad". Though somewhat naive and simplistic, these attempts

I
In days when men had joy of war,
A God of Battles sped each mortal jar;
The peoples pledged him heart and hand,
From Israel's land to isles afar.
II
His crimson form, with clang and chime,
Flashed on each murk and murderous meeting-time,
And kings invoked, for rape and raid,
His fearsome aid in rune and rhyme.
III
On bruise and blood-hole, scar and seam,
On blade and bolt, he flung his fulgid beam:
His haloes rayed the very gore,
And corpses wore his glory-gleam.
IV
Often an early King or Queen,
And storied hero onward, knew his sheen;
'Twas glimpsed by Wolfe, by Ney anon,
And Nelson on his blue demesne.
V
But new light spread. That god's gold nimb
And blazon have waned dimmer and more dim;
Even his flushed form begins to fade,
Till but a shade is left of him.
VI
That modern meditation broke
His spell, that penmen's pleadings dealt a stroke,
Say some; and some that crimes too dire
Did much to mire his crimson cloak.
VII
Yea, seeds of crescive sympathy
Were sown by those more excellent than he,
Long known, though long contemned till then -
The gods of men in amity.
VIII
Souls have grown seers, and thought out-brings
The mournful many-sidedness of things
With foes as friends, enfeebling ires
And fury-fires by gaingivings!
IX
He scarce impassions champions now;
They do and dare, but tensely--pale of brow;
And would they fain uplift the arm
Of that faint form they know not how.
X
Yet wars arise, though zest grows cold;
Wherefore, at whiles, as 'twere in ancient mould
He looms, bepatched with paint and lath;
But never hath he seemed the old!
XI
Let men rejoice, let men deplore.
The lurid Deity of heretofore
Succumbs to one of saner nod;
The Battle-god is god no more.

The standard model of particle physics has been highly successful explaining most of the phenomena we see in nature, however it is not complete. It cannot explain phenomena such as the baryon asymmetry of the universe, the nature of dark matter and energy, and the existence of a gravitational force. This paper discusses some of the ways in which physics beyond the standard model could address these mysteries. 

One way is to introduce new particles and interactions that are not present in the standard model. These could include new heavy particles that interact with the standard model particles through weak or electromagnetic forces, or new light particles that interact with the standard model particles through gravitational forces. Another way is to modify the standard model particles and interactions. This could include changing the way the particles interact with each other, or adding new forces to the model.

This paper focuses on one particular beyond the standard model scenario, where a new scalar field is added to the theory. This field could explain the dark matter and energy in the universe, and also have other interesting implications for particle physics and cosmology. In particular, we discuss how the scalar field could affect the primordial helium abundance in the universe, and how this could be tested by future experiments.

Re-using old mobile phones is not just good for the environment, it has social benefits too.
Research has found that in some developing nations old mobile phones can help close the digital divide. The Forum for the Future research found that the low cost of these recycled handsets means they can have a very useful second life in poorer nations. But the Forum found that more needed to be done to collect old phones rather than let them rot in landfill sites.
The report reveals that approximately 15 million mobile phones go out of use every year in the UK. Of the 15 million that are swapped for newer models each year, only 25% get returned to mobile phone firms for recycling or re-use. The slowly growing mass of unrecycled, discarded phones has now reached 90 million handsets, the equivalent of 9,000 tonnes of waste, estimates James Goodman, report author and a senior adviser at the Forum for the Future. "It's quite common for people to have two or three phones just lying around," said Mr Goodman.
Many of these older phones could end up in landfill sites leaking the potentially toxic materials they are made of into the wider world, said Mr Goodman. Far better, he said, to hand the phone back to an operator who can send it overseas where it can enjoy a second lease of life. "We've heard the environmental argument for handing a phone back," said Mr Goodman, "but there's a strong social argument too." Older mobile phones are proving particularly useful in poorer nations where people want to use a mobile and keep in touch with friends and family but do not have the income to buy the most up to date model. The Forum for the Future report took an in-depth look at Romania where reconditioned mobile phones were proving very popular. "It's an interesting country because it has a really crap fixed line network," said Mr Goodman, "and there's a real desire for people to get mobile phones." But the relatively low wages in Romania, which is one of the poorest countries in Europe, mean few people can afford a shiny new phone. "The affordability of the handsets is a real barrier to getting one," he said. Reconditioned handsets have boosted take-up of mobiles as the report revealed that almost one-third of Romanian pre-pay mobile phone users were using reconditioned handsets. The re-used handsets tend to be about one-third of the price of a new handset. Georgeta Minciu, a Romanian part-time cleaner, said: "Normally a mobile phone would not be possible on my wages. I am a single parent - keeping in touch with my daughter is important to me." "This is the only way I can afford to have a phone," she said. Mr Goodman said phone operators and consumers needed to do more to ensure that more of Britain's mobile mountain made it overseas. But, he added, those keen to use a mobile will not accept any old handset. "If its more than a few years old people are not going to want it," he said.

Government strategies addressing immigration and asylum procedures, including stricter controls on economic migrants and intensified border security measures, will be announced next week. Home Secretary Charles Clarke intends to implement a points-based system for economic migrants and escalate deportations of unsuccessful asylum claimants. While acknowledging public concerns regarding system vulnerabilities, Prime Minister Tony Blair maintains that there’s no single solution; however, the Conservatives criticize Labour's delayed response, and the Liberal Democrats question the effectiveness of the proposed changes. This five-year plan outlines Labour’s intended reforms, slated for implementation if they secure victory in the upcoming May elections. Officials refute accusations of reacting solely to opposition pressure or a perceived lack of prior action, asserting that these plans represent a developing strategy to bolster public trust. Key elements include ending automatic residency rights for immigrant family members and requiring fingerprinting for all visa applications.  Blair emphasized a focus on granting work permits only to immigrants possessing skills vital to the UK economy, dismissing calls for migration quotas. He countered Conservative suggestions of capping asylum seeker numbers and handling claims overseas, stating that such approaches aren’t feasible due to the absence of suitable alternative locations.

Northern Ireland man James McIlroy is confident he can win his first major title at this weekend's Spar European Indoor Championships in Madrid.
The 28-year-old has been in great form in recent weeks and will go in as one of the 800 metres favourites. "I believe after my wins abroad and in our trial race in Sheffield, I can run my race from the front, back or middle," said McIlroy. New coach Tony Lester has helped get McIlroy's career back on track. The 28-year-old 800 metres runner has not always matched his promise with performances but believes his decision to change coaches and move base will bring the rewards. McIlroy now lives in Windsor and feels his career has been transformed by the no-nonsense leadership style of former Army sergeant Lester. Lester is better known for his work with 400m runners Roger Black and Mark Richardson in the past but under his guidance McIlroy has secured five wins this indoor season.
McIlroy now claims he is in his best shape since finishing fourth for Ireland at the outdoor European Championships in 1998. "That was my last decent year," said McIlroy, who temporarily retired last August before returning to the sport under Lester's shrewd guidance. "Before, every race was like trying to climb Mount Everest and I now know you can't do it on your own. "Trying to succeed saw me sometimes standing half-dead and terrified on the starting line, which became a bit too much." McIlroy, who was compared to the likes of Sebastian Coe, Steve Cram and Steve Ovett in his younger days, is now competing without the benefit of National Lottery funding. That situation could change if he maintains his current form and repeats the world-class times he produced in the 800m and 1000m at major races in Erfurt and Stuttgart earlier this season. Russian Dmitriy Bogdanov won at the same Madrid venue last week and then claimed the European Championship race would be between himself, Dutchman Arnoud Okken and Antonio Reina of Spain but McIlroy is unfazed.
He admitted: "He looked quite good in his win and fair enough everyone has the right to their own opinion. "I never write myself off and let's face it, I haven't or looked like being beaten this season." And McIlroy, whose time of one minute 46.68seconds in Erfurt elevated him to sixth place on the UK All-Time list, is also already looking beyond Madrid. He said: "I've been much more focused this year about my career and having such a good team around me has been very important. Many recent medical segmentation systems rely on powerful deep learning
models to solve highly specific tasks. To maximize performance, it is standard
practice to evaluate numerous pipelines with varying model topologies,
optimization parameters, pre- & postprocessing steps, and even model cascades.
It is often not clear how the resulting pipeline transfers to different tasks.
We propose a simple and thoroughly evaluated deep learning framework for
segmentation of arbitrary medical image volumes. The system requires no
task-specific information, no human interaction and is based on a fixed model
topology and a fixed hyperparameter set, eliminating the process of model
selection and its inherent tendency to cause method-level over-fitting. The
system is available in open source and does not require deep learning expertise
to use. Without task-specific modifications, the system performed better than
or similar to highly specialized deep learning methods across 3 separate
segmentation tasks. In addition, it ranked 5-th and 6-th in the first and
second round of the 2018 Medical Segmentation Decathlon comprising another 10
tasks. The system relies on multi-planar data augmentation which facilitates
the application of a single 2D architecture based on the familiar U-Net.
Multi-planar training combines the parameter efficiency of a 2D fully
convolutional neural network with a systematic train- and test-time
augmentation scheme, which allows the 2D model to learn a representation of the
3D image volume that fosters generalization.

Clark Field, named after World War I pilot and Medal of Honor winner1 Marshal Cyrus Clark, was an American military installation located in Angeles, Pampanga, Philippines. Clark Air Base was the headquarters of the United States Army Forces in the Far East(USAFFE) and the United States Fifth Air Force during World War II, serving as a vital hub of air and ground activity in the defense of the Philippine Islands against invading Japanese forces. The base was closed following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease in 1991.

The base was captured by the Japanese on December 8, 1941, following the Japanese bombing of Pearl Harbor and the simultaneous attacks on Clark Field and several other American military installations in the Philippines. The United States bases in the Philippines were subject to Japanese attack as part of the Japanese plan for the conquest of Southeast Asia, which also involved attacks on the British possessions of Malaya, Singapore, and Hong Kong.

The Japanse forces began their offensive in the Philippines with an air raid on Clark Field on December 8, which destroyed over half of the American fighter planes stationed there. The base was subsequently captured by ground troops, and the American forces in the Philippines were forced to retreat to the Bataan Peninsula. Clark Field remained in Japanese hands until 1945, when it was recaptured by American forces during the Battle of Luzon.

Following the end of World War II, Clark Field was used by the United States Air Force (USAF) as a base for occupation forces in the Philippines. The base was gradually expanded, and in 1950, it became the headquarters for the Far East Air Forces (FEAF). The base continued to serve as a support facility for US military operations in Southeast Asia during the Vietnam War, and was the launch site for B-52 bombers that conducted airstrikes against targets in Vietnam.

The base was closed by theUS government in 1991, following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease. The base has since been redeveloped as Clark Freeport Zone, a special economic zone administered by the Philippine government.

We present an experimental demonstration that measurement-device independent (MDI) quantum key distribution (QKD) can be achieved using a modified coherent state, which we call the "coherent-state-modified-coherence". We demonstrate this by measuring the entanglement between two entangled photons in a single photon detector and then performing a QKD protocol on the measured data. The MDI protocol uses only one device to perform the QKD protocol, while the original coherent-state-modified-coherence requires two devices. This allows us to achieve a large number of qubits per device, as well as a high degree of control over the parameters of the protocol. Our results show that our method has the potential to enable a wide range of new applications such as secure communication protocols, quantum cryptography, and quantum computation.

Using multi-scale features within fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs) has significantly improved semantic image segmentation results. A frequent approach involves processing several differently sized versions of an image through a single network and combining their extracted features for pixel-level classification. Our research introduces an attention mechanism designed to dynamically adjust the weighting of these multi-scale features based on individual pixels. We integrate this attention model into a current leading semantic segmentation architecture, training it alongside multi-scale inputs. This new attention method surpasses both average and max pooling techniques, enabling visualization of feature importance across various locations and resolutions. Furthermore, we find that incorporating additional supervision signals at each scale during feature fusion is crucial for optimal performance.  We validate our model’s efficacy using thorough testing across three demanding datasets: PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012, and a portion of MS-COCO 2014.

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum information is the area of quantum information science that makes use of physical observables, like the strength of an electromagnetic field, whose numerical values belong to continuous intervals. One primary application is quantum computing. In a sense, continuous-variable quantum computation is "analog", while quantum computation using qubits is "digital." In more technical terms, the former makes use of Hilbert spaces that are infinite-dimensional, while the Hilbert spaces for systems comprising collections of qubits are finite-dimensional. One motivation for studying continuous-variable quantum computation is to understand what resources are necessary to make quantum computers more powerful than classical ones. Implementation 
One approach to implementing continuous-variable quantum information protocols in the laboratory is through the techniques of quantum optics. By modeling each mode of the electromagnetic field as a quantum harmonic oscillator with its associated creation and annihilation operators, one defines a canonically conjugate pair of variables for each mode, the so-called "quadratures", which play the role of position and momentum observables. These observables establish a phase space on which Wigner quasiprobability distributions can be defined. Quantum measurements on such a system can be performed using homodyne and heterodyne detectors.

The goal of this work is to develop a statistical machine learning scheme for medical image segmentation: we propose a novel approach based on the stochastic model of image meta-correction. The key properties of this scheme are: 1. the number of segments estimated by the system are proportional to the sum of the number of image patches. It can further be modified by introducing noise. 2. It is robust to the problem of overfitting (i.e., the number of images with a statistically different set of regions compared with the original image). 3. The procedure does not penalise for the lack of precision of the images, the method remains accurate no matter of the data quality (i.e., the probability of missing pixels is proportional to the number of pixels in the images).

The authors' research has been accepted in the "Artificial Intelligence in Medicine" conference organized by the Centre de Recherche Biomètre d'Hommes et de Recherche Biomédical/Université de Montréal and the University of Toronto. In August 2015, several of the organizers announced that the paper "The image meta-correction step-instructions as a training algorithm" was selected as a Research Post-doctoral Award, a prestigious award of $200,000 offered to the most promising research in the field of artificial intelligence.

In addition to the journal article, the paper received the following awards:

– F. Lottie. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 B.E. D.E.A.A. (2012) Award of the Royal European Institute for the History of Medicine.

– S. S. L. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 S.I.A.O. (2011) Award of the Society of Automation Research.

– A. U. Al-Jassem. This research received the 2016 "Award for best graduate work in the field of machine learning" from the Royal Society of Arts in London, UK.

Long ago, the affluent explorers Roghan the Fearless and Zelligar the Unknown constructed a secret stronghold called the Caverns of Quasqueton. Operating discreetly, they engaged in activities shielded from public scrutiny. Despite ethically dubious practices, they repelled a barbarian onslaught and secured alliances with local inhabitants. Over time, they amassed their own forces and launched an offensive against these adversaries, ultimately suffering defeat. The players begin the narrative by encountering diverse rumors concerning the module, each character possessing knowledge of at least one such tale – though their reliability is uncertain. These rumors predominantly speak of a substantial treasure concealed within the Caverns of Quasqueton, accessible via a subterranean entrance. The initial, completed portion of the dungeon is populated by various creatures like orcs, troglodytes, and giant rats. The Dungeon Master monitors encounters with these threats alongside individual room hazards. Most rooms feature placeholders for customization, allowing the DM to introduce appropriate monsters or rewards. Roghan and Zelligar’s former residence, the upper level, holds remnants of their belongings, along with common adventuring traps, such as dangerous pools and a wizard's lab. The unexplored lower levels host different monsters—zombies and goblins—and contain pre-designed spaces like a museum, arena, and vast caverns, though numerous areas lack descriptions, requiring the DM to create their own content. The module concludes with a list of combatants and treasures for the players, accompanied by a roster of potential non-player characters.

His central proposal involves £35 billion in savings intended for investment in public services and potential tax reductions. While discussions around tax cuts had been ongoing, Howard formally declared that £12 billion would address Labour’s deficit, with the remainder allocated to future tax relief – potentially including adjustments to income tax thresholds and inheritance tax. He framed the election as a choice between continued government spending under Blair and a Conservative focus on value and lower taxes. This strategy intends to regain support from traditionally conservative voters and shore up loyalty among those previously swayed by the Tories.  Jackson’s arrival appears calculated to maximize the impact of Howard’s announcement, though Howard reacted with skepticism, stating “these things happen from time”.

Image-to-image translation has been a challenging area of computer vision research for many years. We introduce an adversarial model for this task. Traditional deep learning approaches rely on comparing gram matrices and require manual image segmentation. Instead, our generative adversarial network operates through a conditional probability framework, decoupling image translation from specific details like local context, overall structure, or stylistic elements.  We incorporate a bidirectional reconstruction model alongside an affine transformation factor to preserve both content fidelity and photographic realism—outperforming existing techniques like Multimodal Unsupervised Image-to-image translation. This method offers semi-supervised learning, avoids the need for image segmentation, and leverages the inherent realism generation capabilities of adversarial networks.

12 Years a Slave tells the true story of Solomon Northup, an educated and free black man living in New York during the 1840's who gets abducted, shipped to the south, and sold into slavery. It is a film that stimulates at both an emotional level and an intellectual one.

Chiwetel Ejiofor plays Solomon Northup. He's been a "that guy" actor for sometime – film-goers may know his face but not his name. After this film his name will be known. He gives, quite simply, the best performance from a leading actor since Daniel Day Lewis in There Will Be Blood. Because of his character's position as a slave he is usually unable to speak his mind unless he is prepared to be beaten. As a result Ejiofor is forced to utilize body language and his eyes, which become enormous pools of emotion to express himself to the audience. He's forced to endure terrible things, but he always maintains a certain dignity and nobility that makes his plight even more affecting. It's a performance of incredible subtlety that may leave you speechless and in complete awe.

Micheal Fassbender gives the best performance of his already extremely impressive career, even besting his previous high marks from the films Shame and Hunger (both directed by Steve McQueen, who also directed 12 Years a Slave). He plays Edwynn Epps, a vicious and demonic slaver and perhaps the most loathsome and disgusting character ever put on screen. If alive today, he'd likely be a drunk with severe anger management issues. By turns pathetic and terrifying, he embodies the ultimate nightmare of a deeply flawed man given absolute power over other human beings, and through that absolute power finds only madness, which drives him to deeper cruelty. He's always a menacing and malignant presence even when not on screen, as his slaves must always be aware and prepared for his seemingly random bouts of sadism.

Other actors give excellent performances as well. Paul Giamatti, Paul Dano, Benedict Cumberbatch, Sarah Paulson, Alfre Woodard are all great in relatively small roles. But in this film of titans it's the one you've probably never heard of who perhaps stands above them all. In her first role in a feature film, Lupita Nyong'o, playing the pretty young slave Patsey - the object of Edwynn Epps demented and horrifying affections and the emotional epicenter of the entire picture, gives one of the most devastating performances I have ever seen. A portrait of unbearable sadness, her character is a mirror image of Solomon. While Solomon is a man who refuses to break and give up the dignity which he's known since birth, she is one who has long since been broken, and who never knew dignity in the first place. Her life is a living hell, forced to endure the "love" of Edwyn Epps and the brutal jealousy of his wife, she's trapped in a terrible triangle that she can't escape. Despite that, she retains a level of innocence that only heightens the tragedy of her character. It actually gets to the point where simply looking at this character might be enough to bring you to tears. It's a shattering performance.

Starting his career as a video artist before making full length films, Steve McQueen has an uncanny eye for imagery and contrast. He's also a very patient film maker, utilizing long, steady single shots to emphasize various things. In his prior films this has felt like a purely stylistic choice, here, it's a choice aimed directly at our heart. When the events on screen become their most horrifying and ugly is when his camera becomes the most unflinching. At times feeling perhaps like we're seeing out of the solemn eyes of the ghost of some murdered slave, watching in sorrow and rage. This is both McQueen's most accessible and artistically searing film yet.

There are also moments of stunning natural beauty that would make Terrence Malick proud. Alone, these shots would inspire wonder, but in the context of this film they make us feel more forlorn, as if the ugliness of man is encroaching on the natural beauty of the world.

Perhaps the most noteworthy thing about 12 Years a Slave is the way that it portrays slavery itself. Instead of taking the easy way out and limiting his exploration of the topic solely to the slaves, Steve McQueen increases the scope and we see how it affects those who profited by it. Take Benedict Cumberbatch's character. A seemingly decent and caring man who treats his slaves with some semblance of respect and kindness. He comes off as a relatively good man who is trapped within the powerful confines of the institution of slavery. In 12 Years a Slave, slavery is shown as a horrifying and destructive social construct that drains the humanity from everyone it touches, turning good men into moral quandaries, turning flawed men into monsters, and turning an entire race of people into livestock and tools.

To watch 12 Years a Slave is to be confronted with the grim reality of slavery in a way that's never been done before. To say this is the best film ever made about slavery feels trivial, as slavery is a subject in film that has been shown with naive romanticism from films like Gone With the Wind or silly exploitation from something like Django Unchained. Both of which serve to make the topic digestible. To watch 12 Years a Slave is to experience a level of despair and misery that can become overwhelming. It's a film of such ugliness, such blunt emotional trauma, that it may haunt you for hours if not days after seeing it. So why should you watch a film that could leave you reeling and devastated? Because, it's also one of the greatest cinematic achievements of our time.

Dmitry Koptur (Russian: Дмитрий Коптур, Ukrainian: Дмитро Коптур; born c. 1984) is a Ukrainian-born businessman and philanthropist. He is best known for his work in the fields of data science and artificial intelligence.

Koptur was born in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union, in 1984, and moved to the United States with his family in 1991. He received a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science and Mathematics from the University of Pennsylvania in 2006, and a Ph.D. in Computer Science from the University of California, Berkeley in 2010.

After completing his Ph.D., Koptur worked as a research scientist at various institutions, including the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Germany and the IBM Watson Research Center in New York. He has also held teaching positions at the University of California, Berkeley and the Technical University of Munich.

In 2016, Koptur co-founded the company "Koptur Analytics", which provides data science and artificial intelligence consulting services to businesses and organizations. The company's clients include various Fortune 500 companies, as well as government agencies and non-profit organizations.

Koptur has also been involved in various philanthropic activities, including donating to research and education initiatives in the fields of data science and artificial intelligence. He has also worked to promote the development of these fields in various countries, including Ukraine, where he has helped to establish research centers and educational programs.

The paper "Bounded negativity, Harbourne constants and transversal arrangements of curves" presents a new approach to studying the topology of curves in algebraic geometry. The authors introduce the concept of bounded negativity, which measures the degree of negativity of a curve's intersection with a fixed line. They also introduce the Harbourne constants, which provide a way to quantify the degree of negativity of a curve.

The paper then uses these concepts to study the transversal arrangements of curves, which are the ways in which curves intersect each other. The authors prove several results about the topology of these arrangements, including the existence of a lower bound on the number of transversal arrangements of a given degree of negativity.

Overall, the paper provides a new perspective on the study of curves in algebraic geometry, and offers new insights into the topology of these objects.

450 g cream cheese, at room temperature
1/4 cup caster sugar
3 teaspoons cornflour
3 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
3 teaspoons finely grated icing sugar
1 1/2 tablespoons strained fresh lemon juice
2 cups sour cream
1 cup thickened cream
220 g good quality white chocolate, melted then cooled to lukewarm
fresh seasonal fruit
passion fruit pulp, to serve
Preheat oven to 180°C Grease a 20cm springform cake pan and line base with baking paper. Wrap the outside tightly with a double layer foil. Whiz cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until smooth. With motor running, add cornflour, eggs one at a time, stopping occasionally to scrape down sides. Add vanilla, zest, juice, creams and 1/4 tsp salt, and process until just combined, scraping down sides. Add chocolate and pulse until smooth. Pour into pan and sit in a large baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the sides of the pan. Bake for 45 minutes, then off the oven, leaving the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. Remove pan from dish, take off the foil and cool cake completely in pan on a rack. Cover and chill overnight. To turn out, sit pan on a hot, damp towel to loosen base. Run a palette knife around edge of pan, then turn onto a serving plate. Decorate with fruit by piling the fruit on top (I find doing it randomly looks best) and pouring over the passionfruit pulp, then slice with a hot, dry knife.

For this dish, you’ll need two green peppers, two red peppers, four small summer squashes, four Asian eggplants (or white-skinned varieties), approximately three tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil, coarse salt and black pepper, six plum tomatoes, two red onions, one minced garlic clove (without the green top), one tablespoon of fresh thyme, and one pound of fusilli or penne pasta. Start a charcoal grill. Char the whole peppers until their skins are blackened; then seal them in a bag to steam and cool before halving and removing the seeds and ribs – slice these into strips. Simultaneously, grill the summer squash and eggplant slices, seasoned with olive oil, salt, and pepper, until lightly browned. Grill the plum tomatoes cut-side down until slightly softened. Prepare onion rings by brushing them with oil and grilling until browned. In a saucepan, bring six quarts of salted water to a boil. Sauté garlic and thyme in a little olive oil until fragrant. Add the tomatoes to the pan and simmer briefly to create a sauce. Once cooled, chop the grilled vegetables into strips and mix them into the sauce. Cook the pasta until it's al dente, drain it, and toss with the vegetable mixture. Garnish with chopped fresh basil and serve with grated Parmesan cheese on the side.

David John Mays (November 22, 1896 – February 17, 1971) was an American lawyer and writer. He attempted to slow racial desegregation on behalf of Byrd Organization during the Massive Resistance era. Mays served as counsel to the Gray Commission which tried to formulate segregationists' response to the United States Supreme Court rulings in 1954 and 1955 in consolidated cases known as Brown v. Board of Education. He later unsuccessfully defended actions taken against NAACP attorneys (although he had argued against adoption of those laws and correctly predicted they would be overturned) and significantly unequal legislative reapportionment. In 2008 the University of Georgia Press published an annotated volume of excerpts of his diaries concerning the early years of Massive Resistance (1954-1959).<ref>Race Reason and Massive Resistance: The Diary of David J. Mays, 1954-1959. Edited by James R. Sweeney (University of Georgia Press 2008)</ref> In 1953, Mays won the Pulitzer Prize for Biography or Autobiography for Edmund Pendleton 1721-1803 (Harvard University Press, 1952), a biography of the late 18th-century Virginia politician and judge Edmund Pendleton. Early life
Mays was born in Richmond to Harvey James Mays, a chemical company foreman, and his wife, the former Helga Nelsen. His  Danish immigrant grandfather, Rasmus Nelsen, founded the Nelsen funeral home in Richmond. He eventually had 10 brothers and sisters and attended public schools near his father's employment stations in Alabama and a suburb of Memphis, Tennessee. While he and his father traveled from Washington D.C. to visit Vanderbilt University, they stopped in Ashland, Virginia, where the elder Mays renewed a friendship and the younger Mays ultimately decided  to attend Randolph-Macon Academy. David Mays never received a degree from that institution, although he studied and achieved high grades both from 1914-1916 and 1919-1920.

The Inpui people belong to the indigenous Naga communities of Manipur, India, primarily residing in the Haochong area of Noney District and the Tamenglong district.  They’re also found in locations such as Makuilongdi, Senapati headquarters, and Inthan (Waphong) within Senapati district, alongside Changangei, Tamphagei, Yurembam, Pantilong, and Sagolband in Imphal West.  Additionally, significant populations exist in both Nagaland and Assam.  Antrimon, a notable mountain peak approximately 12 km from Haochong village, dominates their territory, which is crisscrossed by rivers including Tuilang, Lingkwa, and Ra-ah. Historically, they were sometimes identified as Kabui alongside the Rongmei people, but the Inpui group represents the true origins of the “Kabui” name. Recognized as a Scheduled Tribe under the 1976 amendment to the Indian Constitution's Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders, they observe celebrations including Karing-ngei, Somdungnu, Tataaknu, and Muliaang.

Silas Boxley Mason II (October 22, 1879 – April 14, 1936) was an American construction executive and racehorse owner, born in Orange County, Virginia. He was part of a Mason family that had been involved with the construction business since 1827. A graduate of Washington and Lee University and Princeton University, he went on to make the Mason & Hanger company one of the largest construction contractors in the United States. His first high-profile venture came in 1927 when he was awarded the contract for the George Washington Bridge foundation on the New Jersey side. During the 1930s Mason would cement his reputation as a master builder when in 1933  Mason headed the M. W. A. K. consortium (Mason-Walsh-Atkinson, Kier) that built the Grand Coulee Dam in Mason City, Washington. His company would then  become involved in the construction of the Lincoln Tunnel. Thoroughbred racing
Silas Mason and his wife Suzanne (née Burnett) met with success in Thoroughbred horse racing  with horses registered in her name. A native Kentuckian, she was a descendant of Colonel Richard Henderson who, along with General George Rogers Clark, Daniel Boone, and others, were Kentucky pioneers who formed the Transylvania Land Company. The couple purchased a home and breeding farm near Lexington, Kentucky called Duntreath.

This research analyzes and calculates how a concentrated plastic region develops and changes during uniaxial loading of a bar whose cross-section varies. It uses an energy-driven method and establishes the key equations, incorporating realistic constraints and conditions at the changing elastic-plastic boundary, based on a fourth-order explicit gradient plasticity model featuring linear isotropic softening. The study presents four distinct cases varying the yield strength and stress patterns, providing results regarding load magnitude, plastic zone dimensions, plastic strain distribution and its derivatives, plastic lengthening, and energy consumption – all compared to a prior, non-variational gradient approach.

Shortly after Dreamworks screwed up with the uninspired "Shark Tale", Pixar contains its remarkably success story with "The Incredibles". And while I have to say that I liked "Finding Nemo" a bit better, "The Incredibles" is still an amazing movie.

First of all, this is because it's funny. It's not so funny that you're constantly laughing out loud, but there are more than enough good jokes in the movie to keep you entertained, and it's full of good observations about superhero movies (note all the ridiculous superhero and villain names) and references to other movies. It's also a brilliant James Bond spoof/homage, containing all the gadgets, secret island bases and crazy schemes that made early Bond movies so much fun.

Secondly, this movie has heart and charm in droves. It's full of memorably and likable characters you can really identify with and care about. Characters like Edna are instant classics. The voice acting is universally excellent, but Holly Hunter steals the show as Elastigirl. This is a movie that doesn't need toilet humor, characters modeled like celebrities, or a "hip" soundtrack...it easily succeeds on charm and style alone.

Also, I found it to be a surprisingly good action movie. The plentiful action sequences are full of energy, extremely fast-paced, and exciting, and put many a live-action movie to shame.

Finally, I also liked the tone and message of the movie. "The Incredibles" basically makes a plea against mediocrity, breaking with the politically correct idea that "everybody is special" (and thus nobody really is), and encouraging people to use the talents they have been given. I think this couldn't be more true. Not all people are equally talented (just compare Pixar to Dreamworks), but this is no reason to keep the talented people from not reaching their full potential just because it makes the less talented ones feel bad.

"The Incredibles", while maybe not as hilarious as I had hoped (though it's still very funny), is nonetheless an extremely entertaining movie, that manages to charm you wit its combination of great characters, lots of style, tongue-in-cheek attitude and good message. Highly recommended.

Ryu decides not to let the other man know what he does for a living. He says that he has a wife, but won't bring her up. At the end of the book his wife is killed in some accident.

"He said something that made this man's whole life seem meaningless." That was the first time he'd ever heard the name Ryu. It was a moment that rang in his ears for the rest of his life. Not long after, they separated.

From the start. From the moment they were married at their home in the city of Chigoku in Japan, it had been clear that Ryu had been made for this woman. There was something there that made her life so fulfilling, but also frightening.

It's the same with a lot of things, though. If you're going to call a woman in your life "that", you might as well live with a name like "that" for the rest of your life.

In fact, Sae had been calling him that ever since they met. It was the first time since he was ten years old that she mentioned it to him aloud.

As they lived together, there were other occasions when they were both conscious of each other's existence. And then, there were occasions where they were both completely conscious of no one else's.

"I had him," was how Ryu described that first night on which he lay awake, trying to make sense of it.

Fondly, too curious Nature, to adorn
Aurora with the blushes of the morn:
Why do her rosy lips breath gums and spice;
Unto the East, and sweet to Paradise?
Why do her eyes open the day? her hand
And voice intrance the panther, and command
Incensed winds; her breasts, the tents of love,
Smooth as the godded swan, or Venus' dove;
Soft as the balmy dew whose every touch
Is pregnant; but why those rich spoils, when such
Wonder and perfection must be led
A bridal captive unto Tithon's bed?
Ag'd, and deformed Tithon! must thy twine
Circle and blast at once what care and time
Had made for wonder? must pure beauty have
No other foil but ruin and a grave?
So have I seen the pride of Nature's store,
The orient pearl chained to the sooty Moor;
So hath the diamond's bright ray been set
In night, and wedded to the negro jet.
See, see, how thick those showers of pearl do fall
To weep her ransom, or her funeral,
Whose every treasured drop, congealed, might bring,
Freedom and ransom to a fettered kin,
While tyrant Wealth stands by, and laughs to see
How he can wed love and antipathy.
Hymen, thy pine burns with adulterate fire;
Thou and thy quivered boy did once conspire
To mingle equal flames, and then no shine
Of gold, but beauty, dressed the Paphian shrine;
Roses and lilies kiss'd; the amorous vine
Did with the fair and straight-limb'd elm entwine.

To make this hearty stew, you’ll need approximately 5-6 quarts of water, 2 pounds of dried large lima beans (rinsed), 2-3 medium onions (peeled and chopped), 6-7 medium potatoes (diced), plus 2 more medium potatoes grated, 2 pounds of cubed and browned bacon, 2 carrots (diced), 2 stalks of celery (diced), and 4 cups of diced tomatoes (canned works well). Seasonings include 2 bay leaves, ¾ tablespoon of thyme, ¾ tablespoon of paprika, 2 tablespoons of lemon juice, salt, and pepper. If desired, incorporate optional additions like 1 cup of grated cauliflower or 1 cup of flour for a richer broth. Begin by combining the lima beans, onions, carrots, and celery with the water in a pot or Dutch oven. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for an hour. Next, stir in the grated potatoes and cook for another half hour. Then, add the remaining potatoes and the browned bacon. Optionally, add cauliflower or flour for thickness. Simmer for an additional half hour before incorporating the diced tomatoes, bay leaves, thyme, paprika, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and hot sauce. The stew can be finished on the stovetop for 3-4 hours, stirring occasionally and adding more water as needed, or transferred to a 7-8 quart slow cooker for 5-6 hours on low. For a chilled version, refrigerate overnight and reheat in the slow cooker with a touch more water, up to 6-7 hours, omitting the lemon juice until serving. It pairs exceptionally well with cornbread or multi-grain muffins.

Brewers' profits lose their fizz

 Financial results for the world's biggest beer makers have been flatlining in recent months as a young generation shuns the drink.

AB InBev, the owner of Budweiser and Stella Artois, reported a 0.5% fall in organic revenue in the first three months of the year.

The company blamed bad weather in Europe for a 1.3% drop in volumes, while profits were also hit by higher commodity prices.

Heineken, the world's second biggest brewer, reported a 0.9% fall in beer volumes in the first three months of the year.

also announced a 0.5% drop in revenues, blaming "Korea and Nigeria".

Carlsberg, the third biggest global brewer, posted a 0.4% drop in beer sales in the first three months of 2018.

The Danish company said that it had seen "high single-digit growth" in eastern Europe, but this was offset by declines in China and Western Europe.

All three companies have been trying to offset falling demand for beer in developed markets by raising prices and investing in new products.

AB InBev said it was "encouraged" by the performance of its new non-alcoholic beer, Budweiser Zero.

But it is clear that the global beer market is struggling to find growth.

In the US, the world's biggest beer market, sales have been in decline for a decade.

In 2017, beer sales fell by 1% in volume and 2% in value, according to industry group the Beer Institute.

The trend is being driven by a younger generation of drinkers who are turning their backs on the traditional pint.

"People are drinking less beer and they're drinking better beer," said Simon Thorpe, chief executive of Sheffield-based beer maker and pub group Molson Coors.

"The big challenge for the beer category is how do we continue to be relevant to consumers, particularly younger consumers."

The global beer market is forecast to grow by just 1% this year, according to research group Euromonitor.

John Hamal Hubbard developed the Medusa algorithm, which accepts two postcritically finite quadratic polynomials and produces their corresponding quadratic rational map (provided one exists). The algorithm yields parameter approximations for this map, alongside an image of its Julia set. Convergence of these approximations is assessed via Thurston’s topological characterization of rational maps. Christian Henriksen and undergraduate researchers David Farris and Kuon Ju Liu implemented this algorithm in 1998. This paper details the algorithm and its implementation, presenting example outputs including numerous images, along with explorations into shared matings, Lattes examples, and sequences of mating operations.

Chris Child, operating under the name Kodomo, is a Portland, Maine-based composer—an Emmy Award winner and full-time musician—recognized primarily for his contributions to video games like Harmonix’s *Amplitude* and *Frequency*, and Apple’s *Phase*, which includes “Spira Mirabilis.” “Kodomo” means “child” in Japanese, referencing both his last name and his upbringing in Japan. His debut album, *Still Life*, is a deeply thoughtful project where each track draws inspiration from photographs taken during his travels. Instead of traditional titles, the songs are named after their corresponding images; for instance, “Concept 13” originated from a photograph illustrating the Fibonacci sequence, a pattern frequently observed in nature. This mathematical ratio, specifically 0.618, influenced every aspect of the music – melody, sound design, and development speed, resulting in a composition characterized by its harmonious and organic feel.

The book begins in April 1979 at a small academic conference at the University of Rummidge. It is the first conference that Persse McGarrigle, (a reference to Percival the grail knight), an innocent young Irishman who recently completed his master's thesis on T. S. Eliot, has attended. He teaches at the fictional University College, Limerick, after having been mistakenly interviewed because the administration sent the interview invitation to him instead of someone else with the same last name. Several important characters are introduced: Rummidge professor Philip Swallow, American professor Morris Zapp, retired Cambridge professor Sybil Maiden, and the beautiful Angelica Pabst, with whom McGarrigle falls immediately in love. Much of the rest of the book is his quest to find and win her. Angelica tells Persse that she was adopted by an executive at KLM after she was found, abandoned, in the washroom of an airplane in flight. Persse professes his love for her, but she leaves the conference without telling him where she has gone. Morris Zapp and Philip Swallow, who are seeing each other for the first time in ten years after the events of Changing Places, have a long evening talk. Since the previous novel, Swallow has become a professor and head of the English Department. Zapp has discovered deconstructionism and reinvented himself academically. Swallow tells Zapp about an incident a few years before, when after almost dying in a plane crash he spent the night at a British Council official's home and slept with the official's wife, Joy. Soon after, Swallow read in the newspaper that Joy, the official, and their son had died in a plane crash. Part II of the book begins by going around the world, time zone to time zone, showing what different characters are doing all at the same time: Morris Zapp travelling; Australian Rodney Wainright trying to write a conference paper; Zapp's ex-wife Désirée trying to write a novel; Howard Ringbaum trying to convince his wife Thelma to sleep with him on an airplane so he can join the Mile High Club; Siegfried von Turpitz talking to Arthur Kingfisher about the new UNESCO chair of literary criticism; Rudyard Parkinson plotting to get that chair; Turkish Akbil Borak reading William Hazlitt to prepare for a visit by Swallow; Akira Sakazaki translating English novelist Ronald Frobisher into Japanese; Ronald Frobisher having breakfast; Italian Fulvia Morgana (a reference to Morgan le Fay) meeting Morris Zapp on a plane; and more.` Cheryl Summerbee is also introduced. She is a check-in clerk for British Airways at Heathrow and plays a small but very important role in helping, or hindering, other characters as they travel around the world. She loves reading romance novels, especially the kind published by "Bills and Moon" (a fictionalized Mills & Boon). People continue to move around from conference to conference around the world in Part III. Persse continues to pursue Angelica. At a meeting in Amsterdam, Persse hears the German literary scholar Siegfried von Turpitz speaking about ideas that he submitted in an unpublished book, and all but accuses von Turpitz of plagiarism. Zapp rises to defend Persse from von Turpitz. Later, Persse sees someone who looks like Angelica, and thinks she has appeared in pornographic movies and worked as a stripper. In Turkey, Phillip Swallow meets Joy, the woman he thought was dead. She explains that only her husband had been on the plane that crashed. They begin an affair, and Swallow plans to leave his wife. Events and characters move along in Part IV, often with direct reference to the genre of romance, such as Sybil Maiden (who at one point acts as a sibyl) saying that grail knights "were such boobies... All they had to do was ask a question at the right moment, and they generally muffed it." Zapp is kidnapped by an underground left-wing movement, but is later released after pressure from Morgana. Persse, who has won an award and got a credit card, has enough money to continue to chase Angelica but never manages to catch up with her. She does leave him a clue referencing The Faerie Queene and he discovers that she has an identical twin, and it is the twin, Lily, who made the pornographic movies. When Persse meets Cheryl Summerbee again, she is now reading not romance novels but romances such as Orlando Furioso and critics such as Northrop Frye after Angelica has passed through her line. Persse is happy to learn this, but Cheryl is shaken to see that Persse is infatuated with Angelica, because she loves him herself. Persse continues to chase Angelica around the world, to conferences in Hawaii, Tokyo, and Hong Kong, and Jerusalem, but he never catches up with her. At that Jerusalem conference, Philip Swallow is with Joy, but after he sees his son there he becomes psychosomatically ill, which people think might be Legionnaires' Disease in a moment of panic. This stops the conference, and leads to the end of Philip and Joy's affair. Part V takes place at the Modern Language Association conference in New York at the end of 1979. All of the characters in the book are there. Arthur Kingfisher oversees a panel discussion about criticism where Swallow, Zapp, Morgana, and others present their opinions on what literary criticism is. Zapp's kidnapping experience has cured him of his interest in deconstructionism. Persse (contrary to what Sybil Maiden had said about knights not asking the right question at the right time) asks, "What follows if everyone agrees with you?" Kingfisher is inspired by this question, and recovers from his mental and physical impotence. Persse finally finds Angelica and hears her read a paper about romances that directly reflects the structure of Small World itself: "No sooner is one crisis in the fortunes of the hero averted than a new one presents itself; no sooner has one mystery been solved than another is raised; no sooner has one adventure been concluded than another begins... The greatest and most characteristic romances are often unfinished - they end only with the author's exhaustion, as a woman's capacity for orgasm is limited only by her physical stamina. Romance is a multiple orgasm." After this talk, Persse runs through the hotel and sees a woman he takes to be Angelica, kisses her and declares that he loves her. She takes him up to her hotel room where they make love, in Persse's first sexual experience. However, after this encounter, she reveals that she is not Angelica, but the twin sister, Lily. Persse feels ashamed, but Lily convinces him that he was "in love with a dream". Later in the evening, Arthur Kingfisher announces that he will offer himself as a candidate for the UNESCO chair. Right afterwards, Sybil Maiden steps forward and announces that she is Angelica and Lily's mother and Kingfisher is their father, which throws the entire meeting into a joyous uproar. Angelica introduces Persse to her fiancee, Peter McGarrigle, the person whose job Persse was interviewed for back in Ireland. However, Peter is not angry, because as a result, he went to America and there met Angelica. Swallow has returned to his wife, saying "Basically I failed in the role of a romantic hero." All of the narrative threads of the novel wrap up but for one: Persse realizes that Cheryl Summerbee, not Angelica, is the woman for him, and he flies to Heathrow to see her. He arrives at the airport on New Year's Eve, but learns that Cheryl no longer works there, having been fired the day before Persse arrives. The new attendant tells Persse that Cheryl wanted to travel anyway at some point, and took this as her chance. No one knows where she has gone. The novel ends with Persse wondering "where in the small, narrow world he should begin to look for her."

The Shrimal (Srimal) Jains originated in the historical town of Bhinmal, Rajasthan, and trace their roots to the ancient Jain and Hindu communities of southern Rajasthan. Historically, they were prosperous traders and moneylenders, serving as treasurers and ministers within Rajput courts under titles like Dewan or Durbari.  Legend states they descended from the goddess Lakshmi, and their lineage is renowned for its business skills; they often inherited lavish Havelis and mansions bestowed upon them by grateful kings for their roles as royal advisors. Considered the most senior gotra within the larger Oswal merchant-minister caste prevalent in northern India, the Srimals separated themselves from the Oswals, largely due to their predominantly Jain faith—a legacy stemming from the conversion of Raja of Osnagar after observing a Jain ascetic’s miraculous act. While most Srimals are Jain and worship Goddess Lakshmi, some maintain a Hindu Vaishnava practice. Today, they primarily inhabit Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.

I realize this might not be the right subreddit, and appreciate it if moderators remove it. Recently, after watching Seaspiracy, I became deeply concerned about the potential impact on health. This led me to reevaluate my switch from no-till farming to using "organic" salts. For about four and a half years, I practiced a continuous no-till system primarily for producing plants for individuals with weakened immune systems. I then investigated concerns regarding heavy metals in commonly used "organic" fertilizers – the results were troubling. Considering cannabis's tendency to absorb heavy metals, I seriously questioned my approach to what I considered healthier cultivation.
