Microsoft is offering Windows XP users a free swap to a later version of the operating system, in an attempt to boost the number of computers that are secure against malware.

The company has promised to provide a free one-year licence for Windows 7, Windows 8 or Windows 10 to any XP user who visits a special website.

The offer is being run in partnership with the nonprofit group, Preserve Connectivity.

"Customers who browse the web with an unpatched browser on an unsupported operating system are more vulnerable to security risks," said Christine Hall, head of Microsoft's Windows marketing for Asia Pacific.

"This offer is for those consumers who are unaware or less informed about the risks of continuing to use an unsupported operating system."

Windows XP was released in 2001 and discontinuted in 2014. Nevertheless, analyst firm NetMarketShare reported that as of March this year, it was still running on 8.93% of desktops.

It is particularly popular in Asia, where it accounts for more than a quarter of desktops.

Windows 7, which was released in 2009, will also be discontinued next year.

However, it is still used on half of all desktops, according to NetMarketShare.

Microsoft is making the offer available in Hong Kong, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines and India.

Traditional “background subtraction” methods, often used to detect moving vehicles in videos like those of freeways, work by removing the average background from each frame. This leaves behind only objects that change over time. However, this method is imprecise – it struggles with slowly moving items and cannot differentiate between genuine motion and shadows. This research proposes a new approach where each pixel is classified based on its appearance within various categories. We employ a mixture-of-Gaussians classification model for every pixel, learned through an efficient, adaptive unsupervised algorithm (an enhanced Expectation-Maximization).  Unlike traditional averaging, our system dynamically adjusts the probability of each category assigned to a pixel based on its likelihood. Consequently, slow-moving objects are accurately detected. Furthermore, it outperforms simple thresholding techniques at identifying and eliminating shadows. Implementing this method within the Roadwatch traffic surveillance project should lead to substantial gains in vehicle recognition and monitoring.

Neil Hope (born September 24, 1972 – deceased November 25, 2007), a Canadian actor recognized as Neil Hope, gained recognition for his role as Derek “Wheels” Wheeler in the teen series *Degrassi Junior High* and *Degrassi High* between 1987 and 1991. Before this, he played Griff in *The Kids of Degrassi Street* from 1985 to 1986, returning briefly for appearances in *Degrassi: The Next Generation*. Sadly, his death wasn’t revealed until five years after it occurred in 2007.

Born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, on September 24, 1972, Hope was the fourth of four sons and fifth child overall within a family marked by parental alcoholism and instability, resulting in frequent moves between his parents' homes. Despite these challenges, he maintained a strong bond with his father, whom he viewed as a source of support and affection.  He frequently watched television with his father and siblings, sparking an early fascination with how shows were created. With financial assistance from his father, he enrolled in a television training program and commissioned professional photographs.  His acting career began with a part in “Martin Meets The Pirates” of *Kids of Degrassi Street*; Hope described television as providing a refuge from personal difficulties and a way to actively participate in its creation.

This work connects initial expansions of basic modules with specific filtrations within standard modules using graded Hecke algebras. We utilize insights from the Langlands classification and a refined grasp of module structures; notably, we examine modules stemming from Knapp-Stein-like intertwining operators, which are quotients of generalized standard modules. Furthermore, we derive consequences concerning the blocks of finite-dimensional modules in these graded Hecke algebras. As an example, we calculate Ext-groups for irreducible modules within a block of the graded Hecke algebra of type $C_3$, contingent upon a version of the Jantzen conjecture.

Everton manager David Moyes will discipline striker James Beattie after all for his headbutt on Chelsea defender William Gallas.
The Scot initially defended Beattie, whose dismissal put Everton on the back foot in a game they ultimately lost 1-0, saying Gallas overreacted. But he has had a rethink after looking over the video evidence again. He said: "I believe that I should set the record straight by conceding that the dismissal was right and correct." Moyes added: "My comments on Saturday came immediately after the final whistle and at a point when I had only had the opportunity to see one, very quick re-run of the incident."
The club website also reported that Beattie, who seemed unrepentant after Saturday's match, insisting Gallas "would have stayed down a lot longer" if he had headbutted him, has now apologised. Moyes continued: "Although the incident was totally out of character - James has never even been suspended before in his career - his actions were unacceptable and had a detrimental effect on his team-mates. "James did issue a formal apology to myself, his team-mates and to the Everton supporters immediately after the game and that was the right thing to have done. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation based on affinity learning. Our approach is based on the principle of maximin affinity, which aims to maximize the similarity between neighboring pixels while simultaneously minimizing the similarity between dissimilar pixels. To learn the affinity between pixels, we use a convolutional neural network (CNN) which is trained using a novel loss function that is based on the maximin principle. We evaluate our approach on the Weizmann Horse Segmentation dataset and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our approach outperforms existing methods and offers a new way to approach the problem of image segmentation.

The families EPT (resp. EPG) Edge Intersection Graphs of Paths in a tree
(resp. in a grid) are well studied graph classes. Recently we introduced the
graph classes Edge-Intersecting and Non-Splitting Paths in a Tree ENPT, and in
a Grid (ENPG). It was shown that ENPG contains an infinite hierarchy of
subclasses that are obtained by restricting the number of bends in the paths.
Motivated by this result, in this work we focus on one bend {ENPG} graphs. We
show that one bend ENPG graphs are properly included in two bend ENPG graphs.
We also show that trees and cycles are one bend ENPG graphs, and characterize
the split graphs and co-bipartite graphs that are one bend ENPG. We prove that
the recognition problem of one bend ENPG split graphs is NP-complete even in a
very restricted subfamily of split graphs. Last we provide a linear time
recognition algorithm for one bend ENPG co-bipartite graphs.

2-1/2 cups Whole Milk
1/2 cups Heavy Cream
1/2 cups Light Agave Syrup
2 ounces, weight Unsweetened Baking Chocolate
1/2 cups Cocoa Powder
1/4 teaspoons Salt
4 whole Eggs
2 Tablespoons Cornstarch Stirred Into 1/4 Cup Cold Water
16 envelopes Sweet-N-Low
2 teaspoons Real Vanilla
Pour milk, cream and agave into a medium sized pot. Add chopped chocolate. Stir in cocoa and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring frequently, until cocoa is dispersed and chocolate is melted. Continue to heat until mixture is quite hot. Meanwhile, crack eggs into a small mixing bowl. Stir cornstarch into water until smooth. Stir cornstarch water into eggs. Set aside. Open Sweet-N-Low packets and place into a small bowl. Measure vanilla into another small bowl. When milk mixture in pot is quite hot, like hot chocolate, spoon about 1 cup into the egg mixture and mix well. This tempers your eggs so they don't scramble when you add them to the pot. Once your eggs are well mixed, pour this egg mixture back into the pot with the rest of the hot milk, etc. Continue to cook until this mixture is very thick. It will coat a spoon thickly. At this point you can remove the pot from the heat and blend mixture with a stick blender, or pour into a blender and blend until completely smooth. Now add the vanilla and the sweetener to the mix. Blend well. Pour the pudding into serving-sized bowls or into one or two larger bowls. Place in the fridge until cold. Eat. Yum yum.

To make this lasagna, you’ll need 14 pounds of ground beef, 3 minced garlic cloves, 1 cup of finely chopped onion, 8 ounces of chopped mushrooms, 6 ounces of tomato paste, 32 ounces of diced tomatoes (with their juice), 1 ½ cups of dry red wine, 1 teaspoon of dried oregano, 1 bay leaf, 1 ½ teaspoons of salt, 1 ½ teaspoons of black pepper, 1 tablespoon of light brown sugar, 8 ounces of lasagna noodles, 12 ounces of cottage cheese, 1 egg, 8 ounces of Swiss cheese, and 1 ½ cups of grated Parmesan cheese. First, brown the beef, onion, and mushrooms in a large skillet with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, seasoning with some salt and pepper. Bake for 35-45 minutes, covering loosely with foil if the top browns too quickly. Let it cool for 15 minutes before serving with a salad and garlic bread – this recipe yields 12 servings.

A stuffless ghost above his struggling land,
Retching in vain to render up the groan
That is not there, being aching dust's alone?

Scaling properties of time series are usually studied in terms of the scaling
laws of empirical moments, which are the time average estimates of moments of
the dynamic variable. Nonlinearities in the scaling function of empirical
moments are generally regarded as a sign of multifractality in the data. We
show that, except for the Brownian motion, this method fails to disclose the
correct monofractal nature of self-similar L\'evy processes. We prove that for
this class of processes it produces apparent multifractality characterised by a
piecewise-linear scaling function with two different regimes, which match at
the stability index of the considered process. This result is motivated by
previous numerical evidence. It is obtained by introducing an appropriate
stochastic normalisation which is able to cure empirical moments, without
hiding their dependence on time, when moments they aim at estimating do not
exist.

"Ingredients: 1/2 cup butter, softened 4 cups shredded Cheddar cheese 3 tablespoons chopped green onions 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce 1 loaf French bread Directions Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). In a medium bowl, mix together the butter, cheese, green onion and Worcestershire sauce until well blended. Cut the top off the loaf of bread, leaving about an inch at the bottom. Hollow out the inside of the bread, leaving a shell with about 1-inch thick walls. Fill the hollowed out center with the cheese mixture. Place the lid back onto the filled bread. Wrap in aluminum foil and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes."

1 large onion, chopped
100 g smoked bacon lardons
2 tablespoons olive oil
500 g lean stewing beef, cubed
2 tablespoons plain flour
3 parsnips, cubed
500 ml brown ale
300 ml beef stock
2 tablespoons cranberry jelly or 2 tablespoons red currant jelly
4 fresh thyme sprigs
greens, to serve (optional)
butter, for greasing
300 g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
2 teaspoons English mustard powder
140 g shredded suet
Heat a large pan and cook the onion and lardons together for 5 mins until golden. Scoop out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Add the oil to the pan, dust the beef with the flour, then evenly brown over a high heat. Add the parsnips, ale, stock, jelly, thyme and lardon mixture to the pan. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hrs until the meat is tender. Generously butter a 1.5-litre pudding basin. To make the pastry, mix together the flour, mustard powder, suet and 1/2 tsp table salt. Add enough cold water, about 150ml, to make a soft dough. Remove one-quarter of the dough and set to one side. On a heavily floured surface, roll out the remaining dough to make a large round, big enough to line the basin. Carefully lay the pastry in the basin (aim to have 1cm of pastry overhanging the rim), then press the edges of the join together to seal. Roll out the remaining one-quarter into a circle big enough to cover the top. Pour off the cooking liquid from the filling into a small pan and set aside. Discard the thyme stalks. Spoon the filling into the lined basin and pour over 100ml of the cooking liquid. Fold over the overhanging pastry and brush with water. Place the lid on top, pressing firmly around the edges to seal. Butter a sheet of baking parchment, fold in a large pleat and lay, butter-side down, on top of the pudding. Cover with a pleated layer of foil and finally tie with string, making a loop for the handle so you can lift the pudding easily. Sit a small trivet or a large cookie cutter in the bottom of a deep saucepan that's big enough to take the basin easily. Half-fill the pan with water and bring to the boil. Lower in the pudding, cover and simmer for 2 hrs, topping up with boiling water when necessary. Reheat the cooking liquid, bubbling it down a little so it reduces into a tasty gravy. Carefully lift out the pudding. Run a knife around the rim, then turn out and serve with gravy and greens, if you like.

We build on recent works on Stein's method for functions of multivariate
normal random variables to derive bounds for the rate of convergence of some
asymptotically chi-square distributed statistics. We obtain some general bounds
and establish some simple sufficient conditions for convergence rates of order
$n^{-1}$ for smooth test functions. These general bounds are applied to
Friedman's statistic for comparing $r$ treatments across $n$ trials and the
family of power divergence statistics for goodness-of-fit across $n$ trials and
$r$ classifications, with index parameter $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ (Pearson's
statistic corresponds to $\lambda=1$). We obtain a $O(n^{-1})$ bound for the
rate of convergence of Friedman's statistic for any number of treatments
$r\geq2$. We also obtain a $O(n^{-1})$ bound on the rate of convergence of the
power divergence statistics for any $r\geq2$ when $\lambda$ is a positive
integer or any real number greater than 5. We conjecture that the $O(n^{-1})$
rate holds for any $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.

Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) has great potential for medical imaging
applications. Most of the existing FSS techniques require abundant annotated
semantic classes for training. However, these methods may not be applicable for
medical images due to the lack of annotations. To address this problem we make
several contributions: (1) A novel self-supervised FSS framework for medical
images in order to eliminate the requirement for annotations during training.
Additionally, superpixel-based pseudo-labels are generated to provide
supervision; (2) An adaptive local prototype pooling module plugged into
prototypical networks, to solve the common challenging foreground-background
imbalance problem in medical image segmentation; (3) We demonstrate the general
applicability of the proposed approach for medical images using three different
tasks: abdominal organ segmentation for CT and MRI, as well as cardiac
segmentation for MRI. Our results show that, for medical image segmentation,
the proposed method outperforms conventional FSS methods which require manual
annotations for training.

US oil prices have fallen by 6%, driven down by forecasts of a mild winter in the densely populated northeast.
Light crude oil futures fell $2.86 to $41.32 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange (Nymex), and have now lost $4 in five days. Nonetheless, US crude is still 30% more expensive than at the beginning of 2004, boosted by growing demand and bottlenecks at refineries. Traders ignored the possible effects of Asia's tidal waves on global supplies.
Instead, the focus is now on US consumption, which is heavily influenced in the short term by the weather. "With the revised milder temperatures... I'm more inclined to think we'll push lower and test the $40-40.25 range," said John Brady of ABN AMRO. "The market definitely feels to be on the defensive." Statistics released last week showed that stockpiles of oil products in the US had risen, an indication that severe supply disruptions may not arise this winter, barring any serious incident. Oil prices have broken records in 2004, topping $50 a barrel at one point, driven up by a welter of worries about unrest in Iraq and Saudi Arabia, rising demand and supply bottlenecks. London's International Petroleum Exchange remained closed for the Christmas holiday.

In this paper, we present a theoretical analysis of active contours on graphs, which are a generalization of traditional active contour models that operate on graph-structured data. We propose a new formulation of active contours on graphs, based on a probabilistic framework that allows for efficient inference and learning. Our approach enables the integration of domain knowledge into the segmentation process, leading to improved accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods.

We derive a set of algorithms for active contour evolution on graphs, including a novel iterative algorithm that converges to an optimal solution under certain conditions. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical bound on the convergence rate of our algorithm, providing insights into its performance.

Our analysis also covers the case where the graph structure is uncertain or noisy, in which case we propose a robust variant of our algorithm that can handle such scenarios. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on several real-world datasets, showcasing its ability to accurately segment complex objects in various domains.

Overall, our work provides a solid foundation for understanding and improving active contour models on graph-structured data, opening up new possibilities for applications in computer vision, machine learning, and related fields.

Tumor detection in biomedical imaging is a time-consuming process for medical
professionals and is not without errors. Thus in recent decades, researchers
have developed algorithmic techniques for image processing using a wide variety
of mathematical methods, such as statistical modeling, variational techniques,
and machine learning. In this paper, we propose a semi-automatic method for
liver segmentation of 2D CT scans into three labels denoting healthy, vessel,
or tumor tissue based on graph cuts. First, we create a feature vector for each
pixel in a novel way that consists of the 59 intensity values in the time
series data and propose a simplified perimeter cost term in the energy
functional. We normalize the data and perimeter terms in the functional to
expedite the graph cut without having to optimize the scaling parameter
$\lambda$. In place of a training process, predetermined tissue means are
computed based on sample regions identified by expert radiologists. The
proposed method also has the advantage of being relatively simple to implement
computationally. It was evaluated against the ground truth on a clinical CT
dataset of 10 tumors and yielded segmentations with a mean Dice similarity
coefficient (DSC) of .77 and mean volume overlap error (VOE) of 36.7%. The
average processing time was 1.25 minutes per slice.

Fig and Peach Salad Recipe

Ingredients:
- 6 fresh figs, quartered
- 4 ripe peaches, sliced
- 1/2 cup of walnuts or almonds (or both!), chopped
- 4 oz. crumbled goat cheese or feta cheese 
- 2 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- The juice of half a lemon
- Fresh mint leaves, chopped
- Arugula or baby spinach for serving 

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine the quartered figs, sliced peaches, chopped nuts, and crumbled cheese.
2.In a small bowl mix together the honey, lemon juice, and mint leaves.
3. Pour the dressing over the fruit mixture and gently toss to coat.
4. Serve immediately over a bed of arugula or baby spinach leaves.
5. Enjoy your sweet and healthy Fig and Peach Salad!

This research investigates how cataract impacts automated iris recognition accuracy, finding it substantially lower than for healthy eyes. Existing studies are limited by small, incomplete datasets lacking diverse disease representations. We created a new dataset comprising 1288 eye images from 37 patients at the Medical University of Warsaw, encompassing cataracts alongside other conditions like altered iris patterns due to illness or injury. These images were taken using both near-infrared and visible light. Given the prevalence of cataract within the dataset, our analysis concentrates primarily on this condition. Using three iris recognition techniques—both commercial and academic—we evaluated their performance on both healthy and cataract-affected eyes, measuring genuine match scores. The results demonstrate a notable decline in recognition reliability, evidenced by increased genuine scores across all three systems (ranging from a 12% rise in an academic matcher to a 175% increase in a commercial matcher). This elevated scoring impacted the false non-match rates in two of the matched systems.  To date, this is the first study utilizing multiple iris matchers and exploring iris image segmentation as a possible factor contributing to reduced accuracy.

For this recipe, you’ll need a 5-to-6 pound pork shoulder or Boston butt roast, along with 2 teaspoons of salt. Start by seasoning the pork with salt and chilling it for 30 minutes. Build your first charcoal fire using 5 to 6 pounds of hardwood charcoal; allow it to burn for 15 to 20 minutes until covered in gray ash. Divide the coals into two piles on either side of the grill. Add one hickory chunk to each pile, then set up a cooking rack and place the pork, skin-side down, in the center. Keep the lid fully open for ventilation. Simultaneously prepare a second charcoal fire with 12 briquettes in a separate grill, letting it burn for 30 minutes until ashen. Add 6 briquettes to each coal pile, placing another hickory chunk on top of each. Repeat this process every 30 minutes. Continue cooking, covered, for approximately 5 hours and 30 minutes, or until a meat thermometer reads at least 165° Fahrenheit in the thickest part – turn the pork once after the final two hours. This temperature ensures easy bone removal. Once cooked, let the pork rest briefly before chopping and serving with Cider Vinegar Barbecue Sauce or Peppery Vinegar Sauce.

1 (16 ounce) package frozen pound cake, thawed
1 (8 ounce) package cream cheese, softened
1/2 cup confectioners' sugar
1 cup heavy whipping cream
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling

Directions:

1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour one 9x13 inch baking pan.

2. In a large bowl, combine thawed cake, cream cheese, and confectioners' sugar. Mix well and spread evenly into the prepared pan.

3. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 25 minutes. Cool completely.

4. In a large bowl, combine whipping cream, vanilla extract, and cherry pie filling. Mix well and spread over the cooled cake.

5. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

Finally, a Buendía descendant unlocks a coded message revealing the source of all the family’s luck and suffering across the centuries.

1/4 teaspoon rapid rise yeast
1 1/2 cups water at room temperature
1 3/4 teaspoons salt
4 cups all-purpose flour, or as needed
1/2 teaspoon cornmeal, or as needed
Place yeast into the bottom of a large mixing bowl and stir with water; mix in salt. Beat flour into yeast mixture with a wooden spoon until dough is thick and sticky and pulls flour from the side of the bowl, 5 to 10 minutes. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let stand in a turned-off oven until doubled in size, 12 to 14 hours. Dough will be bubbly and very sticky. Place a silicone baking mat onto a baking sheet and dust generously with cornmeal. Use a floured spatula to scrape dough out onto a well-floured work surface and dust dough with flour. With well-floured hands, pat dough into a rectangle and cut into 4 equal-size pieces. Dust a piece of dough with flour and use your floured fingers to gently roll and stretch it out into a log about 10 inches long and 1 1/2 inches around. Gently transfer to prepared baking sheet. If desired, wipe off excess cornmeal with a damp paper towel. Repeat with another piece of dough. (Reserve remaining dough to bake later or prepare 2 baking sheets to bake all 4 at once). Dust loaves lightly with flour. Dust a large piece of plastic wrap with flour and drape plastic lightly over the baking sheet with floured side down. Let loaves rise, covered, until doubled, 1 to 1 1/2 hour. Move oven racks to the bottom and middle positions. Preheat oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C) or as high as your oven will go. Place an oven-safe baking dish full of water into bottom rack of the oven. Use a sharp kitchen shears to cut 4 or 5 angled slashes into the top of each loaf. Poke down the little sharp tips of dough left by the scissors. Spray loaves with water, using a spray bottle. Bake in the preheated oven until baguettes are browned, about 15 minutes, spraying loaves with water after 5 minutes and 10 minutes. Turn the pan around on the second spraying. Transfer baguettes to a cooling rack and let cool to room temperature before slicing with a serrated knife.

When Sara's mother is killed in a car accident she comes to live in a predominately black area in Chicago. She is befriended by black Chenille and starts to fall for her brother Derek. Derek teaches her the latest hip-hop dances to help her fit in and together they begin to fall for each other. However a white girl seeing a clever black man is never going to be popular and the couple must overcome many obstacles to see their dreams and be true to themselves.

Did someone say `a black Dirty Dancing?' Essentially that's what this is, although the story is naturally a bit more urban than that film. The story is about overcoming to reach your dreams, and it does it quite well  better than I expected. The love story is nice without being too romanticised. The obstacles are the usual things in an `urban' film  the challenge of mixed race relationships, the temptation to back up your crew instead of getting out etc. These are quite cliched but are still well done.

My main problem came with the strength of black culture in the filmnot every black person (even in a poor area) talks like a gangstaand not everyone says `aiiiirite'  and why did Sara only become accepted when she started to imitate black culture and speak in that way. It may be realistic, but I felt that Sara should have been allowed to be herself rather than be seen to be assimilated into the hip-hop culture (I don't mean that she shouldn't have got involved with the scene  but did she have to lose part of herself to get there?). However these are minor side issues that many people won't even think about.

The cast are good for MTV teens. Julia Stiles is cool and Thomas is cute and charming. The rest of the cast fall into so many black stereotypes  we have gangsta friend, baby mothers galore, useless baby father, jealous bitchy ex-girlfriends etc. However they are just what you expect so I wasn't too upset. Fredro Starr was cool as Malakai  even if the character was just one big hood cliché.

The soundtrack is hot and the dance scenes are sexy  I wish I could do it! They are much more enjoyable than Dirty Dancing's scenes  although some day this will feel dated too! Overall I expected another piece of MTV teen tat, but I was pleasantly surprised by a story that, despite being ridden with clichés, is actually very involving and enjoyable.

Jeremy Fisher resides in a moist cottage nestled among buttercups near a pond. His dwelling is perpetually damp, and his movements are often “slippy-sloppy” due to the water, yet he enjoys the sensation of being wet and remains immune to illness. Seeking an outing, he decides to fish when rain falls. If he catches more than five minnows, he’ll host a gathering for his companions. Equipped with a raincoat, waterproof boots, a fishing rod, and a basket, he journeys to his lily-pad boat with powerful leaps. He paddles to a promising spot and settles onto his pad, preparing his equipment – a small red float and a horsehair line. After an unsuccessful hour, he pauses for a butterfly sandwich. Distracted by a water beetle and rustling rodents, he relocates and casts his line, instantly hooking a stickleback named Jack Sharp, which painfully pricks his fingers. A school of fish jeers at his misfortune, prompting him to retreat as a trout swiftly grabs him, ejecting only his goloshes. He surfaces dramatically, resembling a cork, and returns to the pond’s edge. Exhausted, he climbs the bank and hops home across the meadow, determined to abandon fishing. Later, adorned with bandages on his fingers, he receives guests: Sir Isaac Newton, a newt sporting a black and gold waistcoat, and Alderman Ptolemy Tortoise, accompanied by a salad in a sack. Jeremy serves roasted grasshoppers with ladybirds.

We introduce a new light-field dataset of materials, and take advantage of
the recent success of deep learning to perform material recognition on the 4D
light-field. Our dataset contains 12 material categories, each with 100 images
taken with a Lytro Illum, from which we extract about 30,000 patches in total.
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mid-size dataset for
light-field images. Our main goal is to investigate whether the additional
information in a light-field (such as multiple sub-aperture views and
view-dependent reflectance effects) can aid material recognition. Since
recognition networks have not been trained on 4D images before, we propose and
compare several novel CNN architectures to train on light-field images. In our
experiments, the best performing CNN architecture achieves a 7% boost compared
with 2D image classification (70% to 77%). These results constitute important
baselines that can spur further research in the use of CNNs for light-field
applications. Upon publication, our dataset also enables other novel
applications of light-fields, including object detection, image segmentation
and view interpolation.

1 tablespoon sugar

Press with floured hands to a 5 to 6 inch circle, place dough between floured wax paper and roll out to desired thickness, remove top piece of wax paper and flip dough into 9 inch deep dish pie plate, remove other sheet. For the Creamy Filling: In medium size bowl add heavy whipping cream, and beat with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Then add powdered sugar and vanilla, continue beating until firm peaks form. Set aside. In separate bowl add cream cheese and sugar, blend until sugar dissolves. Then fold whipped cream into cream cheese mixture. Spread on bottom of pie crust and refrigerate. For the Guava Topping: In medium size sauce pan on top of stove over medium heat add the water and bring to a simmer. Then add guava cubes stirring constantly until cubes are melted, then remove from heat and add the gelatin, sugar and food coloring, stirring until well blended. Then pour gently over cream filling and place in refrigerator till set. For Whipped Cream Topping: In medium size bowl add cream and beat with electric mixer until soft peaks form. Add powdered sugar and vanilla, continue beating until firm. Spoon topping into pastry bag and decorate as desired leaving some of the guava top showing.

1 cup Buttermilk
2 cups Breadcrumbs
1 Tablespoon Garlic Salt
2 whole Shallots, Finely Chopped
2 Tablespoons Butter
1 whole Onion, finely chopped
1 cup Brown Mushrooms, Chopped
2 Tablespoons Flour
2 cups Beef Broth
1 Tablespoon Salt And Pepper, Or To Taste
Preheat oven to 375F. After hammering out the tenderloins, soak them in the buttermilk for 5-10 minutes. After they have soaked, were going to bread them in the breadcrumb and garlic salt mixture. Lay one side down into the bread crumb mixture and on the side facing up, sprinkle in a generous layer of the sauteed shallots. Serve the venison with a few spears of steamed asparagus over the mushroom sauce and you are ready to eat!

Bill Conti's job of musical director of the Oscars show is not for the faint-hearted since conducting the orchestra is the ultimate plate-spinning assignment.
This year marks Conti's 17th turn at the helm of the Academy Awards orchestra. "The excitement is a live performance as a musician," he says. "All of your colleagues, everyone in the film industry is in the theatre. All the important people. "I guess it's just a television show but we always think it's a bit more.' The orchestra strikes up more than 110 times during the average Oscars show. As well as playing the presenters and winners on and off stage, it also performs during the commercial breaks to entertain the live audience in the house.
"It's a very busy evening, it takes a certain amount of preparation of music, orchestrating, sketching rehearsing, before the show. But you don't know what the unexpected will be and as the musical director, it's exciting," explains Conti. And much of the preparation goes into mastering scores that will never be performed. "We don't know who the winners will be. So when they say, 'the winner is', we have five different pieces of music in front of us, they say the name, we play the appropriate one immediately," adds Conti.
The orchestra is often called upon to play when the winners ramble on too long during their acceptance speeches, despite being told to be brief by the show's producers.
The decision to drown out or 'kill' the offending star with music is relayed from the director's box to the orchestra via Conti's earpiece. "I don't feel good about it at all. It's not my call though," he says. "When the director says 'music' the orchestra plays and he takes a long shot of the hall. We don't usually see the person speaking while his microphone is cut off. "The person that's been cut off, who's 10 feet from me, is glaring at me like it's death time." On occasions, some stars have taken it upon themselves to send a warning shot across the bows of the musical director before they start to speak. "Julia Roberts, when she came on, she asked me to not get ready to play because she had so much to do," he says. Conti received an Oscar in 1983 for the original score of The Right Stuff. He also received two nominations in the original song category in 1976 for Gonna Fly Now from Rocky and in 1981 for the title song from For Your Eyes Only.
"It's a moment in the sun," he says. "When people get up there, some people, this is hard to believe, people that spend their lives in front of the camera or audiences entertaining, might get a little flustered. "But there's this moment in time when the biggest award that they could possibly get in their life has been handed to them and they're either not in control or they want to thank everyone that they ever met."
The image of the Oscars telecast is one of slick presentation and smooth transitions between performances and the award categories. Behind the scenes, the key players, such as Conti, have a bewildering array of technical props to deal with. "There's a big script and video monitors you have to watch and there are also audio controls. I can control hearing in my ears, the left ear or the right ear - different things at different times.
"I have to communicate with the director. I have a little microphone that's attached to my headset. To open up that microphone, I have a footswitch," he explains. Conti's most nerve-wracking moment came during his first Oscars show as musical director, in 1977, when a member of the orchestra alerted him that they could smell smoke. Conti immediately told the show's director: "I start cursing and screaming, I tell him we're not going to die for this show - you must do something or I'm going to climb out of this pit with 60 musicians and we're going to be home in 10 minutes. "'Oh no Bill don't do anything," came the response. "Imagine these elegantly dressed ladies and gentlemen of the orchestra, 60 or so of them in the pit and while we're playing, firemen with their helmets and their hatchets crawling among us trying to find the reason for the smoke." The smell turned out to be new paint smouldering on the music stands. "No one died, it's not a big story, but it was scary at the time," laughs Conti. When the ceremony is over, the music director attends the annual Governor's Ball with his family. "I have a drink and relive the show," he says. "I'm not for too much carousing. I go home and unwind. It takes me about a day."

After losing her mother in a tragic car accident, Sara moves to a predominantly Black neighborhood in Chicago, where she finds friendship with Chenille and develops feelings for Derek, her brother. Derek introduces her to hip-hop dancing to aid her integration, and their connection deepens. Yet, a white woman’s attraction to a Black man often faces social disapproval, forcing them to navigate numerous challenges to pursue their aspirations and remain authentic.

This story resembles “Dirty Dancing” in its exploration of pursuing dreams, though set within a more urban context and executed effectively. The romance feels genuine, avoiding excessive sentimentality, while the obstacles—such as navigating interracial relationships and group loyalty—are familiar tropes handled competently. A key concern for me was the portrayal of Black culture; not all residents, even in a disadvantaged community, adopt stereotypical "gangsta" speech patterns, and Sara's acceptance seemed contingent on mimicking Black cultural expressions. While understandable from a realism standpoint, I wished she could have maintained her individuality rather than assimilating through imitation. These criticisms are relatively minor.

The actors performed adequately for a teen audience; Julia Stiles shines, and Thomas is appealing. Much of the supporting cast relies on established Black stereotypes – including tough friends, troubled mothers, and jealous rivals – which aligns with expectations. Despite this reliance on recognizable archetypes, I didn't find it overly disruptive. Fredro Starr delivered a strong performance as Malakai.

In a sign of a thaw in relations between Egypt and Israel, the two countries have signed a trade protocol with the US, allowing Egyptian goods made in partnership with Israeli firms free access to American markets.
The protocol, signed in Cairo, will establish what are called "qualified industrial zones" in Egypt. Products from these zones will enjoy duty free access to the US, provided that 35% of their components are the product of Israeli-Egyptian cooperation. The US describes this as the most important economic agreement between Egypt and Israel in two decades.
The protocol establishing the zones has been stalled for years. There has been deep sensitivity in Egypt about any form of co-operation with Israel as long as its peace process with the Palestinians remains blocked. But in recent weeks an unusual warmth has crept into relations between the two countries. Both exchanged prisoners earlier this month, with Egypt handing back an Israeli who has served eight years in prison after being convicted for spying.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has described Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon as the best chance for the Palestinians to achieve peace. The government in Cairo now believes Mr Sharon is moving towards the centre and away from the positions of right wing groups. It also believes the US, pressed by Europe, is now more willing to engage seriously in the search for a settlement. But there are also pressing economic reasons for Egypt's decision to enter into the trade agreement. It will give a huge boost to Egyptian textile exports, which are about to suffer a drop after new regulations come into force in the US at the beginning of the year.

Born in North Shields, Northumberland on March 14, 1909, Horace Cedric Lee was an English cricketer who batted right-handed and bowled fast-medium pace. He began his career with Northumberland in the 1929 Minor Counties Championship, appearing in 67 matches before World War II. His first first-class game came in 1935 as part of a Minor Counties team versus Oxford University, where the Minor Counties scored 251 and 294, with Lee contributing 45 runs before being bowled by Whitehouse. Despite Oxford’s strong start, the match ended in a draw. A subsequent first-class outing occurred in 1936 against Ireland, resulting in a Minor Counties defeat after they had scored only 69 and 133, with Lee dismissed once again by James Graham for one run. After the war, he played another Minor Counties Championship match against Staffordshire.

Ingredients:

1 cup whole wheat flour

1 cup ricotta cheese

1 egg

1/4 teaspoon salt

1 tablespoon olive oil

1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese

Directions:

1. In a medium bowl, combine flour, ricotta, egg, and salt. Mix well.

2. On a lightly floured surface, roll dough into a 1-inch-thick rope. Cut rope into 1-inch pieces.

3. In a large pot of boiling water, add gnocchi. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, or until they float to the top.

4. In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add cooked gnocchi. Toss to coat.

A Spanish football hooligan who stabbed a police officer to the death on the Spanish town of Fuengirola in April has admitted to detectives that he killed and had his victim decapitated.

Rios Romero Gomez, who was known as "Gomez the Jackal", was on Wednesday accused of killing 24-year-old Elisabeth Lopez at Fuengirola, and then "having her head shaved and put into a suitcase in a nearby garden", according to a statement released by prosecutors.

The 31-year-old spent three months in a psychiatric hospital and has since been released and is seeking legal action.

In the four-minute video Gomez admitted to throwing a stone to the officer's face that killed Lopez on April 23 in an incident that resulted in her death. He also said he "honestly believed".

In the video, when asked if he had killed Lopez Lopez answered: "Yes."

Lopez had fallen asleep on a sofa, then woke up, screaming and falling headfirst onto the carpet. Gomez allegedly rushed over and stabbed her several times.

After he was arrested he said she had been a "pig" who stole from others. He claimed he had been trying to clean a sink when the knife got stuck in a piece of metal on the floor.

After the stabbing, he went to the garden where he was joined by three other Fuengirola men. There they threw Lopez' head into the garden and sawed a plastic bag back together – only for Gomez to see them doing the same to a plastic bag containing a dead monkey, and to conclude that he should have used it to wash his hands before going out.

He then asked the four men if he could borrow a lighter from one of those who had been using it. The five made their way out of Fuengirola after a few minutes, before police found their red Ferrari parked up outside a hotel.

> Abstract: We study magnetic reconnection in two dimensions using resistive MHD simulations with an imposed guide field and periodic boundary conditions. In this configuration, we find that large scale effective potentials can be generated during the early stages of reconnection which reduce ion heating significantly compared to the case without such potentials. These potentials are created due to the presence of a strong guide field and are found to have a characteristic length scale comparable to the system size. This effect is not observed when the guide field is weak or absent. Our results suggest that the generation of these potentials may play an important role in reducing ion heating during magnetic reconnection in astrophysical systems where there is a significant guide field present.

2 sticks (1 cup) unsalted butter, softened
1 large egg, separated
1 teaspoon almond extract
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup sliced almonds (about 1 1/2 oz)
Pulse almond paste in a food processor until broken up into small bits, then add salt and 1/4 cup sugar and continue to pulse until finely ground, about 1 minute. Put oven rack in middle position and preheat oven to 350°F. Butter a 9-inch square baking pan, then line with foil, leaving a 2-inch overhang on 2 opposite sides, and butter foil. Beat together butter and remaining 1/2 cup sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer at medium-high speed until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes in a stand mixer (preferably fitted with a paddle attachment) or 6 minutes with a handheld. Add almond mixture, egg yolk, and almond extract and beat until combined well, about 2 minutes. Reduce speed to low, then add flour and mix until combined. Spread batter evenly in pan with an offset spatula. Lightly beat egg white in a small bowl, then brush some of it over batter and sprinkle evenly with almonds. Bake until top is golden, 35 to 40 minutes. Cool completely in pan on a rack, about 1 hour. Transfer with foil to a cutting board, then discard foil. Ingredients:

* 1 head of garlic (about 12 cloves), cut in half
* Olive oil for drizzling
* 1 can chickpeas, drained
* 60ml cold water, plus a 30ml for a looser consistency
* 1 small lemon, juiced then ½ zested
* 3 tbsp tahini
* 1¼ tsp salt, plus a pinch
* ¼ tsp black pepper
* 2 tbsp pastrami, very finely chopped

Method:

* Preheat oven to 210°C/190°C fan/gas 6½.
* Squeeze the garlic cloves from their skins into a bowl.
* Pick out any stray skins, add 4 tbsp olive oil, then blitz with a stick blender until as smooth as possible.
* Tip the chickpeas into the bowl of a food processor with the garlic oil, water, lemon juice and zest, tahini, salt and pepper.
* Process until smooth, then pour into a bowl and stir in the pastrami.
* Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and the reserved lemon zest, then serve with crudités and toasted pitta.

Recent progress in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has greatly advanced medical image segmentation, a crucial step for many clinical applications. Yet, current methods struggle to effectively model long-range relationships and often create complex, deeply nested networks that sacrifice fine-grained detail. To overcome these limitations, a more efficient approach is needed that balances understanding broader contextual information with retaining local nuances. This paper introduces TransFuse, a new parallel architecture integrating Transformers and CNNs to tackle this problem. By combining these approaches in parallel, TransFuse captures both global dependencies and detailed spatial information within a streamlined network. Furthermore, a BiFusion module is employed to seamlessly merge features from the Transformer and CNN branches. Evaluation across various 2D and 3D medical datasets – including polyp, skin lesion, hip, and prostate segmentation – shows that TransFuse surpasses existing state-of-the-art performance with reduced parameters and faster processing times.

Born in Yorkshire, England in 1862, Constance Eaton Hamilton (1862–1945) was a Canadian government official and dedicated advocate. Initially active in Winnipeg’s efforts to aid refugees and champion women’s rights, she later relocated to Toronto where she further supported movements like women’s suffrage, eventually leading the Equal Franchise League of Toronto. Elected to Toronto City Council for one year in 1920, she broke barriers as the first female council member in Ontario – the first at either the municipal, provincial, or federal level. Following two terms, she stepped down to focus on immigrant resettlement and refugee advocacy alongside broader equality campaigns. In recognition of her contributions, the Toronto city council created the Constance E. Hamilton Award on the Status of Women in 1979. Her upbringing included private tutoring and studies, fluency in German, musical training at the Conservatory of Music in Leipzig, and periods working as a farmer. With her family, she emigrated to Canada in 1887, settling in Vancouver before marrying Lauchlan Hamilton in 1888.

Henry Loeb III, born December 9, 1920, and died September 8, 1992, was a Democratic Party politician who served as mayor of Memphis, Tennessee, twice during the 1960s—from 1960 to 1963 and again from 1968 to 1971. He became well-known nationally due to his stance against the 1968 strike by city sanitation workers. Known as a segregationist, Loeb actively resisted civil rights for Black citizens and upheld principles of white supremacy, mirroring the policies of previous Memphis mayor E. H. Crump. His family history included German Jewish grandparents who immigrated to Memphis in the 1860s, a Jewish father, and an Irish Catholic mother. Loeb himself received education at Phillips Academy and Brown University before serving as a naval lieutenant in World War II. Post-war, he cultivated support among the white middle class by emphasizing his wartime experience and opposing communist ideology.

Security analysis through information flow examines how secrets unintentionally reveal themselves via connections between hidden data and observable outputs. Because complete elimination of these correlations is often impossible, quantifying the leakage is crucial. Information theory provides common methods for measuring this leakage, and the recently developed $g$-leakage framework has proven particularly effective. However, calculating $g$-leakage can become demanding for complex systems. This work investigates scenarios where the system’s communication channel can be broken down into smaller, more manageable channels – frequently occurring when observables include several parts. Our key result is establishing upper limits on the multiplicative $g$-leakage of the entire system based on the $g$-leakages of its individual components. Furthermore, we explore specific instances like min-entropy leakage and parallel channels, building upon existing research and providing a structured approach. We validate our technique by illustrating its utility and assessing the accuracy of our derived bounds through concrete examples.

Here’s a recipe for Dipping Sauce, Coleslaw, and Coconut Shrimp Rolls:

**Dipping Sauce:** Combine 5 ounces of apricot jam, 1/4 cup of crushed pineapple, 1 teaspoon of apple cider vinegar, and 1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes in a bowl.

**Coleslaw:** Blend 1/4 cup of water, 1/4 cup of olive oil, 1/2 cup chopped scallions, 1/2 cup cilantro, one minced garlic clove, a pinch of salt, and 2 tablespoons of lime juice in a food processor until smooth. Stir in 1/2 cup of sour cream. Add 1 cup of shredded green cabbage and 1 1/2 cups of shredded purple cabbage; drizzle with the olive oil mixture and toss gently.

**Coconut Shrimp:** Whisk together 3 ounces of beer, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup of milk, 1 cup of flour, 1/4 teaspoon of baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Dip peeled and deveined shrimp into the batter, then coat thoroughly with 5 ounces of coconut flakes. Deep-fry the coated shrimp in hot oil until the coconut flakes are golden brown. Drain on a wire rack set over a sheet pan to remove excess oil. Allow to cool.

**Assembly:** Moisten rice paper sheets slightly. Spoon a generous amount of coleslaw onto the center of each sheet, leaving about an inch uncovered at the edges. Roll tightly, folding the edges inward to enclose the slaw. Once the shrimp has cooled and drained, arrange two shrimp atop the rolled coleslaw and continue wrapping to seal. Slice each roll in half and serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce.

To create this recipe, you’ll need 220 grams of strong bread flour, 30 grams of plain flour, 25 grams of sugar, 3 grams of dry yeast, 4 grams of salt, 7 grams of honey, 160 grams of milk, 55 grams of chopped, drained yomogi (Japanese mugwort), 20 grams of unsalted butter, and 240 grams of prepared azuki bean paste. Combine all the bread ingredients, including the yomogi, in a bread machine and initiate the “bread dough” cycle. After five minutes, add the butter. Gently deflate the dough, divide it into six equal parts, and allow each portion to rest for fifteen minutes under a damp cloth. On a lightly floured surface, roll each dough ball into a 11 cm circle, making the center slightly thicker. Place an azuki bean paste ball in the center and carefully flatten. Using a technique similar to gyoza making, pinch and pleat the dough around the filling, ensuring a tight seal. Continue pinching and folding to create a circular shape over the filling. Position the finished dough circles on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Let them rise until doubled in size. Preheat the oven to 210°C and then reduce it to 190°C. Edge Intersection Graphs of Paths within trees (EPT) and grids (EPG) have received considerable attention. Lately, we presented Edge-Intersecting and Non-Splitting Paths in a Tree (ENPT) and in a Grid (ENPG). Our research revealed that ENPG possesses an endless series of subclasses defined by limiting path bends. Building upon this discovery, we concentrate here specifically on “one bend” ENPG graphs. We demonstrate that these one-bend ENPG graphs are a subset of two-bend ENPG graphs. Furthermore, we establish that trees and cycles qualify as one-bend ENPG graphs, and detail the characteristics of split and co-bipartite graphs within this category. We verify that determining if a one-bend ENPG graph is a split graph is NP-complete, even when considering a narrow group of split graphs. Finally, we offer a linear-time algorithm to identify one-bend ENPG co-bipartite graphs.

Erik's journey truly begins when he is sent on a treacherous mission across the North Sea to protect a neighbouring village from an upcoming ambush. During this mission, Erick uncovers his destiny - a prophesy that he will be a legendary Viking Chief who will unite rival Norse tribes. He also meets Astrid, a fierce and dedicated shield maiden, who inspires and assists him throughout his journey. 

Erik experiences numerous trials and tribulations as he navigates through brutal battles, political upheavals, and personal betrayals. As Erik continues to grow and develop, he demonstrates the true essence of a Viking warrior with his physical strength, strategic intelligence, and unyielding courage.

Aside from the clash of swords, Erik and Ragnor fight a battle of ideologies, with Erik championing unity and understanding, while Ragnor is adamant in maintaining the status quo. The novel concludes on a hopeful note as Erik, emerging victorious, starts his journey towards fulfilling the prophecy, leading his tribe with wisdom, and striving towards a united Norse world. 

"Viking Warrior" traverses the stark landscapes of ancient Scandinavia while exploring themes of bravery, destiny, and the unquenchable thirst for honour and freedom. Erik emerges as an embodiment of a true Viking, not just as a ruthless warrior, but also as a wise and eminently fair leader.

Marthinus Theunis “Tjol” Lategan (born September 29, 1925; died March 8, 2015) was a South African rugby union center renowned for his partnership with Ryk van Schoor. He played for both the University of Stellenbosch and Western Province clubs. Representing South Africa eleven times from 1949 to 1953, he initially debuted against the visiting New Zealand All Blacks in 1949 and subsequently participated in the celebrated 1951-52 tour of Great Britain, Ireland, and France—a campaign considered among the most successful in South African rugby history, boasting 30 wins out of 31 matches, including all five international games. Born in Stellenbosch and educated through Stellenbosch Boys’ High School and Stellenbosch University (where he studied accountancy), Lategan was affectionately called “Tjol.” After establishing a career as an accountant, becoming a partner in a prominent firm based in East London and retiring in 1991, he married twice. His first wife passed away in 1970, and he later married Trudie, residing together in a retirement facility in Somerset West. China’s economic expansion surged to 9.5% in 2004, exceeding forecasts and surpassing the 9.1% growth of 2003. This rapid increase prompted authorities to consider tightening investment and lending controls to moderate the pace of expansion, as excessive consumption of resources could negatively impact global markets. While industrial growth decelerated to 11.5% (down from 17% the prior year), service sector contributions fueled much of the growth. However, consumer price increases accelerated to 2.4%, raising concerns about potential inflation due to a significant jump in producer prices of 7.1%. Investment in fixed assets remained robust at 21.3%, though lower than the peak reached in early 2004. Consequently, China raised interest rates by 0.27 percentage points to 5.8% in October 2004 – their first increase in nearly a decade. Economists maintain a positive outlook, predicting continued strength into 2005. Driven by both domestic demand and substantial export gains—up 35% over the past year—China’s economy continues to gain momentum, partly supported by the relatively low value of the yuan against the U.S. dollar. Despite pressure to allow greater exchange rate flexibility, officials remain committed to maintaining the current peg, citing the need for careful planning and execution.

Within a k-linear triangulated category (with k as a field), we demonstrate that the presence of Auslander-Reiten triangles guarantees that objects are uniquely identified, modulo shifts, based on the dimensions of their homomorphisms. Typically, these objects are distinguishable using this data, a result previously obtained by Jensen, Su, and Zimmermann under related assumptions. Our method involves examining bilinear forms on Grothendieck groups resembling the Green ring of a finite group. Focusing on the category of perfect complexes associated with a self-injective algebra, where the Auslander-Reiten quiver possesses a defined structure, we characterize various types of perfect complexes – including those of lengths 1, 2, and 3, rigid complexes, and truncated projective resolutions – within the quiver’s components containing projective modules. We establish connections between complex homology at distinct quiver positions, leading to the conclusion that self-injective algebras with a radical length of at least 3 invariably possess indecomposable perfect complexes exhibiting arbitrarily high homology degrees. Furthermore, we observe that homology stabilizes away from the edges of the quiver. When the algebra is symmetric, one particular form developed earlier turns out to be Hermitian, enabling computation of its values utilizing information restricted to objects near the quiver's boundary.

The graph Laplacian is frequently used across various fields like data science, machine learning, and image processing. Its associated matrix often has intricate properties and can be very full, leading to challenging calculations, especially when performing matrix-vector products. Often, researchers need to compute many of its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, but conventional techniques fail for graphs with a large number of nodes. Our work introduces a fast summation technique utilizing the nonequispaced Fast Fourier Transform (NFFT) to efficiently calculate these dense matrix-vector products without needing to construct the entire matrix. The NFFT's adaptability lets us integrate this acceleration into algorithms like Lanczos eigenvalue routines and iterative linear solvers, and also supports diverse kernel functions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through experiments involving tasks ranging from image segmentation to graph-based partial differential equation learning. Specifically, we benchmark it against the Nyström method, and explore a modified, combined version incorporating the NFFT.

Quantitative image analysis often depends on accurate classification of
pixels through a segmentation process. However, imaging artifacts such as the
partial volume effect and sensor noise complicate the classification process.
These effects increase the pixel intensity variance of each constituent class,
causing intensities from one class to overlap with another. This increased
variance makes threshold based segmentation methods insufficient due to
ambiguous overlap regions in the pixel intensity distributions. The class
ambiguity becomes even more complex for systems with more than two
constituents, such as unsaturated moist granular media. In this paper, we
propose an image processing workflow that improves segmentation accuracy for
multiphase systems. First, the ambiguous transition regions between classes are
identified and removed, which allows for global thresholding of single-class
regions. Then the transition regions are classified using a distance function,
and finally both segmentations are combined into one classified image. This
workflow includes three methodologies for identifying transition pixels and we
demonstrate on a variety of synthetic images that these approaches are able to
accurately separate the ambiguous transition pixels from the single-class
regions. For situations with typical amounts of image noise, misclassification
errors and area differences calculated between each class of the synthetic
images and the resultant segmented images range from 0.69-1.48% and 0.01-0.74%,
respectively, showing the segmentation accuracy of this approach. We
demonstrate that we are able to accurately segment x-ray microtomography images
of moist granular media using these computationally efficient methodologies.

For this recipe, start with one pound of ziti or whole wheat penne. Use eight ounces of fresh mozzarella, cubed. Combine one cup of freshly chopped basil, one tablespoon of cold-pressed organic extra-virgin olive oil, four chopped organic garlic cloves, fourteen ounces of diced organic tomatoes, eight ounces of organic tomato paste, one cup of water, two tablespoons of dried organic oregano, two tablespoons of dried organic basil, salt, and pepper in a saucepan. Heat the oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, adding the garlic and stirring until lightly browned—avoid burning it. Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, water, herbs, salt, and pepper, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 1-2 hours, stirring occasionally.

Simultaneously, cook one half-teaspoon of sea salt in a large pot of boiling water; this flavors the pasta. Add one pound of brown rice pasta (or another whole grain variety) along with a tablespoon of olive oil to prevent sticking. Cook for 7-10 minutes until al dente, draining and adding to the sauce. In the last few minutes of cooking the pasta, gently fold in the cubed mozzarella cheese until melted, being careful not to overcook it. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil and Parmesan cheese – enjoy!

Simone Wilkie is an Australian-British actress and writer. She was born in 1984 in Manchester, England, by French and Australian parents. After a degree in Classical Civilizations, she studied on the Postgraduate Course in Screenwriting at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School.

Wilkie has also written several screenplays. Her credits include the biographical drama film The Moodys (2016), the sci-fi comedy The Infiltrer (2017), and the drama film The Light Years.

In addition to her acting and writing, Wilkie is an avid reader and has worked as a book reviewer for the Melbourne Age. She is also a skilled writer of non-fiction, having penned several articles on the subject of classical music for The Quietus.

Overall, Simone Wilkie has established herself as a talented and versatile performer, who has made a significant contribution to the Australian entertainment industry.

Written in 1492 from Domrémy, France, the foreword is penned by the fictional Sieur Louis de Conte to his relatives, detailing his connection to Joan d'Arc—initially as a childhood companion, then as her page and secretary. He reflects, "I remained with her throughout her entire journey." The narrative commences with de Conte’s birth on January 6th, 1410, in Neufchâteau, France, describing his early life marked by hardship due to English and Burgundian military pressure endured for over seventy-five years. Following the loss of his family to a Burgundian attack in 1415, he was placed with the parish priest in Domrémy, where he encountered young Joan. Even during her youth, de Conte recounts numerous instances demonstrating Joan’s wisdom and courage, such as protecting vulnerable children, persuading villagers to aid a traveler, and peacefully subduing a threatening individual. By Chapter VI, the story notes a shift in Joan’s demeanor around her fourteenth birthday, when she became noticeably serious. A subsequent chapter reveals the cause of this transformation: on May 15th, 1428, she discloses visions of saints and angels, declaring her divine mission to command armies, reclaim France, and crown the Dauphin as king. Initially reluctant, Joan admits, "I am but a child, inexperienced – unaware of much."

Cold War Steve is the nom de plume of Christopher Spencer, a British collage artist and satirist. He is the creator of the Twitter feed @Coldwar_Steve. His work typically depicts a grim, dystopian location in England populated by British media figures, celebrities, and politicians, usually with EastEnders actor Steve McFadden (in character as Phil Mitchell) looking on in disgust. His work has been described as having "captured the mood of Brexit Britain" and has been likened to that of earlier British political satirists Hogarth and Gillray. As of September 2021, his Twitter account has over 345,000 followers. Early life
Spencer was born in Birmingham in 1975. He went to art college at Nuneaton in Warwickshire where his fellow students included film director Gareth Edwards.  He then failed to get into three different universities and subsequently spent the next twenty years working a series of mundane jobs in factories and the public sector.  Recovering after an attempted suicide, Spencer concentrated on his art creating the montages on his phone, often while travelling to work on the bus.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of computer-aided knee joint Magnetic Resonance Image (MRI) segmentation techniques. The study focuses on the importance of accurate knee joint segmentation in diagnosing and treating knee-related ailments. It explores various methodologies, including thresholding, region-growing, clustering, active contour models, and machine learning approaches. The paper also discusses the challenges faced in knee joint segmentation, such as the complexity of knee joint anatomy, the variability in MR image quality, and the lack of standard evaluation metrics. The survey aims to provide a reference point for researchers and practitioners in the field, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of existing methods and suggesting potential areas for future research.

"Story of O" is an intriguing novel that revolves around the life of a young Parisianne named 'O', who lives a relatively normal life by day but indulges in the world of BDSM and submission at night. Introduced to this alternative lifestyle by her boyfriend René, O embarks on a journey of self-discovery as she learns to navigate and derive pleasure from the pain in a consensual BDSM relationship that eventually leads to her deep transformation.

As the story unfolds, O's experiences become more extreme as she is taken by René to Roissy, a chateau where women are trained in submission through methods ranging from bedroom games, sensory deprivation to physical torment. They are treated as objects for pleasure, with their own desires dismissed or considered secondary. 

The narrative showcases a stark contrast between the sophisticated life O leads as a respected photographer in French society and her enslaved existence in the chateau. As her engagement in submission intensifies, O begins to question her identity and societal norms, getting used to the complexity of her dual life.

The climax sees O fully submitting not only to her master René but also to Sir Stephen, a more dominant figure who places stricter demands on her. O's unflinching surrender to her own desires and choice to devalue societal standards encapsulates the core essence of the novel.

"Story of O" is a gripping exploration of polarizing themes such as power dynamics, human eroticism, sexuality, and depravity. The novel ends with a profound question about the extremities one can go to for love and desire, leaving readers reflecting on the subjective boundary line separating passion and obsession.

Jung considers the Book of Job a landmark development in the "divine drama", for the first time contemplating criticism of God (Gotteskritik). Jung described the book as "pure poison", referring to the controversial nature of the book (Storr, 1973). He did, however, feel an urge to write the book. The basic thesis of the book is that as well as having a good side, God also has a fourth side - the evil face of God. This view is inevitably controversial, but Jung claimed it is backed up by references to the Hebrew Bible. The book, has however, been criticised. For example, it assumes that the John who wrote the fourth Gospel was the same John who wrote The Book of Revelation - which most Bible scholars today dispute. Jung saw this evil side of God as the missing fourth element of the Trinity, which he believed should be supplanted by a Quaternity. However, he also discusses in the book whether the true missing fourth element is the feminine side of God. Indeed, he saw the dogmatic definition of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary by Pope Pius XII in 1950 as being the most significant religious event since the Reformation.

Ingredients:

* 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
* 1/2 cup unsalted butter, chilled and cut into small pieces
* 1/4 cup granulated sugar
* 2 tablespoons salt
* 1/4 cup sour cherry jam
* 1/4 cup sour cream
* 1 egg, beaten
* 1/2 cup chopped fresh sour cherries
* 1/2 cup chopped pecans (optional)
* 1/4 cup confectioners' sugar

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, butter, sugar, and salt. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
2. In a small bowl, mix together the sour cherry jam and sour cream until smooth.
3. Add the egg and mix until well combined.
4. Add the cherry mixture to the flour mixture and mix until a dough forms.
5. Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and roll out to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
6. Cut the dough into 8 equal triangles.
7. Place a spoonful of the sour cherry jam in the center of each triangle.
8. Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle shape, pressing the edges to seal.
9. Brush the tops of the rugelach with a little bit of milk and sprinkle with chopped pecans, if using.
10. Place the rugelach on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
11. Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
12. Allow the rugelach to cool on a wire rack.

Chelsea have sacked Adrian Mutu after he failed a drugs test.
The 25-year-old tested positive for a banned substance - which he later denied was cocaine - in October. Chelsea have decided to write off a possible transfer fee for Mutu, a £15.8m signing from Parma last season, who may face a two-year suspension. A statement from Chelsea explaining the decision read:"We want to make clear that Chelsea has a zero tolerance policy towards drugs." Mutu scored six goals in his first five games after arriving at Stamford Bridge but his form went into decline and he was frozen out by coach Jose Mourinho. Chelsea's statement added: "This applies to both performance-enhancing drugs or so-called 'recreational' drugs. They have no place at our club or in sport. "In coming to a decision on this case, Chelsea believed the club's social responsibility to its fans, players, employees and other stakeholders in football regarding drugs was more important than the major financial considerations to the company. "Any player who takes drugs breaches his contract with the club as well as Football Association rules. "The club totally supports the FA in strong action on all drugs cases." Fifa's disciplinary code stipulates that a first doping offence should be followed by a six-month ban. And the sport's world governing body has re-iterated their stance over Mutu's failed drugs test, maintaining it is a matter for the domestic sporting authorities. "Fifa is not in a position to make any comment on the matter until the English FA have informed us of their disciplinary decision and the relevant information associated with it," said a Fifa spokesman. Chelsea's move won backing from drug-testing expert Michelle Verroken. Verroken, a former director of drug-free sport for UK Sport, insists the Blues were right to sack Mutu and have enhanced their reputation by doing so. "Chelsea are saying quite clearly to the rest of their players and their fans that this is a situation they are not prepared to tolerate. "It was a very difficult decision for them and an expensive decision for them but the terms of his contract were breached and it was the only decision they could make. "It is a very clear stance by Chelsea and it has given a strong boost to the reputation of the club." It emerged that Mutu had failed a drugs test on October 18 and, although it was initially reported that the banned substance in question was cocaine. The Romanian international later suggested it was a substance designed to enhance sexual performance. The Football Association has yet to act on Mutu's failed drugs test and refuses to discuss his case.

White matter hyperintensities (WMH) frequently occur in older adults and are linked to neurological conditions. The U-net, a prevalent convolutional neural network for medical image segmentation, has recently shown promise in WMH detection. Typically, U-net models are initialized with random weights, which can lead them to converge to suboptimal solutions. Our research demonstrates that combining and thresholding the segmentations produced by multiple U-nets initiated with varied random seeds significantly enhances WMH segmentation precision.  Therefore, we developed a novel post-processing method focusing on optimized averaging and thresholding strategies. Specifically, we convert the scores from three U-nets into binary masks using thresholds and subsequently average these masks to generate the final WMH segmentation. Quantitative metrics (Dice coefficient) and visual assessments confirm the effectiveness of our approach. Importantly, this post-processing technique is model-agnostic and adaptable to various deep learning architectures, particularly those utilizing random initialization without prior training.

The Conservatives' campaign director has denied a report claiming he warned Michael Howard the party could not win the next general election.

But Mr Crosby said in a statement: "I have never had any such conversation... and I do not hold that view." Mr Howard later added there was not "one iota" of truth in the report.
