Constance Eaton Hamilton (1862–1945) was a British-Canadian government official and activist. After activism supporting refugees and women in Winnipeg, she moved to Toronto and continued to support causes such as women's suffrage, becoming president of the Equal Franchise League of Toronto. She was elected for a one-year term on the  Toronto City Council in the 1920 elections, becoming the first female member of Toronto City Council and the first woman in Ontario to hold elected office at either the federal, provincial, or municipal level. After two terms  she resigned to continue her work campaigning for immigrant settlement and refugee issues, and for equal rights. In 1979, the Toronto city council established the Constance E. Hamilton Award on the Status of Women. Early life and education
She was born in Yorkshire, England in 1862 to Dr George Fowler Bodington (1829-1902) and Caroline Mary Eaton (1825-1873). Early she studied with private tutors. Fluent in German, she attended the Conservatory of Music in Leipzig, Germany and became a skilled pianist. She also worked as a part-time farmer for parts of her early life.  Hamilton immigrated to Canada with her family in 1887 and settled in Vancouver. The following year she met and married Lauchlan Hamilton, an older businessman.

WIS, a virtual and VHF digital channel 10 station affiliated with NBC and CW, serves Columbia, South Carolina. Owned by Gray Television, its headquarters are situated on Bull and Gervais Streets in downtown Columbia, while its broadcast transmitter resides on Rush Road, southwest of I-20 near Lugoff. Through Charter Spectrum, viewers can access WIS in standard and high definition on channel 3. Established on November 7, 1953, the station’s inaugural broadcast featured a football match between South Carolina and North Carolina. Initially operated by the Broadcasting Company of the South – then a division of Liberty Life Insurance – WIS was founded by Charles Batson, who served as president and general manager until 1983. It debuted as the fourth television station in South Carolina and the third in the Columbia area, launching only four months after WCOS-TV (channel 25), which later shut down, and two months after WNOK-TV (channel 67, now WLTX on channel 19), relocating in 1961. WIS holds the distinction of being among the longest-running television stations in the state, trailing only WCSC-TV in Charleston and the combined legacy of WNOK/WLTX.

This research focuses on analyzing the stability of iterated polynomials and linear transformations that maintain strong q-log-convexity. We establish conditions for the linear transformation $y_n(q) = \sum_{k=0}^nT_{n,k}x_k(q)$ to uphold this property. Specifically, we demonstrate that several transformations—including various Stirling, Jacobi-Stirling, Legendre-Stirling, and central factorial forms—preserve both strong q-log-convexity and log-convexity in a consistent way. These findings validate Lin and Zeng’s conjecture, expand upon previous work by Chen *et al.* and Zhu concerning strong q-log-convexity, and build on Liu and Wang's results regarding transformations preserving log-convexity. The relationship between polynomial stability and q-log-convexity is explored; using zero interlacing, we offer two criteria for the stability of iterated Sturm sequences and the q-log-convexity of polynomials. This leads to the determination of the stability of iterated Eulerian polynomials of types A and B, along with their q-analogues. Furthermore, we prove that generating functions representing alternating A and B runs, longest alternating subsequences, and up-down runs of permutations constitute q-log-convex sequences.

“The Remains of the Day” recounts the life of Stevens, an English butler, told entirely through his own narration, as he reflects on his unwavering devotion to Lord Darlington – whose past is gradually explored through flashbacks. The narrative starts when Stevens receives a letter from his former associate, Miss Kenton, suggesting a troubled marriage, prompting him to consider reconnecting with her while seeking potential work. His new boss, Mr. Farraday, suggests a “motoring trip” for Stevens’ relaxation, allowing him to contemplate his steadfast commitment to Darlington, the concept of “dignity,” and memories of his deceased father. Gradually, Stevens confronts the unspoken emotions between himself and Miss Kenton, as evidence of their mutual attraction surfaces after many years of professional restraint. They consistently maintained a courteous friendship bordering on romantic feelings, though neither ever acted upon them. Later revealed to be married for over two decades as Mrs. Benn, Miss Kenton admits to occasional wistful thoughts about a life with Stevens, yet embraces her current family. Stevens regrets missed chances with both Miss Kenton and Lord Darlington, ultimately finding solace in his continued service with Mr. Farraday at the novel’s conclusion.

Continuing into 2005, China’s strategy to manage economic slowdown through tightened lending policies will persist, according to reports. These measures were initially implemented to prevent excessive growth from triggering high inflation and stressing the already vulnerable banking sector. Despite maintaining a robust 9.1% annual growth rate – fueled by substantial corporate investment exceeding 25% – and a manufacturing boom driving global energy demand, the government maintains it won’t experience a sharp economic downturn. Its targeted growth of 7% appears significantly higher, and the undervalued yuan (pegged at approximately 8.28 to the dollar) contributes to competitive exports. While resisting calls to adjust the currency’s value, evidence suggests the credit controls are beginning to yield results, as industrial output decreased to 15.7% in October compared to 23% in February, and inflation eased to 4.3%, even as retail sales remain strong.

If elected, the Conservative Party intends to decrease the number of Members of Parliament by approximately one-fifth, according to party leader Michael Howard. This proposal is included in their forthcoming “smaller government bill,” which also involves cutting down the number of government special advisors. Furthermore, a referendum in Wales will determine whether the Welsh Assembly is abolished. These reforms would occur within five years of a Conservative victory in a general election. The exact reduction in MPs would be contingent upon the outcome of the Welsh vote, likely resulting in a loss of roughly 120 seats from the current 659. Maintaining the Welsh Assembly would lead to fewer MP losses.  Howard emphasized that, considering Labour’s plans to eliminate over 80,000 civil servants and the Tories’ intention to remove nearly 100,000, a similar reduction in parliamentary numbers is warranted. He stated, “This aims to lessen unnecessary and expensive governmental involvement by shrinking the State.” Howard added that the plan addresses the disproportionate representation of Scottish and Welsh MPs compared to those from England, where constituencies average 70,000 residents, contrasted with figures for Wales (59,000) and Northern Ireland (66,000). If the Welsh Assembly is dismantled, the number of Welsh MPs would align with a fairer representation across the UK. Howard suggests swift implementation, potentially even before the subsequent election.

Our research introduces a new technique for diagnosing heart conditions by analyzing cardiac images. This method extracts key visual details about the heart’s shape and movement using a unique process involving 2D+t cine MRI sequences. We created a semi-supervised learning system that effectively utilizes both extensive unlabeled images and limited expert-labeled segmentations to derive pixel-wise motion information between consecutive frames. By integrating these motion maps with manual cardiac segmentations, we create localized motion data representing the movement of the heart muscle and chambers.  This generates time series data reflecting changes in myocardial radius and thickness, providing robust and understandable indicators of abnormal cardiac motion.  Combining these motion features with shape attributes, we build a straightforward and adaptable model capable of classifying different heart diseases – utilizing just nine input parameters. The model demonstrated high accuracy—95% on the training dataset and 94% on the test dataset—matching current leading methods. Comparisons against alternative approaches highlight the model's strengths.

I'm 25 years old. I have no children. So why am I praising a 'kid's movie' which nobody saw? Because I have never seen a film pack the emotional wallop 'The Iron Giant' provided.

The film's plot is similar to 'E.T.' - a young boy meets an alien robot from outer space, who is stranded on earth, and runs afoul of paranoid government agents. Not to knock the Spielberg film, but what makes 'The Iron Giant' the better film is that the young boy is the teacher. It is he who has to teach the Giant about the beauty of life, the difference between good and evil, and choices we have to make. The Iron Giant, it turns out, is a weapon, who has to struggle against his own nature. The film has an obvious (and timely) gun control message, but its real message is about the choice we make when dealing with other people. We can use our powers for good or lash out at everyone around us.

I dare not give away the climax. All I will say is that it features a sacrifice absolutely breaktaking and emotionally shattering (albeit somewhat blunted by the ending). The animation is gorgeous, Michael Kamen's score is perfect, and the film beautifully evokes the 1950s.

Sadly, poor marketing kept audiences away in droves. All I can say is, to heck with the box office gross. Despite Warner's appearant desire to pretend the film never existed, the word is getting around about what a magical film this is, and I have no doubt it will join 'It's a Wonderful Life' as a film which bombed in theatres but became a classic over the years. See it now, so you can say you discovered it before everyone else did.

Over the past few years it has been demonstrated that "coarse timesteppers"
establish a link between traditional numerical analysis and microscopic/
stochastic simulation. The underlying assumption of the associated
lift-run-restrict-estimate procedure is that macroscopic models exist and close
in terms of a few governing moments of microscopically evolving distributions,
but they are unavailable in closed form. This leads to a system identification
based computational approach that sidesteps the necessity of deriving explicit
closures. Two-level codes are constructed; the outer code performs macroscopic,
continuum level numerical tasks, while the inner code estimates -through
appropriately initialized bursts of microscopic simulation- the quantities
required for continuum numerics. Such quantities include residuals, time
derivatives, and the action of coarse slow Jacobians. We demonstrate how these
coarse timesteppers can be applied to perform equation-free computations of a
kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of E. coli chemotaxis. Coarse-grained
contraction mappings, system level stability analysis as well as acceleration
of the direct simulation, are enabled through this computational multiscale
enabling technology.

The Football Association is investigating incidents involving Liverpool and Millwall following a contentious Carling Cup game on October 26th. Millwall, defeated 3-0, faces charges related to potential racist conduct exhibited by its fans, alongside reports of disruptive behavior including seat destruction and four expulsions. Injuries occurred when a disabled supporter was hurt near the field, necessitating police intervention to manage escalating tensions. While Liverpool fans suggested the unrest stemmed from taunts referencing the tragic Hillsborough disaster of 1989, Millwall’s chairman, Theo Paphitis, refuted these allegations, citing CCTV evidence indicating a clash between supporters as the initial trigger. 12 ounces flank steak, trimmed of excess fat and sinew
1 tablespoon peeled, minced fresh ginger
1 1/2 teaspoons soy sauce
1 teaspoon cornstarch
1 teaspoon peanut or vegetable oil
1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons oyster sauce
2 tablespoons Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
2 tablespoons peanut or vegetable oil
1 1/2 cups sugar snap peas (about 7 ounces), strings removed
1 cup very thinly sliced carrots (about 2 small)
4 medium scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup pickled ginger slices (about 1 ounce), coarsely chopped if large
Basic Steamed White Rice, for serving
Cut the flank steak with the grain into 2-inch-wide strips, then cut each strip against the grain into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Place the beef and the remaining ingredients in a medium bowl and stir to evenly coat the meat; set aside. Place the oyster sauce and Shaoxing wine or sherry in a small bowl and stir to combine; set aside. Heat a 14-inch flat-bottomed wok over high heat until a bead of water vaporizes when dropped in the pan. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of the oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the reserved beef in an even layer. Cook undisturbed until the beef begins to sear, about 1 minute. Then, using a metal spatula, stir-fry for 30 seconds until the beef is lightly browned but not cooked through. Transfer to a plate. Drizzle the remaining tablespoon of oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the sugar snaps and carrots. Stir-fry until just warmed through, about 1 minute. Return the beef and any accumulated juices to the wok along with the reserved oyster sauce mixture, green onions, and pickled ginger. Stir-fry until the beef is just cooked through and the pickled ginger is well distributed, about 30 to 60 seconds. Serve with steamed rice.

Phases of matter are conventionally characterized by order parameters
describing the type and degree of order in a system. For example, crystals
consist of spatially ordered arrays of atoms, an order that is lost as the
crystal melts. Like- wise in ferromagnets, the magnetic moments of the
constituent particles align only below the Curie temperature, TC. These two
examples reflect two classes of phase transitions: the melting of a crystal is
a first-order phase transition (the crystalline order vanishes abruptly) and
the onset of magnetism is a second- order phase transition (the magnetization
increases continuously from zero as the temperature falls below TC). Such
magnetism is robust in systems with localized magnetic particles, and yet rare
in model itinerant systems where the particles are free to move about. Here for
the first time, we explore the itinerant magnetic phases present in a spin-1
spin-orbit coupled atomic Bose gas; in this system, itinerant ferromagnetic
order is stabilized by the spin-orbit coupling, vanishing in its absence. We
first located a second-order phase transition that continuously stiffens until,
at a tricritical point, it transforms into a first- order transition (with
observed width as small as h x 4 Hz). We then studied the long-lived metastable
states associated with the first-order transition. These measurements are all
in agreement with theory.

Within his foul mind, slime and swamp reside,
Illuminated by slanted glances, flickering with gloom!
His form, a rat crammed within a place for solace,
Showed him the world – a sickly green stare of a trapped feline.
Existing on remnants of vanished might, on wounded grace,
On women twisted and broken, he remained, a brutal force, intending further harm.
Yet, when one bravely faced him with a metallic grip,
His defenses dulled, and he’d favor those who followed.
Who finds refuge in God’s shallow praise today?
Your riches are merely his trick to lengthen suffering.
Your strong muscles endure greater agony while yielding.
He’s created a demand for your loveliness
That no amount of payment can satisfy, even as you offer yourselves.
He knows no peace, no respite from wakefulness;
And when darkness releases the rodents, they become cautious.
We remain secure until he arrives at first light,
Having extracted something vital from unfamiliar sources,
And tomorrow, a faint, unsettling stillness will begin.
Reality isn’t bizarre, and forgotten things are quickly dismissed.
Oh, if the sun were barren, utterly gone from our lives—
But it lingers with us, like strands of our being,
And only in silence does its movement cease.
And in the dim light, burdens lighten and shift,
While lingering unease obscures the paths we’ve abandoned.
Our hands grasp at echoes of conversations fading away,
Where simple goodbyes are readily accepted....
Ah! This suffocating essence of a decaying deity!

British film director Sir Alan Parker has been made an officer in the Order of Arts and Letters, one of France's highest cultural honours.
Sir Alan received his decoration in Paris on Wednesday from French Culture Minister Renaud Donnedieu de Vabres. "You have explored the possibilities of film with an immense talent," Mr de Vabres said as he presented the award. Parker praised French films, saying: "Hollywood, which created modern cinema, uses it only as a commodity." He told the minister: "I am honoured to be thus distinguished by France, the flag carrier of cinema throughout the world." Sir Alan's films include Oscar-winning Fame plus Midnight Express and The Commitments.
A founding member of the Director's Guild of Great Britain, he is a former chairman of the UK Film Council and on the board of the British Film Institute. "Through your work and your campaigns, you have shown us how the artist occupies an essential place in our contemporary society," Mr de Vabres said. In one wild night the city fell;
Fell shrines of prayer and marts of gain
Before the fiery hurricane.
On threescore spires had sunset shone,
Where ghastly sunrise looked on none.
Men clasped each other's hands, and said
'The City of the West is dead!'
Brave hearts who fought, in slow retreat,
The fiends of fire from street to street,
Turned, powerless, to the blinding glare,
The dumb defiance of despair.
A sudden impulse thrilled each wire
That signalled round that sea of fire;
Swift words of cheer, warm heart-throbs came;
In tears of pity died the flame!
From East, from West, from South and North,
The messages of hope shot forth,
And, underneath the severing wave,
The world, full-handed, reached to save.
Fair seemed the old; but fairer still
The new, the dreary void shall fill
With dearer homes than those o'erthrown,
For love shall lay each corner-stone.
Rise, stricken city! from thee throw
The ashen sackcloth of thy woe;
And build, as to Amphion's strain,
To songs of cheer thy walls again!
How shrivelled in thy hot distress
The primal sin of selfishness!
How instant rose, to take thy part,
The angel in the human heart!
Ah! not in vain the flames that tossed
Above thy dreadful holocaust;
The Christ again has preached through thee
The Gospel of Humanity!
Then lift once more thy towers on high,
And fret with spires the western sky,
To tell that God is yet with us,
And love is still miraculous!

In biological cells and novel diagnostic devices biochemical receptors need
to be sensitive to extremely small concentration changes of signaling
molecules. The accuracy of such molecular signaling is ultimately limited by
the counting noise imposed by the thermal diffusion of molecules. Many
macromolecules and organelles transiently bind to molecular motors and are then
actively transported. We here show that a random albeit directed delivery of
signaling molecules to within a typical diffusion distance to the receptor
reduces the correlation time of the counting noise, effecting an improved
sensing precision. The conditions for this active focusing are indeed
compatible with observations in living cells. Our results are relevant for a
better understanding of molecular cellular signaling and the design of novel
diagnostic devices.

Building a connectome from electron microscopy data involves identifying neurons and mapping their synaptic connections. Because manually doing this takes a huge amount of time, researchers have focused on automating neuron segmentation to assist and ultimately supplant manual tracing. Previously, automated synapse detection received less attention compared to segmentation. This difference stems partly from the need to initially identify neuron shapes, the greater time investment required for manual tracing versus synapse annotation, and the use of neuron contact areas as a rough estimate of synaptic connections. 

Recent studies show that contact area isn’t always reliable for pinpointing synapses, and as segmentation techniques improve, synapse annotation now dominates reconstruction timelines – a trend likely to worsen. To tackle this challenge, we've created algorithms capable of automatically finding both pre-synaptic and post-synaptic neurons. Specifically, we utilize a Deep and Wide Multiscale Recursive Network to recognize pre-synaptic structures and an MLP incorporating segmented local features to find post-synaptic partners. 

Our approach is innovative due to its low training requirements, direct utilization of improved image segmentation, and provision of a comprehensive solution for polyadic synapse detection. We also present new evaluation metrics suitable for assessing our algorithm on sizable connectomes, revealing that fully automated synapse prediction can accurately represent connectivity in many cases.

- 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro
- 1/4 cup of chopped scallions
- 2 cloves of minced garlic

- 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil
- 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon of sesame oil
- 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper
- 6 egg roll wrappers
- 1 avocado
- Salt

Instructions:
1. Drain the tofu and cut it into small cubes.
2. In a pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and add the minced garlic.
3. Once the garlic is fragrant, add the chopped scallions and black pepper.
4. Add the cubed tofu to the pan and cook for about 5 minutes until it is lightly browned.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and salt to taste.
6. Pour the sauce over the tofu and stir to coat.
7. Add the chopped cilantro and stir to combine.
8. Lay out the egg roll wrappers and place a spoonful of the tofu mixture in the center of each wrapper.
9. Slice the avocado and place a few slices on top of the tofu mixture.
10. Fold the wrapper over the tofu mixture and tuck in the sides.
11. Roll the egg roll tightly and seal the end with a little water.
12. Heat a pan with vegetable oil over medium heat and add the egg rolls.
13. Cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown.
14. Serve the egg rolls with your favorite dipping sauce and enjoy!

boundary. We indicate appropriate Sobolev spaces of negative smoothness to
study the non-homogeneous Cauchy problem for an elliptic differential complex
{A_i} of first order operators. In particular, we describe traces on the
boundary of tangential part t_i (u) and normal part n_i(u) of a
(vector)-function u from the corresponding Sobolev space and give an adequate
formulation of the problem. If the Laplacians of the complex satisfy the
uniqueness condition in the small then we obtain necessary and sufficient
solvability conditions of the problem and produce formulae for its exact and
approximate solutions. For the Cauchy problem in the Lebesgue spaces L^2(D) we
construct the approximate and exact solutions to the Cauchy problem with
maximal possible regularity. Moreover, using Hilbert space methods, we
construct Carleman's formulae for a (vector-) function u from the Sobolev space
H^1(D) by its Cauchy data t_i (u) on a subset S on the boundary of the domain D
and the values of A_i u in D modulo the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Some
instructive examples for elliptic complexes of operators with constant
coefficients are considered.

This research introduces a novel Dynamic Mixture Model (DAMM) capable of adapting both its component mix and individual parts dynamically based on incoming data. To make this dessert, start by preheating your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch spring-form pan with high sides. Melt 4 ounces of bittersweet chocolate using a double boiler, stirring until smooth, then let it cool slightly for 10 minutes. In a large bowl, combine 3/4 cup sugar, 6 tablespoons (3/4 stick) of softened butter, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract, blending with an electric mixer. Incorporate the egg yolks one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each addition. Stir in the cooled melted chocolate and poppy seeds. In a separate bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form. Gently fold half of the egg whites into the chocolate mixture, then fold in the flour and the remaining egg whites. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread evenly. Bake for approximately 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the torte cool completely before releasing it from the pan by loosening the sides and removing them. Dust generously with powdered sugar, transfer to a platter, and serve chilled with whipped cream. It can be made ahead and stored covered at room temperature for up to one day.

The pacing is just right, allowing for moments of quiet reflection and character development without losing the momentum of the story. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the energy and excitement of the draft room and the city of Cleveland.

One of the standout aspects of Draft Day is its portrayal of the relationships between the characters. From Sonny's strained relationship with his wife to the bond between him and his daughter, the film explores themes of family, loyalty, and sacrifice. These relationships add emotional depth to the story and make the stakes even higher.

Overall, Draft Day is a must-see for football fans and anyone who enjoys a well-crafted drama. It's a thrilling ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

For many, many days together
The wind blew steady from the East;
For many days hot grew the weather,
About the time of our Lady's Feast.
For many days we rode together,
Yet met we neither friend nor foe;
Hotter and clearer grew the weather,
Steadily did the East wind blow.
We saw the trees in the hot, bright weather,
Clear-cut, with shadows very black,
As freely we rode on together
With helms unlaced and bridles slack.
And often, as we rode together,
We, looking down the green-bank'd stream,
Saw flowers in the sunny weather,
And saw the bubble-making bream.
And in the night lay down together,
And hung above our heads the rood,
Or watch'd night-long in the dewy weather,
The while the moon did watch the wood.
Our spears stood bright and thick together,
Straight out the banners stream'd behind,
As we gallop'd on in the sunny weather,
With faces turn'd towards the wind.
Down sank our threescore spears together,
As thick we saw the pagans ride;
His eager face in the clear fresh weather,
Shone out that last time by my side.
Up the sweep of the bridge we dash'd together,
It rock'd to the crash of the meeting spears,
Down rain'd the buds of the dear spring weather,
The elm-tree flowers fell like tears.
There, as we roll'd and writhed together,
I threw my arms above my head,
For close by my side, in the lovely weather,
I saw him reel and fall back dead.
I and the slayer met together,
He waited the death-stroke there in his place,
With thoughts of death, in the lovely weather,
Gapingly mazed at my madden'd face.
Madly I fought as we fought together;
In vain: the little Christian band
The pagans drown'd, as in stormy weather
The river drowns low-lying land.
They bound my blood-stain'd hands together,
They bound his corpse to nod by my side:
Then on we rode, in the bright March weather,
With clash of cymbals did we ride.
We ride no more, no more together;
My prison-bars are thick and strong,
I take no heed of any weather,
The sweet Saints grant I live not long.

I've had this experience before. For me it was sort of a psychological block on getting the music going in a direction that didn't fit the lyrics, so the music was locked into a certain rhythm/melody that I knew was "wrong" for the lyrics, but I couldn't break out of it... sometimes you just have to walk away for a while and come back to it later. Sometimes it means the melody/rhythm you're writing simply isn't right for the lyrics, and you have to scrap it and start over from scratch.

As others have said, it can be helpful to jam on the chords and see if anything new presents itself, or to start singing random notes or lyrics over the chords (exactly what you were doing), until something clicks.

For others, it can help to talk/sing the lyrics aloud as if you're having a conversation, and then sing/speak the tones/rhythms of your speech back into a melody.

Sometimes when I'm really stuck in this situation, I'll reduce the lyrics to just a few key words, or even a single word, and use that as the seed for the melody. I find that once I have a good melody, I can usually modify it to fit the actual lyrics, if I need to.

Delivering intense, grueling horror, the film utilizes its modest budget and occasionally uneven performances to create a genuinely unsettling experience filled with startling visuals and groundbreaking special effects. Viewers sensitive to graphic content should proceed with caution – a swift retreat is advised. 

Several factors contribute to the film’s success. Raimi’s cinematography is exceptionally skilled; his rapid, forceful camerawork establishes a deeply unnerving environment, captivatingly disturbing yet impossible to resist. His distinctive directorial style is immediately recognizable, particularly during the opening sequence where the camera alone generates palpable suspense, suggesting imminent danger around every corner. Extended shots, often lingering amidst overwhelming darkness and violence, initially seem interminable—a visceral thrill simultaneously horrifying and exhilarating. A standout scene depicts encroaching shadows relentlessly pursuing individuals, destroying anything in their path with terrifying force. This technical achievement showcases Raimi’s innovative approach, effectively amplifying the film’s impact.

are constructed, which are parametrized by the central redshift. It is shown
that as the central redshift tends to zero, the states in such a family are
well approximated by a steady state of the Vlasov-Poisson system, i.e., a
Newtonian limit is established where the speed of light is kept constant as it
should be and the limiting behavior is analyzed in terms of a parameter which
is tied to the physical properties of the individual solutions. This result is
then used to investigate the stability properties of the relativistic steady
states with small redshift parameter in the spirit of recent work by the same
authors, i.e., the second variation of the ADM mass about such a steady state
is shown to be positive definite on a suitable class of states.

1 kg beef brisket

2 cups chopped, dried (about 1 lemon), red tomatoes

2 tsp basil

3 tbsp olive oil

1 tbsp freshly ground black pepper

4 tbsp honey

1 cup low fat ricotta cheese (about 30 gms), divided

1 tbsp chopped parsley (optional, add to taste)

fresh ground black pepper to taste

salt and pepper to taste

In a large frying pan, brown the beef brisket in the olive oil with the celery, onion, and garlic over a high heat for 4-5 minutes, removing most of the fat from the pan. 3 small russet potatoes
1 head garlic (12-14 cloves. It's a LOT. Be afraid.)
1/3 cup fresh lemon juice
1/2 tablespoon salt
1/2 cup canola oil
Peel the potatoes and boil in water until soft. Mash and let cool. Crush and peel a whole head of garlic. Cut into quarters. Place raw garlic in a heavy duty blender with the salt and lemon juice. Pour a light layer of oil onto garlic. Puree the garlic, salt lemon juice on high and begin pouring a slow steady stream of the rest of the oil through the blender's handle hole until everything has mixed. At this point, you'll have extreme garlickiness (new word), which some people like, but for "texturizing" like Zankou's, you'll need the taters. Add the mashed potatoes, about 2-3 tablespoons at a time and mix. Continue adding/blending potato until the sauce is mixed well. At some point in this process, you might consider changing blending vessels. After all this work, my blender was starting to think twice about helping me out. Transfer to a bowl and allow to chill completely in the fridge. After about an hour, the flavors will blend together nicely and the texture will take on that library paste consistency like Zankou's sauce.

The Alden staRRcar, short for "Self-Transport Road and Rail Car", was a personal rapid transit (PRT) system designed by William Alden in the 1960s. It originally envisioned small electrically powered cars suitable for short distance trips at low speed within urban areas, which could optionally merge onto tracks that would provide power and guidance for high-speed travel over longer inter-city distances. It was one of the earliest dual-mode vehicles to be proposed, and one of the earliest to be actually built. Over its lifetime the design changed dramatically, originally a four-person vehicle with dual-mode operation but eventually emerging as a much larger people mover for 20 people. In this form, Boeing Vertol was awarded a construction contract in 1970 to build a demonstration system in Morgantown, West Virginia. A smaller system was also built by their licensee, Kobe Steel, and installed at the Expo '75 on Okinawa (as well as the more advanced CVS). The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system first opened for service in 1975, and with the exception of a closure for a major expansion, has remained in service since then.

This paper introduces Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRW-Net) for semantic image segmentation as a combination of convolutional neural networks, random walks on graphs and spectral graph theory. The basic idea is to extend the receptive field of a neural network's convolutional layer at a minimal cost. Given a CNN, CRW-Net extends the receptive field by one convolutional layer which has random connections to the original CNN's convolutional layers. The randomness comes from the random choice of edges in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs). To solve the issue of overfitting in GCN-based models, We proposed a loss function called graph spectral loss. We empirically show that the proposed method can improve segmentation performance when it is combined with fully connected CRF on PASCAL VOC 2012 (segmentation accuracy 71.2\%), VOCS (segmentation accuracy 77.1\%) and COCO-Stuff (segmentation accuracy 51.2\%). Our proposed method achieved the state-of-the-art performance on COCO-Stuff, outperformed the previous best result by more than 3\%.

The above text was extracted from a page on the arxiv.org website (https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06107). I've seen researchers reference arxiv.org, but I've always wondered how people use this resource. Do the papers get cited on Google Scholar? If not, what is the primary use case for authors to release papers on arxiv.org?

A: ArXiv is not a publication venue; it is an archive.  They have an agreement that once an author publishes on the archive, he/she will not post the work elsewhere for at least a month, which is why you see one-month "first notice of use."  That protects the author in case somebody sees the work, then publishes something on it earlier.

A: The primary use of arxiv is to provide a quick way for researchers to distribute their work to a large audience before peer review. Once posted, the paper can be immediately cited, discussed, etc., while the researchers work on tweaking / fixing their paper.
For example, if an author finds a minor error in their arXiv posted paper, they can make the corrections and repost it

Recent advancements utilizing Deep Convolutional Neural Networks have successfully segmented medical images, though these networks struggle with capturing distant relationships within images due to their architectural limitations.  More recently, Transformer models employing self-attention have demonstrated an ability to represent long-range dependencies and create powerful feature representations.  This prompts investigation into applying Transformers to medical image segmentation, despite the challenge that most existing Transformer architectures demand extensive training datasets – a constraint often unmet in the limited medical imaging domain.  To address this, we introduce a Gated Axial-Attention model, enhancing existing Transformers with a novel control mechanism. We also propose a Local-Global (LoGo) training strategy to improve performance by learning both broad contextual information from the entire image and detailed local characteristics from individual patches.  Our resulting Medical Transformer (MedT) was tested across three diverse datasets and outperformed conventional convolutional methods and other Transformer variants. To create these bars, begin with 1 tablespoon of sunflower oil (or another healthy oil). Combine 1 ¼ cups of rolled oats, ¾ cup of toasted and chopped walnuts (or your preferred nut), ½ cup of toasted sliced almonds (or another nut), and ⅔ cup of shredded unsweetened coconut. Add 1 tablespoon of ground flax seeds (or a combination of flax seeds and nutritional yeast flakes), 1 ½ cups of crisp brown rice cereal (such as Rice Krispies), 1 cup of chopped dried cranberries (or alternative dried fruit), 3 tablespoons of finely chopped crystallized ginger, and ⅓ cup of sesame seeds. Fiat's board has approved a deal to give GM a $2.8bn (£1.7bn) stake in its auto business, clearing a major obstacle to a merger of the two carmakers.

The deal had been delayed as Fiat's board debated GM's offer and fought off a rival bid from Ford.

The merger will create the world's third-biggest carmaker by sales.

The combined company will be called Fiat-GM and be headed by Fiat's CEO, Sergio Marchionne.

The deal must still be approved by regulators and shareholders.

If it goes through, GM will get a 20% stake in Fiat, while Fiat will get a 1.5% stake in GM.

The merger has been approved by the boards of both companies but still needs the go-ahead from regulators and shareholders.

If the merger is approved, the new company would be worth about $140bn, based on the companies' current market values.

By comparison, Toyota is currently the world's biggest carmaker with sales of 10.2 million vehicles last year, followed by Volkswagen with 8.3 million.

Fiat-GM would sell about 8.6 million cars a year.

The merger deal comes as the auto industry struggles to recover from a sharp drop in sales in the US and Europe.

The combined company will have about $132bn in debt, ranking it as one of the most indebted companies in the world.

GM sold a record 4.7 million cars and trucks in 2010 but analysts say it needs to expand to survive as sales growth slows in its main markets.

Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornmeal
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 package (2 1/4 teaspoons) active dry yeast
- 1 cup warm water (110°F)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 cup pizza sauce
- 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1/2 cup sliced pepperoni
- 1/4 cup sliced black olives (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced green bell peppers (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced red onions (optional)
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Fresh basil leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, salt, and sugar. In a separate small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until it becomes frothy.

2. Pour the yeast mixture and olive oil into the dry ingredients. Stir until a dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour. If it's too dry, add a little more water. Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.

3. Grease a deep-dish pizza pan or a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Press the dough into the pan, making sure to cover the bottom and sides evenly. Let the dough rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes until it doubles in size.

4. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Once the dough has risen, spread the pizza sauce evenly over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges. Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce.

5. Arrange the pepperoni slices on top of the cheese. If desired, add black olives, green bell peppers, and red onions as additional toppings. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the toppings.

6. Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is bubbly and slightly browned.

7. Remove the pizza from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh basil leaves if desired. Slice and serve hot.

Enjoy your delicious homemade Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza!

Humans, as interpreters of nature, achieve only what they’ve genuinely observed through experience or reflection; exceeding this limit yields no further knowledge or ability. 

Both hands and intellect alone are limited.  Work requires tools and assistance, just as understanding needs guidance. Instruments offer both direction and impetus, mirroring how mental tools provide prompts and warnings.

True human capability resides in the intersection of knowledge and action. Without knowing the cause, effects cannot be created. To control nature, one must first understand it, and that underlying cause dictates subsequent operations.

Essentially, humans manipulate existing materials – assembling or disassembling them – while nature completes the process internally. Mechanics, mathematicians, physicians, alchemists, and magicians pursue this through observation, though often with minimal impact.

Expecting novel achievements without previously attempted methods is illogical. Existing creations stem from refined modifications of established principles, not from fundamental discoveries.

Furthermore, these accomplishments primarily arise from chance encounters and experimentation, rather than established scientific frameworks. Current “sciences” organize and present pre-existing inventions, lacking inventive capacity.

A key issue hindering progress stems from overestimating the mind's potential while overlooking the need to explore its limitations.

Deep learning techniques for 3D brain vessel image segmentation have not been
as successful as in the segmentation of other organs and tissues. This can be
explained by two factors. First, deep learning techniques tend to show poor
performances at the segmentation of relatively small objects compared to the
size of the full image. Second, due to the complexity of vascular trees and the
small size of vessels, it is challenging to obtain the amount of annotated
training data typically needed by deep learning methods. To address these
problems, we propose a novel annotation-efficient deep learning vessel
segmentation framework. The framework avoids pixel-wise annotations, only
requiring weak patch-level labels to discriminate between vessel and non-vessel
2D patches in the training set, in a setup similar to the CAPTCHAs used to
differentiate humans from bots in web applications. The user-provided weak
annotations are used for two tasks: 1) to synthesize pixel-wise pseudo-labels
for vessels and background in each patch, which are used to train a
segmentation network, and 2) to train a classifier network. The classifier
network allows to generate additional weak patch labels, further reducing the
annotation burden, and it acts as a noise filter for poor quality images. We
use this framework for the segmentation of the cerebrovascular tree in
Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Images (SWI). The
results show that the framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, while
reducing the annotation time by ~77% w.r.t. learning-based segmentation methods
using pixel-wise labels for training.

Rinus Michels, the influential Dutch coach renowned for pioneering “total football,” passed away at age 77. Known as “the General” in the Netherlands, he directed the Dutch squad to the 1974 World Cup final – a loss against Germany despite reaching that stage – and then secured the 1988 European Championship victory with a 2-0 triumph over the Soviet Union. He achieved success during his time with Ajax, leading them to four domestic titles and a European Cup in 1971.  His famed 1970s team, centered around Johan Cruyff and Johan Neeskens, revolutionized tactics with its emphasis on collective harmony and player versatility; every player was expected to be capable of contributing across the field. Cruyff served as the team’s tactical leader, orchestrating fluid rotations within the defensive line and promoting inventive attacks. Michels later coached Barcelona to a Spanish league championship in 1974, alongside stints at FC Cologne and Bayer Leverkusen. Recognized as coach of the century by FIFA in 1999, he earned five international appearances for the Netherlands as a forceful striker. Dutch Minister of Sport, Clemence Ross-van Dorp stated, “Together with Cruyff, he transformed Dutch football.”

General Sir John Gordon Noel Wilton,  (22 November 1910 – 10 May 1981) was a senior commander in the Australian Army. He served as Chief of the General Staff (CGS), the Army's professional head, from 1963 until 1966, and as Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (CCOSC), forerunner of the role of Australia's Chief of the Defence Force, from 1966 until 1970. His eight-year tenure as senior officer of first the Army and then the Australian military spanned almost the entire period of the nation's involvement in the Vietnam War. Born in Sydney, Wilton entered the Royal Military College, Duntroon, in 1927. Owing to lack of opportunity in the Australian military at the time, he took a commission in the British Army following his graduation in 1930. He spent most of the remainder of the decade with the Royal Artillery in India. Wilton returned to Australia on the eve of World War II and was commissioned into the Royal Australian Artillery. He saw action with the 7th Division in Syria and the 3rd Division in New Guinea, earning a mention in despatches in the former campaign and the Distinguished Service Order in the latter.  Finishing the war a temporary colonel, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1947. Wilton was posted to Korea in 1953 to take command of the 28th Commonwealth Brigade, leading it in its final action of the war in July. He was raised to Commander of the Order of the British Empire and awarded the US Legion of Merit for his performance in Korea.

It consists of 152 classes with 300k images collected from ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) and Pascal VOC 2012 datasets. Each class has two domains: synthetic rendered images and real world photos. Our research investigates the smallest lexicographical $a/b$-power-free word using the set of non-negative integers as an alphabet. This word often arises as a fixed point within a uniform morphism, or is intimately connected to such a morphism; for instance, the lexicographically smallest $7/4$-power-free word corresponds to a $50847$-uniform morphism. We analyze the structural properties of the lexicographically least $a/b$-power-free word across several infinite sets of rationals $a/b$, including numerous irregular rationals. To achieve this, we create an automated method for demonstrating $a/b$-power-freeness in specific types of morphisms, applicable to both explicit and symbolic rational numbers $a/b$. Furthermore, we link this concept to words over a finite alphabet—specifically, the lexicographically smallest $27/23$-power-free word can be represented as a word with letters from the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ and exhibits a $353$-automatic sequence.

The site was shut down by the FBI in 2012 following an investigation that revealed the massive scale of copyright infringement taking place on the site. 

The jury found that the defendants were aware of the widespread copyright infringement taking place on MegaUpload but took no meaningful action to prevent it. In a statement, the U.S. Attorney's Office said that the defendants "made a profit by encouraging, promoting, and assisting the widespread distribution of copyrighted materials without the permission of the copyright owners." 

The four defendants face a maximum sentence of five years in prison and significant financial penalties for their role in operating MegaUpload. The sentencing hearing is scheduled for later this year.

To improve pixel representations for semantic image segmentation, researchers frequently use co-occurring visual patterns to gather contextual data. Current techniques primarily model context at the overall image level, leveraging image-wide contextual information. However, these methods can diminish the importance of pixel representations within specific categories – that is, semantic-level contextual details. This work introduces a method to enrich pixel representations by combining image-level and semantic-level contexts. Specifically, an image-level context module captures contextual information for each pixel. Subsequently, representations of pixels belonging to the same category are aggregated based on supervised learning using ground truth segmentations. Then, similarity scores are calculated between individual pixel representations and both the image-level and semantic-level contexts. Finally, a pixel representation is augmented through weighted aggregation, utilizing the similarity scores as weights for the combined image and semantic context.  This approach achieves state-of-the-art results across four datasets—ADE20K, LIP, COCOStuff, and Cityscapes.

**Dough:** Combine 1 cup softened butter and 8 ounces softened cream cheese, then stir in 1/2 cup sugar. Gradually mix in 2 3/4 cups flour along with 1 teaspoon of salt. Form the dough into a ball, kneading gently until smooth and fully combined. Divide the dough into eight portions, flatten each into a disc, and cover with plastic wrap. Chill for one hour. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).

**Filling:** In a separate bowl, combine 3/4 cup sugar, 2/3 cup finely chopped dried sour cherries, 1 stick of melted butter, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, and 1 teaspoon allspice.

**Glaze:** Whisk together 1 egg and granulated sugar.

**Instructions:** Roll out each chilled dough disc into an 8”x8” square on a lightly floured surface. Spread approximately 1/4 cup of the filling evenly over the center, leaving a ½-inch border. Brush each cookie with the egg mixture and sprinkle with additional sugar. Bake for 20 minutes, or until golden brown. Let cool on wire racks before serving. *Note:* Cherries and walnuts can be quickly chopped using a food processor.*

Chips (1940–1946) was a trained sentry dog for United States Army, and reputedly the most decorated war dog from World War II. Chips was a German Shepherd-Collie-Husky mix owned by Edward J. Wren of Pleasantville, New York. During the war, private citizens like Wren donated their dogs for duty. Chips shipped out to the War Dog Training Center, Front Royal, Virginia, in 1942 for training as a sentry dog. He served with the 3rd Infantry Division in North Africa, Sicily, Italy, France and Germany.  His handler was Pvt. John P. Rowell.  Chips served as a sentry dog for the Roosevelt-Churchill conference in 1943. Later that year, during the invasion of Sicily, Chips and his handler were pinned down on the beach by an Italian machine-gun team.  Chips broke from his handler and jumped into the pillbox, attacking the gunners. The four crewmen were forced to leave the pillbox and surrendered to US troops. In the fight, he sustained a scalp wound and powder burns.  Later that day, he helped take ten Italians prisoner.

Deep learning methods have achieved promising performance in many areas, but
they are still struggling with noisy-labeled images during the training
process. Considering that the annotation quality indispensably relies on great
expertise, the problem is even more crucial in the medical image domain. How to
eliminate the disturbance from noisy labels for segmentation tasks without
further annotations is still a significant challenge. In this paper, we
introduce our label quality evaluation strategy for deep neural networks
automatically assessing the quality of each label, which is not explicitly
provided, and training on clean-annotated ones. We propose a solution for
network automatically evaluating the relative quality of the labels in the
training set and using good ones to tune the network parameters. We also design
an overfitting control module to let the network maximally learn from the
precise annotations during the training process. Experiments on the public
biomedical image segmentation dataset have proved the method outperforms
baseline methods and retains both high accuracy and good generalization at
different noise levels.

Although deep convolutional neural networks have significantly advanced medical image processing, their reliance on extensive labeled data—a supervised learning approach—can lead to overfitting and limits successful outcomes. Obtaining detailed semantic annotations is challenging in many clinical scenarios due to the need for specialist biomedical expertise and limited availability of labeled examples. To address this, we introduce a new few-shot medical image segmentation technique that allows models to quickly adapt to previously unseen classes even with minimal training data. Our segmenter utilizes a deep convolutional network trained iteratively, leveraging the inherent spatial coherence of medical imagery. We created a ‘global correlation network’ incorporating an efficient module designed to capture relationships between support and query images. This module enhances the discriminative power of learned embeddings, promoting grouping features from the same organ while separating those of different organs.  Results from ablation studies confirm the value of our correlation module and discriminatory embedding loss. Experiments using abdominal CT and MRI images showcase superior performance compared to existing methods.

Demand for automatic sign language recognition is growing rapidly, particularly within the deaf community.  While some research teams have explored techniques like using videos and colored gloves, these often necessitate precise data separation for training and recognition. Recognizing sign language images presents difficulties due to the diverse range of hand gestures. This paper introduces a method combining image segmentation with topological derivative restoration to enhance recognition accuracy. We evaluate image quality metrics to compare our approach subjectively and objectively. Results demonstrate that pre-restoring images before segmentation substantially boosts hand detection accuracy, and that discrete derivatives effectively distinguish various hand poses from the surrounding environment. Ultimately, this work aims to facilitate the development of automated sign language systems intended primarily to benefit individuals with hearing impairments.

The amount of spam circulating online could be about to undergo a massive increase, say experts.
Anti-spam group Spamhaus is warning about a novel virus which hides the origins of junk mail. The program makes spam look like it is being sent by legitimate mail servers making it hard to spot and filter out. Spamhaus said that if the problem went unchecked real e-mail messages could get drowned by the sheer amount of junk being sent.
Before now many spammers have recruited home PCs to act as anonymous e-mail relays in an attempt to hide the origins of their junk mail. The PCs are recruited using viruses and worms that compromise machines via known vulnerabilities or by tricking people into opening an attachment infected with the malicious program. Once compromised the machines start to pump out junk mail on behalf of spammers. Spamhaus helps to block junk messages from these machines by collecting and circulating blacklists of net addresses known to harbour infected machines. But the novel worm spotted recently by Spamhaus routes junk via the mail servers of the net service firm that infected machines used to get online in the first place. In this way the junk mail gets a net address that looks legitimate. As blocking all mail from net firms just to catch the spam is impractical, Spamhaus is worried that the technique will give junk mailers the ability to spam with little fear of being spotted and stopped. Steve Linford, director of Spamhaus, predicted that if a lot of spammers exploit this technique it could trigger the failure of the net's e-mail sending infrastructure. David Stanley, UK managing director of filtering firm Ciphertrust, said the new technique was the next logical step for spammers. "They are adding to their armoury," he said. The amount of spam in circulation was still growing, said Mr Stanley, but he did not think that the appearance of this trick would mean e-mail meltdown. But Kevin Hogan, senior manager at Symantec security response, said such warnings were premature. "If something like this mean the end of e-mail then e-mail would have stopped two-three years ago," said Mr Hogan. While the technique of routing mail via mail servers of net service firms might cause problems for those that use blacklists and block lists it did not mean that other techniques for stopping spam lost their efficacy too. Mr Hogan said 90% of the junk mail filtered by Symantec subsidiary Brightmail was spotted using techniques that did not rely on looking at net addresses. For instance, said Mr Hogan, filtering out e-mail messages that contain a web link can stop about 75% of spam.

However, despite appreciating his work and having prior enthusiasm, I struggled to fully engage with the movie. The actors perform adequately, particularly considering the challenge of expressing emotion towards a simple tennis ball, yet their mannerisms ultimately conceal a lack of depth within the piece. While visually striking, it echoes previous Burton films like *Edward Scissorhands*, which possessed genuine intention; here, we're presented with a largely uninspired CGI world lacking true enchantment. The book's unique settings, peculiar dialogue, and eccentric characters are subdued, losing their mystique and resulting in a visually appealing but easily forgotten imitation. The plot rushes toward a predictable ending, failing to generate significant audience investment due to a lack of compelling characters. Considering the familiarity of the source material—even for casual fans—the film requires fresh interpretation, akin to Svenkmejer’s stop-motion or Gilliam’s *Tideland*, or a truly faithful return to Lewis Carroll. Instead, it offers a mediocre adaptation that misses the core elements of the *Alice* story, relying on a familiar aesthetic and Danny Elfman’s score. The Government of the United Kingdom maintains intelligence agencies within several  government departments. The agencies are responsible for collecting and analysing foreign and domestic intelligence, providing military intelligence, performing espionage and counter-espionage. Their intelligence assessments contribute to the conduct of the foreign relations of the United Kingdom, maintaining the national security of the United Kingdom, military planning and law enforcement in the United Kingdom.  The main organisations are the Secret Intelligence Service (SIS or MI6), the Security Service (MI5), the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) and Defence Intelligence (DI). The history of the organisations dates back to the 19th century. The decryption of the Zimmermann Telegram in 1917 was described as the most significant intelligence triumph for Britain during World War I, and one of the earliest occasions on which a piece of signals intelligence influenced world events. During the Second World War and afterwards, many observers regarded Ultra as immensely valuable to the Allies of World War II. In 1962, during the Cuban Missile Crisis, GCHQ interceptions of Soviet ship positions were sent directly to the White House. Intelligence cooperation in the post-war period between the United Kingdom and the United States became the cornerstone of Western intelligence gathering and the "Special Relationship" between the United Kingdom and the United States.

'Interview with the Vampire' is an atmospheric, highly gripping "film involving vampires" - not a "vampire movie". Whilst the latter would describe a film that focuses on its vampirism and might be judged on the sharpness of its fangs, this "film involving vampires" has all the merits of the very best cinema, and at its core is nothing but a fantastic story carried by compelling, believable characters.

For those who may not be able to overlook the vampiric content, look again. The vampirism herein is a plot device, a way of presenting characters who cannot die or age or be harmed, so that the philosophical questions of life itself can be explored. But equally, for those who will be interested in the vampiric content, this film presents a rich mythology backed by a trilogy of books, which fleshes out the concept of the vampire in a much deeper way than any other production.

Every person has their own world view, their own way of living and thinking. People can be brooding, contemplative, cautious, reasonable, carefree, hedonistic, optimistic, emotional - and every shade in between. But these are all world-views based on the knowledge that life is short. What would happen if told their lives would never end? Who would be happiest? What would they do? How would eternal life affect each person? And most importantly, if a way of living was bringing meaning to a person's life, would that still work once life was infinite? All of these questions help us explore philosophical ideas as old as time, and that exploration is the focus of this film.

The story is propelled by vampires Louis (Pitt) and Lestat (Cruise), each representing a different take on life. Whilst Louis, who began as a depressive wanting to die, thinks of eternity as an extended curse; Lestat, who seems to live every second as it comes, barely even considers the future three minutes hence. Told from Louis' viewpoint as he struggles to find some meaning in a life he knows will never end, we are taken on a ride across the centuries, as Louis' outlook and happiness undulate whilst characters and relationships come and go.

Alongside Louis' turmoil in coming to terms with his (now eternal) life, a secondary theme is explored, which is the notion of survival. Even though Louis is clearly dissatisfied with life, he never attempts to end it, despite this option being open to him. In other words, surviving, in and of itself, was a motivation that outdid any other. Most importantly, survival outdoes Louis' trouble over the fact that his only source of nourishment is now the blood of living animals, preferably humans. Despite attempting abstinence, and then attempting to drink only the blood of rodents, this basic feeding instinct proves too much for Louis. And yet, as Lestat points out, what is the problem? The fittest always survives, and whoever is lower down the food-chain will be eaten. Humans eat animals, and vampires eat humans - it's all natural. But nonetheless, are there moral limits? Even if you have to kill a human, is there a more moral way to do it? "Monstrous," Louis exclaims, as he watches a group of vampires murder a defenceless girl. Yet might survival require the forgetting of moral consciousness, like Lestat?

'Interview with the Vampire' explores all of these deep, important issues whilst delivering an incredibly powerful story populated by charismatic characters, haunting and diverse settings and immortal dialogue. Gripping from start to finish, you will be enamoured at the vampire-world opened up to you; and by the end, you are left wondering what choice you would have made, given the one that Lestat never had...

Scientists are working on ways to ensure laptops can stay powered for an entire working day.
Building batteries from new chemical mixes could boost power significantly, say industry experts. The changes include everything from the way chips for laptops are made, to tricks that reduce the power consumption of displays. Ever since laptops appeared the amount of time they last between recharges has been a frustration for users.
A survey carried out in 2000 by Forrester Research found that the shortness of battery life was the most complained about feature of laptops. "The focus back then was more on performance and features," said Mike Trainor, chief mobile technology evangelist for chip giant Intel.
"For most of the 90s battery life was stuck on two to 2.5 hours." But now, he said, laptops can last much longer. It was not just a case of improving battery life by squeezing more out of the lithium ion power packs, he explained. Other changes are needed to get to the holy grail of a laptop running for about eight hours before needing a recharge. "Lithium ion is never going to get there by itself," he said. "The industry has done a great job of wringing all possible energy storage out of that technology that they can." Some new battery chemistries promise to cram more power into the same space, said Mr Trainor, though work still needed to be done to get them successfully from the lab to manufacturing. He was sceptical that fuel cells would develop quick enough to take over from solid batteries even though they have the potential to produce several times more energy than lithium ion power packs. "In fuel cells you need to have pumps and separators and evaporation chambers," he said. "It's a mini energy plant that needs to be shrunk and shrunk and shrunk."
Intel has been working with component makers to test energy consumption on all the parts inside a laptop and find ways to make them less power hungry.
This work has led to the creation of the Mobile PC Extended Battery Life (EBL) Working Group that shares information about building notebooks that are more parsimonious with power. Some of the improvements in power use come simply because components on chips are shrinking, said Mr Trainor. Intel has also changed the way it creates transistors on silicon to reduce the power they need. On a larger scale, said Mr Trainor, improvements in the way that voltage regulators are made can reduce the amount of power lost as heat and make a notebook more energy efficient. Also, said Mr Trainor, research is being done on ways to cut energy consumption on displays - currently the biggest power guzzler on a laptop. Many laptop makers have committed to creating 14 and 15 inch screens that draw only three watts of power. This is far below the power consumption levels of screens in current notebooks. "If we can get close to eight hours that's a place that people see as extraordinarily valuable that's what the industry has to deliver," Mr Trainor said.

- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups sugar snap peas
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil

Instructions:

2. Place the chicken breasts in a baking dish and pour the hoisin glaze over the top, turning the chicken to coat it evenly. Marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes, or up to a few hours in the refrigerator.

3. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

4. Place the chicken in the oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cooked through.

6. Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes before slicing it into thin pieces.

7. Serve the hoisin-glazed chicken with the sugar snap peas on the side. Enjoy!

Image segmentation is the process of partitioning a image into different
regions or groups based on some characteristics like color, texture, motion or
shape etc. Active contours is a popular variational method for object
segmentation in images, in which the user initializes a contour which evolves
in order to optimize an objective function designed such that the desired
object boundary is the optimal solution. Recently, imaging modalities that
produce Manifold valued images have come up, for example, DT-MRI images, vector
fields. The traditional active contour model does not work on such images. In
this paper, we generalize the active contour model to work on Manifold valued
images. As expected, our algorithm detects regions with similar Manifold values
in the image. Our algorithm also produces expected results on usual gray-scale
images, since these are nothing but trivial examples of Manifold valued images.
As another application of our general active contour model, we perform texture
segmentation on gray-scale images by first creating an appropriate Manifold
valued image. We demonstrate segmentation results for manifold valued images
and texture images.

This paper presents a novel approach to semi-supervised instance segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, by introducing a mask-guided sample selection strategy. The proposed method leverages the power of both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the performance of instance segmentation models. The mask-guided sample selection strategy selects informative samples from unlabeled data based on the prediction confidence of the instance segmentation model. The selected samples are then used to generate pseudo-labels, which are incorporated into the training process to enhance the model's learning. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing significant improvements over existing semi-supervised instance segmentation techniques.

This paper presents a novel approach to computer vision for liquid samples in hospitals and medical labs, utilizing hierarchical image segmentation and relations prediction. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of liquid sample analysis, which is crucial in diagnostics and treatment planning. The proposed method involves segmenting the image of the liquid sample into various hierarchical levels and predicting the relations between these segments. The paper discusses the development and implementation of the algorithm, and evaluates its performance using real-world data from medical labs. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the accuracy and speed of liquid sample analysis, suggesting potential for enhancing diagnostic processes in healthcare settings. The paper also explores potential future developments and applications of this technology in the medical field.

This research details our system designed for human-assisted video object segmentation, built around a one-shot technique. Although efficient, this approach needs precise pixel-level frame segmentation initially. Recognizing manual annotation’s difficulty, we introduce a deep interactive image segmentation method requiring minimal user clicks – approximately 4 – to achieve high accuracy. Our method achieves 90% Intersection over Union (IOU) on the GrabCut dataset using just 3.8 average clicks, representing a significant advancement. It also iteratively improves upon preliminary segmentations, correcting errors within videos and enabling rapid generation of good results, particularly in difficult scenarios. We analyze user behavior, examining the number of steps taken per frame and types of adjustments made, offering valuable data for future enhancements to interactive video segmentation techniques.

"Not only is Singer's film-making aesthetically frustrating (lacking coherent visual rhythm) but his juvenile regard of the July 20, 1944, plot to kill Hitler -- one of 15 documented attempts -- is intellectually insulting..." New York Press The above is the usual negative commentary you'll see regarding this film. Critics bashed it for being insulting, unoriginal, and unmoving. Let me make some corrections for them so that they can save a little face.

I'm no Tom Cruise fan. A buddy of mine, too, is so peeved at Cruise that he refuses to watch anything the man stars in. Mostly this has to do with Cruise's personal life and beliefs (just watch an episode of South Park to see how some people view him and you'll see what I mean). People have similar feelings toward Mel Gibson ...but I digress.

VALKYRIE, as most of you probably now know, is the final of 15 attempts on Hitler's life. Shortly after this (about nine months) he committed suicide in his bunker. But this is about the one time where it almost succeeded. I'd heard about this attempt and read bits of it in history classes, but never really gave it much thought. I mean, the mustachioed murderer offed himself, so that was that. But what gives this film much of its umpf! is how true to history the story sticks (that and how closely many of the actors resemble their true-life counterparts). It is also riveting coming from director Bryan Singer (who did one of my all-time favorite films, THE USUAL SUSPECTS).

Tom Cruise did a great job (probably one of his best since COLLATERAL and MINORITY REPORT). His Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg character was spot-on ...with one exception that seems to be a sticking point for many: his accent. It is true that none of the actors attempts a German cadence in their speech. Did this bother me? No. I think it would have bothered me if they'd TRIED to do one and made it sound forced or ridiculous. So there's that...

What makes the film a success was Cruise's rock solid performance and the amazing supporting cast: Kenneth Branagh, Bill Nighy, Tom Wilkinson, Terrence Stamp, and Eddie Izzard just to sprinkle a few names.

It is also noteworthy to mention that they filmed nearly everything on-location and in the exact same spots where the original incidents took place, including the subsequent trials and executions of the conspirators. Phenomenal authenticity.

If the cadence of their speech bothered some, then I failed to see how the cadence of the film could. It was absolutely perfect. It gradually built up suspense (even though we knew how it would end for the conspirators), and never slowed, right up until the very end. I am forced to use a cliché here in that "I was on the edge of my seat" throughout the second half of the film.

So if you're looking to tear apart Tom Cruise, you might look at WAR OF THE WORLDS or LEGEND. But not here.

Cream of Mushroom Soup is a flavorful and versatile dish that can be served as a starter or a light meal. This recipe requires only a few simple ingredients and can be made in just a few steps.

To begin, heat butter or oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and cook until they are soft and release their liquid. Next, add the onion and cook until it is translucent. Then, add the garlic and cook for another minute.

Once the mushrooms, onion, and garlic are cooked, add the flour and stir until the mixture is smooth. Cook for another minute to get the flour taste out. Then, gradually add the chicken broth, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth and thickened.

Next, add the milk, salt, and pepper and stir until the mixture is combined. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the soup is thickened.

Finally, stir in the parsley and serve the soup hot. This soup can be served as a starter or a light meal, and it can also be paired with a salad or bread for a more filling meal. Whether served as a starter or a main course, this soup is sure to be a hit. It’s warm, comforting, and full of flavor.

Experts predict a significant surge in online spam due to a newly discovered virus. Spamhaus has issued a warning about this program, which disguises the source of junk email by mimicking legitimate mail servers, making detection and filtering significantly more difficult. If left unaddressed, the volume of spam could overwhelm genuine emails. Traditionally, spammers utilized compromised personal computers as anonymous relay servers, infecting them through malware spread via vulnerabilities or deceptive attachments. Spamhaus combats this by maintaining blacklists of infected IP addresses. However, this new worm reroutes spam through the mail servers previously used by the infected machines, effectively creating a seemingly authentic sender address. Blocking entire internet service providers to combat the spam is considered too broad, raising concerns that spammers can operate largely undetected. According to Spamhaus director Steve Linford, widespread exploitation of this method could destabilize the internet’s email system. Ciphertrust’s David Stanley believes this represents a clever tactic employed by spammers to enhance their methods. While overall spam levels continue to rise, Stanley doesn’t foresee a complete email collapse. Nevertheless, Symantec’s Kevin Hogan cautions that such strategies pose a serious threat.

The novel begins when Henry Pulling, a conventional and uncharming bank manager who has taken early retirement, meets his septuagenarian Aunt Augusta for the first time in over fifty years at his mother's funeral. Despite having little in common, they form a bond. Henry finds himself drawn into Aunt Augusta's world of travel, adventure, romance and absence of bigotry. He travels first with her to Brighton, where he meets one of his aunt's old acquaintances, and gains an insight into one of her many past lives. Here a psychic foreshadows that he will have many travels in the near future. This prediction inevitably becomes true as Henry is pulled further and further into his aunt's lifestyle, and delves deeper into her past. Their voyages take them from Paris to Istanbul on the Orient Express, and as the journey unfolds, so do the stories of Aunt Augusta, painting the picture of a woman for whom love has been the defining feature of her life. Henry returns to his quiet retirement, but tending his garden no longer holds the same allure. When he receives a letter from his aunt, he finally gives up his old life to join her and the love of her life in South America, and to marry a girl decades younger than himself. As his travels progress it becomes clear to Henry that the woman he had been raised to believe was his mother was in fact his aunt. His real mother is Augusta, and her reconnection with him at her sister's funeral marked the beginning of her reclamation of her child.
