Sportswear giant Nike has reported strong quarterly growth, exceeding market expectations. The company's revenue for the quarter ending in May reached $12.3 billion, a 96% increase compared to the same period last year. This remarkable growth can be attributed to several factors, including the reopening of economies worldwide and the increasing demand for athletic apparel and footwear.

Nike's digital sales played a significant role in driving the company's success, with a staggering 147% increase in online sales. As consumers turned to online shopping during the pandemic, Nike's robust e-commerce platform proved to be a valuable asset. The company's direct-to-consumer sales also saw a remarkable surge, rising by 73% compared to the previous year.

Furthermore, Nike's strong performance was not limited to its home market. International sales soared by 88%, with particularly impressive growth in China, where revenue increased by 17%. This growth in China is a testament to Nike's ability to tap into the country's booming consumer market and capitalize on the rising popularity of sports and fitness.

Nike's success can also be attributed to its ability to adapt and innovate. The company has been quick to respond to changing consumer preferences, focusing on sustainability and inclusivity. Nike's commitment to sustainability is evident in its efforts to reduce its carbon footprint and increase the use of recycled materials in its products. Additionally, the company's collaborations with diverse athletes and celebrities have helped it resonate with a broader audience and drive sales.

Looking ahead, Nike remains optimistic about its future prospects. The company expects continued growth in the coming quarters, driven by the return of sports events and the ongoing shift towards athleisure wear. Nike's strong brand reputation and innovative product offerings position it well to capitalize on these trends and maintain its market dominance.

Despite the positive outlook, Nike acknowledges potential challenges, including supply chain disruptions and rising raw material costs. However, the company remains confident in its ability to navigate these obstacles and continue delivering strong results.

In summary, Nike's strong quarterly growth reflects its ability to adapt to changing consumer preferences, capitalize on digital sales channels, and expand its international presence. With a focus on sustainability and inclusivity, the sportswear giant is well-positioned to maintain its market leadership and drive further growth in the future.

The explosion in consumer technology is to continue into 2005, delegates at the world's largest gadget show, in Las Vegas, have been told.
The number of gadgets in the shops is predicted to grow by 11%, while devices which talk to each other will become increasingly important. "Everything is going digital," Kirsten Pfeifer from the Consumer Electronics Association, told the BBC News website. The Consumer Electronics Show (CES) featured the pick of 2005's products. "Consumers are controlling what they want and technologies like HDTVs [high-definition TVs], digital radio, and digital cameras will remain strong in 2005. "All the products on show really showed the breadth and depth of the industry." Despite showing diversity, some delegates attending complained that the showcase lacked as much "wow factor" as in previous years.
The portable technologies on show also reflected one of the buzzwords of CES, which was the "time and place shifting" of multimedia content - being able to watch and listen to video and music anywhere, at any time. At the start of last year's CES, the CEA predicted there would be an average growth of 4% in 2004. That figure was surpassed with the rise in popularity of portable digital music players, personal video recorders and digital cameras. It was clear also that gadgets are becoming a lot more about lifestyle choice, with fashion and personalisation becoming increasingly key to the way gadgets are designed. Part of this has been the rise in spending power of the "generation X-ers" who have grown up with technology and who now have the spending power and desire for more devices that suit them. More than 57% of the consumer electronics market is made up of female buyers, according to CEA research. Hybrid devices, which combine a number of multimedia functions, were also in evidence on the show floor. "A lot of this is driven by just the ability to do it," said Stephen Baker, a consumer electronics analyst with retail research firm NPD Group. "Some of these functions cost next to nothing to add."
As well as the show floor showcasing everything from tiny wearable MP3 players to giant high-definition TVs, several keynote speeches were made by industry leaders, such as Microsoft chief Bill Gates. Despite several embarrassing technical glitches during Mr Gate's pre-show speech, he announced several new partnerships - mainly for the US market. He unveiled new ways of letting people take TV shows recorded on personal video recorders and watch them back on portable devices. He disappointed some, however, by failing to announce any details of the next generation of the Xbox games console. Another disappointment was the lack of exposure Sony's new portable games device, the PSP, had at the show. Sony said the much-anticipated gadget would most likely start shipping in March for the US and Europe. It went on sale in Japan before Christmas. There were only two PSPs embedded in glass cabinets at the show though and no representatives to discuss further details. A Sony representative told the BBC News website this was because Sony did not consider it to be part of their "consumer technology" offering.
Elsewhere at the show, there was a plethora of colour and plasma screens, including Samsung's 102-inch (2.6 metre) plasma - the largest in the world. Industry experts were also excited about high-definition technologies coming to the fore in 2005, with new formats for DVDs coming out which will hold six times as much data as conventional DVDs. With so many devices on the move there were a lot of products on show offering external storage, like Seagate's 5GB pocket sized external hard drive, which won an innovation for engineering and design prize. More than 120,000 trade professionals attended CES in Las Vegas, which officially ran from 6 to 9 January.

Ranhill Utilities Berhad  is a Malaysian conglomerate with interests in environment and power sectors. In the environment sector, it provides water supply services, operates water and wastewater treatment plants, and provides specialised services in the management and optimisation of water utility assets. In the power sector, it develops, owns and operates power generation assets. Its operations and services are primarily in Malaysia, and its international operations are centered in Asian markets such as China, Thailand and Southeast Asia. In the environment business, Ranhill has been granted an exclusive license by the Minister of Energy, Green Technology and Water, Malaysia to provide source-to-tap water supply services to end-customers in the entire State of Johor, the second most populous state in Malaysia, with a population of approximately 3.5 million people. Outside Malaysia, it operates water concession assets on a BOT, BTO and TOT basis in China which consist of 8 wastewater treatment plants with capacities ranging from 5.0 MLD to 80.0 MLD and a 30.0 MLD reclamation plant. In Thailand, Ranhill has 4 potable water treatment plants with capacities ranging from 10.5 MLD to 15.0 MLD, 4 wastewater treatment plants with capacities ranging from 1.5 MLD to 24.0 MLD and a 10.0 MLD reclamation plants.  In addition, through its joint venture, Yichun Pinang, Ranhill also operates a potable water treatment plant in Yichun City, China with a treatment capacity of 50.0 MLD.

The Epipalaeolithic, also known as the Late Stone Age or Mesolithic, is a period in human prehistory that falls between the end of the Paleolithic period and the beginning of the Neolithic period. It is characterized by the transition from a nomadic, hunter-gatherer lifestyle to a more settled, agricultural way of life.

The Epipalaeolithic period is generally dated from around 20,000 to 10,000 years ago, although these dates can vary depending on the region. It is a time of significant cultural and technological developments, as humans began to adapt to changing environmental conditions and exploit new resources.

During the Epipalaeolithic, the climate was gradually warming after the last Ice Age, leading to the retreat of glaciers and the expansion of forests. This created new opportunities for human populations, as they could now exploit a wider range of plant and animal resources. As a result, there was a shift towards a more sedentary lifestyle, with the establishment of semi-permanent settlements and the development of more complex social structures.

One of the key innovations of the Epipalaeolithic period was the development of new tools and technologies. Stone tools became more specialized and efficient, with the introduction of microliths – small, finely crafted stone blades that could be hafted onto wooden handles or used as projectile points. These microliths were used for a variety of purposes, including hunting, fishing, and woodworking.

The Epipalaeolithic period also witnessed the emergence of early forms of agriculture and animal domestication. While hunting and gathering remained the primary means of subsistence, there is evidence of early cultivation of wild cereals and the domestication of animals such as dogs. This laid the foundation for the later transition to full-scale agriculture and the development of settled farming communities during the Neolithic period.

Archaeological evidence from Epipalaeolithic sites provides valuable insights into the lives of these early human populations. Excavations have revealed evidence of dwellings, storage pits, and hearths, indicating the establishment of semi-permanent settlements. Artifacts such as pottery, bone tools, and personal ornaments have also been found, suggesting the development of more complex social and cultural practices.

Troubled insurance broker Marsh & McLennan is facing a formal investigation by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The SEC is looking into whether the company misled investors about the way it conducted business and the fees it charged clients.

The probe is the latest setback for Marsh, which has been struggling to recover from a scandal over the way it allegedly rigged bids for insurance contracts.

The company has already agreed to pay $850m (£470m) to settle civil charges brought by New York Attorney General Eliot Spitzer.

Mr Spitzer accused Marsh of taking kickbacks from insurers in return for steering business their way.

The SEC's investigation is at an early stage and it is not clear if any action will be taken against the company.

A Marsh spokesman said the company was co-operating with the SEC.

The SEC probe is the latest in a string of problems for Marsh, which is the world's largest insurance broker.

Last month, the company announced that it was axing 1,700 jobs, or 5% of its workforce, in a bid to cut costs.

And in October, Marsh ousted its chief executive, Jeffrey W. Greenberg, in an attempt to draw a line under the scandal.

Current deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) achieve top results in supervised medical image segmentation using diverse imaging types and applications. However, these networks can sometimes produce inaccurate segmentations, particularly around object edges, creating anomalies like gaps. Recent efforts aim to address this by adding spatial context or anatomical knowledge to improve segmentation plausibility. While incorporating prior information isn’t novel in traditional optimization methods, it's becoming increasingly common in CNN-based segmentation, evidenced by expanding research. This review concentrates on high-level priors integrated directly into the loss function, classifying papers by the type of prior—shape, size, topology, and inter-region relationships. It evaluates existing techniques, examines difficulties in designing and implementing prior losses, explores optimization methods, and proposes potential avenues for future study.

David Zimmer (born January 19, 1946) is a Canadian politician, who served in the Legislative Assembly of Ontario from 1995 to 2014 as a member of the Liberal Party. He served in the cabinet of Premiers Dalton McGuinty and Kathleen Wynne, and was the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario from 2014 to 2018.

Zimmer was born in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and raised in Toronto. He attended the University of Toronto, graduating with a bachelor's degree in Political Science and Economics in 1968. He later attended Osgoode Hall Law School, receiving an LL.B. in 1972. After graduating, he worked as a lawyer and became a partner in the firm of Goldblatt, Fryer, and Zimmer.

Zimmer was first elected to the Ontario legislature in the 1995 provincial election, defeating Progressive Conservative incumbent Bill Saunderson in the riding of Ottawa South. He was re-elected in the 1999, 2003, 2007, and 2011 provincial elections.

Zimmer served in a variety of cabinet positions in the government of Premier Dalton McGuinty. On January 18, 2001, he was appointed Minister of Intergovernmental Affairs. He held this position until September 25, 2001, when he was appointed Minister of Education. On February 25, 2003, he was also appointed Minister of Colleges and Universities. On November 25, 2003, he was appointed Minister of Health and Long-Term Care. On July 30, 2007, he was appointed Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

On February 4, 2008, Zimmer was elected as Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario by his peers. He served as Speaker until October 5, 2011, when he was appointed Minister of Environment.

Zimmer served as Minister of Environment until the defeat of the McGuinty government in the 2011 provincial election. The incoming Premier, Kathleen Wynne, appointed him as Minister of Aboriginal Affairs on February 11, 2013. On July 24, 2015, he was appointed Minister of Health and Long-Term Care.

Zimmer did not re-offer in the 2014 provincial election. After the election, he was elected Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario on November 5, 2014. He served as Speaker until 2018.

Using diffusion MRI, advanced white matter bundle segmentation relies on tractography combined with streamline cluster selection – a demanding process requiring significant computing power and intricate configuration alongside rigorous quality assurance. Traditional direct segmentation techniques frame this as standard image segmentation, though they haven’t yet achieved top results. However, they offer potential improvements.  We introduce a new supervised method for direct tract segmentation utilizing a stacked U-Net architecture, trained with manually segmented bundles from Human Connectome Project data. Our approach was tested both virtually and practically, employing the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge dataset, yielding human-level accuracy and substantial enhancements compared to existing workflows. The learned spatial information effectively guides segmentation, maintaining high precision even with degraded image quality.

The Almshouse is an historic almshouse located at 45 Matignon Road in Cambridge, Massachusetts.  It is now the site of the International School of Boston's main campus.  It was built in 1850 and is a prominent example of institutional residential architecture in stone, resembling prisons of the era.  The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982, where it is incorrectly listed at 41 Orchard Street. Description and history
The former Cambridge Almshouse is located in the northwestern corner of Cambridge, on the north side of Matignon Road between Matignon High School and the St. Sava Serbian Orthodox Church.  It is a large three-story stone structure with modest Greek Revival styling, set partly across the city line between Cambridge and Somerville.  It has a central octagonal administrative section from which four wings of varying sizes radiate.  It is built mostly out of slate blocks that were quarried from a ledge on site, with dressed dark granite corner quoining, and granite belt courses between the floors.  The rooflines are pierced by rows of gabled dormers.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Puree the bananas in a blender or food processor. In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine the 4 tbs. sugar and water. Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally, until sugar dissolves completely. Cook without stirring for an additional minute until mixture thickens slightly. Slowly stir in the banana puree and cook until mixture reaches a full boil. Remove from heat and stir in the cinnamon. Allow mixture to cool slightly in the refrigerator while you prepare the ramekins. Spray 4-6oz. ramekins with nonstick cooking spray and sprinkle sugar all over the bottom and sides. Spin ramekins around to coat completely and shake out any excess sugar. Put the egg whites and salt in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until white and foamy. Add the remaining 1 tbs. sugar and continue to beat, increasing the speed to medium-high, until stiff peaks form. Gently fold about one-third of the egg whites into the banana mixture. Continue to fold in the remaining egg whites. Divide souffle mixture evenly among the prepared ramekins and place them on a baking sheet. Bake for 14-16 minutes, or until tops have risen and browned lightly. Serve immediately.

In a medium bowl combine the chicken, 1 tablespoon of the oil, 1 teaspoon of the cornstarch, 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, and pepper. Stir to combine. In a small bowl combine the remaining 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch and 1/3 cup cold water. In another small bowl combine the paprika and cumin. Heat a 14-inch flat-bottomed wok over high heat until a bead of water vaporizes within 1 to 2 seconds of contact. Swirl in the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, add the onions, then, using a metal spatula, stir-fry 30 seconds or until the onions begin to wilt. Push the onions to the sides of the wok, carefully add the chicken, and spread it evenly in one layer in the wok. Cook undisturbed for 1 minute, letting the chicken begin to sear. Stir-fry 30 seconds or until the chicken is almost completely opaque. Add the ginger, garlic, and the paprika mixture, and stir-fry 1 minute or until the aromatics are fragrant and the chicken is well coated in the spices. Add the red and green bell peppers, reduce the heat to medium, and stir-fry 2 minutes or until the peppers begin to soften. (Do not be alarmed if the spices stick a little to the bottom of the wok.) Add the fish sauce, chilies, zucchini, and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, and stir-fry 1 minute or until almost all the liquid has evaporated. Despite recent successes in computer vision using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), applying them effectively to complex tasks like high-resolution image and video segmentation or 3D medical imaging faces challenges due to memory constraints during training. Specifically, storing network activations for backpropagation demands significant resources, often exceeding available hardware capacity, particularly in three dimensions. Inspired by signal propagation in physical networks described by the Telegraph equation, this research proposes a novel fully conservative hyperbolic network designed for high-dimensional inputs and outputs. It incorporates a coarsening technique utilizing a learnable Discrete Wavelet Transform to reversibly reduce the network’s complexity by altering channel numbers. Experiments demonstrate that these reversible networks match top-tier performance in 4D hyperspectral image segmentation and full 3D video segmentation while requiring substantially less memory – a fixed amount regardless of network depth. Furthermore, the approach is applied successfully to Variational Autoencoders processing high-resolution data.

This work offers a complete relativistic analysis of the galaxy counts seen at large distances, accounting for density fluctuations and redshift-space distortions alongside other relativistic influences. These shared effects stem from distortions within our cosmic coordinate system – specifically, the galaxy redshifts and photon directions – caused by unevenness in the universe’s distribution. We examine these relativistic impacts on both the angular power spectrum and the two-point correlation function. The latter proves particularly effective at revealing these effects due to its inherent reliance on the symmetry properties of the contributing components. We highlight how the Doppler shift and gravitational redshift distortions can be identified through searching for a dipole pattern in the cross-correlation between luminous and dim galaxies.

Segmenting sketches using semantic segmentation offers potential yet presents difficulties because of factors such as (i) the inherent variability in free-hand drawings stemming from diverse artistic styles and skill levels; (ii) distortions introduced by touchpads complicating recognition; and (iii) the substantial amount of labeled data required to train high-performing deep learning segmentation models. This research introduces the Sketch-target Deep FCN Segmentation Network (SFSegNet), designed for automated segmentation of free-hand sketches, assigning multiple parts to each individual sketch. SFSegNet employs an integrated end-to-end architecture consisting of two key components: (i) a refined Deep Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) incorporating a reweighting mechanism to suppress background noise and determine pixel classification; and (ii) affine transform encoders aimed at correcting distortions in sketched lines. The network was trained on a dataset of 10,000 annotated sketches to develop a robust model capable of accurately segmenting strokes based on their semantic content. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that SFSegNet surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in segmentation performance.

Fairfield is a borough in Adams County, Pennsylvania, United States. The population was 507 at the 2010 census. History
During the Gettysburg Campaign in the American Civil War, the Battle of Fairfield played an important role in securing the Fairfield pass and the Hagerstown Road,  enabling Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia to retreat through Fairfield towards the Potomac River. The actual fighting near Fairfield was between elements of the 6th United States Cavalry under Major Samuel Starr, and elements of General "Grumble" Jones' Brigade of Virginia Cavalry. The Union casualties were treated in the town of Fairfield, specifically in the homes of Mrs. Sarah Amanda Blythe, Rufus Christian Swope, and in what is now St. John's Lutheran Church. For more information on the town of Fairfield, see Fairfield In the Civil War, by Sarah Sites Thomas, Tim Smith, Gary Kross, and Dean S. Thomas.
The Fairfield Historic District and Fairfield Inn are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Recall him, consumed by passionate fervor,
Who deeply and hopelessly suffered:
Recount that perilous moment’s sway,
When both remained standing, despite their love’s way.
That yielding form, that gaze of melting grace,
Invited excess, an undeserved embrace;
That humble plea, that sorrowing sigh,
A bolder desire, restrained nearby.
Let me recall that all I forfeited,
Was saving you from conscience’s dread,
And blush at the pain it caused, unbefriended,
To stifle the regret of passing years instead.
Yet ponder this when tongues of judgment speak,
Accusing with words sharp and unkind,
That heart which cherished you, unjustly weak,
And tarnishing your reputation behind.
Remember how, whatever others see,
You have conquered every selfish thought within;
I still bless your spirit, presently,
Even in this solitary night begin.
Good Lord, if we’d met before despair,
With hearts entwined, your hand untainted free,
If you’d loved without committing care,
And I was worthy of your ecstasy!
May your future days escape this worldly show,
And that painful memory fade away,
May such trials cease to come and go,
And grant you peace beyond today.
This heart, corrupted long ago,
Might have perished there, destroying all it knew;
To find you in that dazzling flow,
Would kindle vanity’s hopeful hue.
So relinquish pleasures, joys, and pains,
Like mine, fleeting and utterly untrue,
Forsake those places where true feeling reigns,
Where those who suffer are destined to subdue.
Your youth, your beauty, warmth, and gentle art,
Your soul untouched by earthly, shadowed strife—
From all that happened here, discern the start
Of what awaits you beyond mortal life.
Forgive my tear, compelled by fervent plea,
Not born of virtue, but of passion’s fire,
They will not fall again, eternally,
For you, my love, they’ll nevermore retire.
Though lengthy grief must mark our parting fate,
The thought that we can never reunite—
I deserve the censure, truly great,
And almost welcome this condemning light.
However, had I loved you less profound,
My heart would offer less in sacrifice—
It felt a greater loss, tightly bound,
Than if your own distress had found its price.

Ingredients:
2 lbs mirabelle plums (about 20-25 plums)
2 cups sugar
1/2 cup fresh rosemary leaves
1/4 tsp kosher salt

Instructions:
1. Rinse the mirabelle plums and pat them dry with a paper towel. Remove the stems and cut the plums in half. Remove the pits.
2. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, combine the sugar, rosemary, and salt. Add the plums and stir to combine.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture has thickened and the plums have broken down, about 30-45 minutes.
4. Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture cool for 5 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
5. Transfer the jam to a clean jar and let it cool to room temperature. Cover and refrigerate for up to 1 month.

Anthony Meyer, a Conservative member of parliament who attempted to unseat Margaret Thatcher in 1989, passed away at the age of 84. He succumbed to cancer at his London residence. His unsuccessful leadership campaign facilitated Michael Heseltine’s subsequent attempt, ultimately leading to John Major’s ascension to Prime Minister following the second round of voting. Meyer lost his seat in Clwyd North West, which he’d held for over twenty years, due to the challenge. Born on October 27, 1920, Meyer attended Eton and New College, Oxford, and served with the Scots Guards during World War II, earning wounds in Normandy. After working under Edward Heath at the Foreign Office, he secured the Eton and Slough parliamentary seat in 1964 with a narrow victory. The Labour Party reclaimed the seat in 1966, and Meyer wouldn’t return to Parliament until 1970, consistently disagreeing with party directives.

Progress in generative modeling and adversarial learning has spurred considerable growth in image-to-image (I2I) translation research. Existing I2I methods typically demand either fully paired (supervised) or entirely unpaired (unsupervised) training images; however, acquiring substantial paired datasets is frequently difficult and expensive. Consequently, unsupervised approaches are generally favored despite their lower accuracy. This work seeks to combine the benefits of supervised and unsupervised I2I translation for semantic image segmentation. Leveraging established techniques like pix2pix and CycleGAN, we introduce a strategy for selecting just a small number of paired samples and demonstrate marked enhancements in both supervised and unsupervised I2I scenarios compared to random selection. Additionally, we improve results by integrating these selected paired examples alongside unpaired data during training. Results indicate that even a weakly supervised I2I system utilizing a single paired sample can outperform standard unsupervised CycleGAN and match the performance of supervised pix2pix trained on extensive paired data.

The exceptional Lie algebra E_7(-25), a crucial element in understanding supersymmetric gauge theories, is explored in this research. The study focuses on its representation theory, specifically addressing multiplets and invariant differential operators associated with it. By analyzing these elements of E_7(-25), an extensive overview of their properties contributes to enhancing our comprehension of related mathematical structures while providing valuable insights into applications within physics.

Semantic segmentation models trained on public datasets have achieved great
success in recent years. However, these models didn't consider the
personalization issue of segmentation though it is important in practice. In
this paper, we address the problem of personalized image segmentation. The
objective is to generate more accurate segmentation results on unlabeled
personalized images by investigating the data's personalized traits. To open up
future research in this area, we collect a large dataset containing various
users' personalized images called PIS (Personalized Image Semantic
Segmentation). We also survey some recent researches related to this problem
and report their performance on our dataset. Furthermore, by observing the
correlation among a user's personalized images, we propose a baseline method
that incorporates the inter-image context when segmenting certain images.
Extensive experiments show that our method outperforms the existing methods on
the proposed dataset. The code and the PIS dataset will be made publicly
available.

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs pork belly
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup wild huckleberries
- 1/4 cup honey
- 1/4 cup white wine vinegar
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 1 tbsp cornstarch

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 325°F.

2. Season the pork belly with salt and black pepper.

3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork belly and sear on all sides until browned.

4. Transfer the pork belly to a baking dish and place it in the oven. Bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until the pork is tender and the skin is crispy.

5. While the pork belly is cooking, prepare the wild huckleberry sauce. In a small saucepan, combine the huckleberries, honey, white wine vinegar, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.

6. In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp of water until smooth. Add the cornstarch mixture to the huckleberry sauce and stir until thickened.

7. Remove the pork belly from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing it. Serve with the wild huckleberry sauce.

Now that a critical mass of people have embraced digital TV, DVDs, and digital video recorders, the next revolution for TV is being prepared for our sets.
In most corners of TV and technology industries, high-definition (HDTV) is being heralded as the biggest thing to happen to the television since colour. HD essentially makes TV picture quality at least four times better than now. But there is real concern that people are not getting the right information about HD on the High Street. Thousands of flat panel screens - LCDs (liquid crystal displays), plasma screens, and DLP rear-projection TV sets - have already been sold as "HD", but are in fact not able to display HD.
"The UK is the largest display market in Europe," according to John Binks, director of GfK, which monitors global consumer markets.
But, he added: "Of all the flat panel screens sold, just 1.3% in the UK are capable of getting high-definition." There are 74 different devices that are being sold as HD but are not HD-ready, according to Alexander Oudendijk, senior vice president of marketing for satellite giant Astra. They may be fantastic quality TVs, but many do not have adaptors in them - called DVI or HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) connectors - which let the set handle the higher resolution digital images. Part of this is down to lack of understanding and training on the High Street, say industry experts, who gathered at Bafta in London for the 2nd European HDTV Summit last week. "We have to be careful about consumer confusion. There is a massive education process to go through," said Mr Binks. The industry already recognised that it would be a challenge to get the right information about it across to those of us who will be watching it. Eventually, that will be everyone. The BBC is currently developing plans to produce all its TV output to meet HDTV standards by 2010.
Preparations for the analogue switch-off are already underway in some areas, and programmes are being filmed with HD cameras. BSkyB plans to ship its first generation set-top boxes, to receive HDTV broadcasts, in time for Christmas. Like its Sky+ boxes, they will also be personal video recorders (PVRs). The company will start broadcasts of HDTV programmes, offering them as "premium channel packages", concentrating, to start with, on sports, big events, and films, in early 2006. But the set-top box which receives HDTV broadcasts has to plug into a display - TV set - that can show the images at the much higher resolution that HD demands, if HDTV is to be "real". By 2010, 20% of homes in the UK will have some sort of TV set or display that can show HD in its full glory.
But it is all getting rather confusing for people who have only just taken to "being digital". As a result, all the key players, those who make flat panel displays, as well as the satellite companies and broadcasters, formed a HD forum in 2004 to make sure they were all talking to each other. Part of the forum has been concerned with issues like industry standards and content protection. But it has also been preoccupied with how to help the paying public know exactly what they are paying for.
From next month, all devices that have the right connectors and resolution required will carry a "HD-Ready" sticker. This also means they are equipped to cope with both analogue and HDTV signals, and so comply with the minimum specification set out by the industry. "The logo is absolutely the way forward," said David Mercer, analysts with Strategy Analytics. "But it is still not appearing on many retail products." The industry is upbeat that the sticker will help, but it is only a start. "We can only do so much with the position we are in today with manufacturers," said Mr Oudendijk. "There may well be a number of dissatisfied customers in the next few months." The European Broadcast Union (EBU) is testing different flavours of HD formats to prepare for even better HDTV further down the line. It is similarly concerned that people get the right information on HDTV formats, as well as which devices will support the formats. "We believe consumers buying expensive displays need to ensure their investment is worthwhile," said Phil Laven, technical director for the EBU. The TV display manufacturers want us to watch HD on screens that are at least 42in (106cm), to get the "true impact" of HD, they say, although smaller displays suffice. What may convince people to spend money on HD-ready devices is the falling prices, which continue to tumble across Europe. The prices are dropping an average of 20% every year, according to analysts. LCD prices dropped by 43% in Europe as a whole last year, according to Mr Oudendijk.

Lawrence Sidney Eagleburger (born August 1, 1930, died June 4, 2011) was a prominent American diplomat and politician who held the position of Secretary of State for a short period during George H.W. Bush’s presidency from 1992 to 1993—the briefest such tenure in recent times. Prior to this, he worked in various roles under Presidents Nixon, Carter, and Reagan, including serving as Deputy Secretary of State alongside James Baker during Bush’s administration. Notably, Eagleburger remains the sole individual to have transitioned directly into the role of Secretary of State after a full career within the Foreign Service. His background included being raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, the child of Helen Eagleburger, an educator, and Leon Sidney Eagleburger, a physician. He received his early education at Jacobs High School in Stevens Point, followed by studies at Stevens Point State College (later the University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point), culminating in both bachelor’s and master’s degrees from the University of Wisconsin. While there, he became a member of the Alpha Sigma Phi fraternity.

Born in the 1870s or 1880s, Mussa Moloh is considered the final ruler of the Fuladu kingdom within the Senegambia area of Africa. He strategically allied himself with colonial forces to maintain control and suppress uprisings, a tactic that contributed to his eventual demise. The Fuladu kingdom originated from a revolt initiated by Mussa Moloh's father, Moloh Eggue – also called Alfa Moloh – against the prior Mandinka dominion over the Gambia River region. While the Mandinka retained authority over portions of their former territory within the new Fulbe state, the empire encompassed a remarkably varied population despite the general homogeneity of the Fulbe people. This diversity sparked internal conflicts for influence, prompting several groups to withdraw from the Fulbe state. Alfa Moloh’s primary support came from the Fulbe Firdu, numbering approximately 30,000 individuals, who established lasting communities in Tomari and Jimana—former Mandingo territories along the Gambia Valley. Ultimately, it was Mussa Moloh’s son who transformed the Fulbe realm into a fully-fledged state.

Quasi-power law ensembles are discussed from the perspective of nonextensive
Tsallis distributions characterized by a nonextensive parameter $q$. A number
of possible sources of such distributions are presented in more detail. It is
further demonstrated that data suggest that nonextensive parameters deduced
from Tsallis distributions functions $f\left(p_T\right)$, $q_1$, and from
multiplicity distributions (connected with Tsallis entropy), $q_2$, are not
identical and that they are connected via $q_1 + q_2 = 2$. It is also shown
that Tsallis distributions can be obtained directly from Shannon information
entropy, provided some special constraints are imposed. They are connected with
the type of dynamical processes under consideration (additive or
multiplicative). Finally, it is shown how a Tsallis distribution can
accommodate the log-oscillating behavior apparently seen in some multiparticle
data.

For this recipe, start with 10 ounces of bacon, cut into lardons. Heat olive oil in a large pot, then sauté the lardons until they’re browned and slightly crisp. Incorporate the bay leaf, diced potatoes, and remaining cauliflower florets; cook, stirring frequently, for approximately 5-7 minutes. FANet: A Feedback Attention Network for Improved Biomedical Image Segmentation

Background:
Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications, including disease diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep learning techniques have shown promising results in image segmentation tasks; however, their performance can be limited by the gap between the training data distribution and real-world scenarios. Moreover, the lack of interpretability in deep models hinders understanding the reasoning behind their predictions.

Objective:
To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework called FANet (Feedback Attention Network), which incorporates feedback attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and interpretability of biomedical image segmentation.

Methodology:
FANet consists of two main components: an encoder network and a feedback attention module. The encoder network follows a U-Net architecture with skip connections, designed to capture multi-scale contextual information. Each attention layer computes spatial attention maps to highlight relevant regions, allowing the model to refine its predictions based on the feedback received from previously generated outputs. We implement a self-gated mechanism that adaptively weights the importance of the attention signals, enabling the model to balance between local and global dependencies. Additionally, we introduce a routing strategy that directs the information flow across different attention layers, facilitating better feature representation and exchange.

Actor Daniel Day-Lewis is to be presented with an award for his career in film at the Berlin Film Festival.
The 47-year-old, whose credits include his Oscar-winning performance in My Left Foot, will be presented with the Berlinale Camera award on 15 February. The honour, awarded since 1986, honours figures in cinema that the festival feels "particularly indebted to". Man to Man, a historical epic starring Kristin Scott Thomas, opens the German festival on 10 February. A candid documentary about the life and career of singer George Michael, A Different Story will also be screened at the 10-day event. '
Day-Lewis has competed four times at the Berlin Film Festival, with films In The Name Of The Father (1994), The Crucible (1997), The Boxer (1998) and Martin Scorsese's Gangs Of New York (2003). The festival praises him for his "sensational start" with roles in My Beautiful Launderette and costume classic A Room With A View, and a "great number of celebrated roles" in subsequent productions. Japan's oldest film studio will also be honoured along with Day-Lewis. Shochiku film studios, which was founded 110 years ago, will become the first cinematic institution to receive the Berlinale Camera award. Famous Japanese directors including Akira Kurosawa have had films produced at the studio.

This seems to be Miyazake's most personal work, clearly a serious design. It is set in an imaginary time which blends the time of the ancient gods (Shinto style, gods of place and nature) with the settlement of humans and the coming of metalworking and war. The world is not in balance, and a distant conflict between industry and nature has wounded one of the gods of the forest, which is then killed by a sentry boy as it rampages into farmland he guards. The evil controlling it transfers to him, beginning a slow takeover, and he must journey to the origin of the conflict to find a way to cure himself and incidentally, as he will learn, to try to restore balance. But this is not a simplistic tale, he finds there are other characters in play, and there is good and evil in everyone, and no easy balance. The Princess (Hime) of the story is a mysterious human who has been raised by wolves (which are themselves powerful forest gods, a little reminiscent of the Amerindian Coyote myth), who becomes both his ally and his enemy. The story is not easy to understand. It has many Japanese mythic elements but even then, it is a work of Miyazake's unique imagination, and is not intended to be simple or to have a clean resolution.

The animation is spectacular, and unusual, with new elements even for Miyazake and marks a new departure for style which you can see continued in his next film, Sen to Chihiro - more nature, more wild, more jamming on elements from Japanese myth and folklore. And, continuing the trend to be more personal, concerned with ethics and character, and less sci-fi. There are at least half a dozen well developed characters threaded through the story, and their animation is wonderful in displaying subtle character.

The original Japanese soundtrack has some amazing singing and draws upon some of the best talent available for voices - in Japan, Miyazake is universally known and this was a masterpiece carefully crafted. Japanese television documented a lot of the production. The English translation drew on some good talent but they seem not to have "gotten it" quite so intensely as the Japanese crew.

If you haven't seen Miyazake, give it a try (but maybe look at Sen to Chihiro first, or even Laputa or Kiki's Delivery Service, for easier and lighter introduction to his work). Some say he is the Japanese Disney, but I don't like that. His work has a depth and sophistication that goes beyond Disney cute. There is no other animation like it. This is truly an adult work: children might like some of the visuals, but I doubt that many kids below teen age will have any idea what it is all about, and even adults will get more out of this each time you see it again.

Born in Manhattan on November 19, 1906, Georgia E. Engelhard Cromwell (1906-1986) was a prominent American mountaineer who achieved significant feats in the Canadian Rockies, the Selkirk, and Purcell mountain ranges. She holds the distinction of being the first woman to summit numerous peaks within these areas and was widely recognized as the foremost female amateur climber of her era. Beyond her climbing accomplishments, Cromwell was a skilled painter and photographer. Her family background included connections to influential figures: she was the child of a lawyer, George Engelhard, and Agnes Stieglitz, and a niece of renowned photographer Alfred Stieglitz and artist Georgia O’Keeffe—a key figure in American modernism. Due to name conflicts, she often went by “The Kid” or “Georgia Minor,” and occasionally served as a subject for Stieglitz’s photography, including nude studies. The pair maintained a close relationship and exchanged frequent letters throughout her adolescence and young adulthood.

> Kennekuk was a Native American chief who lived in Illinois during the 18th century, and whose name has been given to several places throughout central Illinois. He was born around 1720 near present-day Peoria, Illinois, and died sometime after 1795. His father's name was Kishkequa (or Keeshkequa), which means "the one with the long hair." His mother's name was Wahpeekanaka ("she who weeps").
>
> In his youth he became known as a great warrior, but later turned away from warfare and devoted himself to peacemaking. He married a woman named Pawheecheka ("she who laughs"), and they had two sons, Tapouyee ("little bear") and Chicagou ("big river").
>
> During the French and Indian War, Kennekuk fought on the side of the British against the French. After the war ended, he helped negotiate peace between the various tribes living in what would become Illinois. He also worked to establish good relations with white settlers moving into the area.
>
> One of Kennekuk's most important contributions was his role in establishing Fort Clark at the confluence of the Sangamon River and the Illinois River. This fort served as a key trading post for many years, and played an important part in opening up central Illinois to settlement by whites.
>
> Kennekuk continued to work for peace until his death sometime after 1795. He is buried on a hill overlooking the site where Fort Clark once stood. A monument marks his grave today.

According to Belgian officials, US Open winner Svetlana Kuznetsova has returned a positive test for the banned stimulant ephedrine, detected on December 19th during an exhibition match in Charleroi. Sports Minister Claude Eerdekens confirmed the finding, stating that Kuznetsova’s innocence must be established through further testing – a B sample has yet to be analyzed.  Kuznetsova herself had previously dismissed concerns, claiming she hadn't used any performance-enhancing substances and was surprised by the timing of the announcement. The test was conducted by local Belgian authorities, not under the auspices of WADA, ITF, or WTA.  Eerdekens indicated that notification of the result was sent to Kuznetsova, Spanish authorities, Belgian prosecutors, and both the Belgian and Russian tennis federations last Friday. While acknowledging the possibility of unintentional contamination within a medication, he emphasized that the relevant federations will determine appropriate sanctions.  However, Russian tennis head Shamil Tarpishchev strongly criticized Eerdekens for publicly identifying Kuznetsova before conclusive evidence existed.

2 medium lemons
2 cups unbleached all-purpose flour
1 3/4 cups sugar
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1 1/3 cups extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/4 cups 2% milk
3 large eggs
1/4 cup limoncello
butter for the pan
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Put out the milk, eggs and limoncello to warm up somewhat (room temperature is ideal) while you prepare the lemons and while the oven preheats. Zest the two lemons; you should end up with about 1 1/2 tablespoons of zest. Then juice one of the lemons which should yield approximately 1/4 of juice. Set aside. Prepare the cake pan: butter it, cover the bottom with parchment paper, and butter the paper also. You will be baking a relatively liquid batter so you want a pan that's at least 2" high. I used a spring-form pan which worked well. In a medium bowl whisk together the dry ingredients -- the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Using a stand mixer with the whisk attached, mix together the wet ingredients: the lemon zest and juice, the olive oil, limoncello, eggs and milk. With the whisk running on slow speed, add your dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in a slow but steady stream until just combined. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and bake for an hour, or until done. When done the cake with have a golden honey brown top in its center, and a cake tester inserted in the middle of the cake will come out clean. Place the cake on a wire rack for 30 minutes. At the end of that time, run a thin knife around the edge of the cake to ensure that it will come out cleanly, and invert on to another wire rack. Now remove the parchment paper from the bottom of the cake, and using another wire rack, turn the cake upside down so that it is again top-side up and let it cool completely, which will take about 2 hours. Once completely cool, the cake is ready to be iced or frosted, as you wish, or served plain as is. My family likes it served just with fresh berries (blueberries and raspberries in particular) and a dollop of whipped cream. This moist cake keeps well for several days when wrapped up and stored at room temperature.

This paper investigates the generation of linear and non-linear Alfvén waves in the coronal funnels through impulsive energy release processes. The authors conducted numerical simulations to study the dynamics and characteristics of these waves, focusing on how they interact and propagate in the coronal structures. It was found that impulsive events can generate both linear and non-linear Alfvén waves, with the latter exhibiting strong nonlinearities and wave steepening effects. The simulations also revealed that the generated waves can transport energy and momentum from the energy release site to distant regions of the funnel, which could have significant implications for coronal heating and solar wind acceleration. These findings provide new insights into the complex wave dynamics in the solar corona and can contribute to our understanding of fundamental physical processes occurring in this highly dynamic environment.

Recent decades have seen the discovery of numerous complex materials. At the
root of the complexity underlying many of these materials lies a large number
of possible contending atomic- and larger-scale configurations and the
intricate correlations between their constituents. For a detailed
understanding, there is a need for tools that enable the detection of pertinent
structures on all spatial and temporal scales. Towards this end, we suggest a
new method by invoking ideas from network analysis and information theory. Our
method efficiently identifies basic unit cells and topological defects in
systems with low disorder and may analyze general amorphous structures to
identify candidate natural structures where a clear definition of order is
lacking. This general unbiased detection of physical structure does not require
a guess as to which of the system properties should be deemed as important and
may constitute a natural point of departure for further analysis. The method
applies to both static and dynamic systems.

Blueberry Muffins Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 cup buttermilk
- 1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a muffin tin with paper liners or grease it lightly with cooking spray.
2. In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
3. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
4. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.
5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, alternating with the buttermilk. Begin and end with the dry ingredients, mixing just until incorporated.
6. Gently fold in the fresh blueberries, being careful not to crush them.
7. Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, filling each cup about 2/3 full.
8. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
9. Remove the muffins from the oven and allow them to cool in the tin for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
10. Enjoy your homemade blueberry muffins plain, or you can top them with a sprinkle of powdered sugar, a drizzle of glaze, or a dollop of whipped cream. Serve and enjoy with a hot cup of coffee or tea!

To function effectively in cells and advanced diagnostics, biochemical receptors must detect minute alterations in signaling molecule concentrations. However, the precision of these signals is constrained by the background interference caused by molecular thermal movement. Frequently, large molecules and cell components temporarily attach to mobile transporters and are subsequently moved around. This study demonstrates that randomly but purposefully delivering signaling molecules close enough to a receptor lowers the timescale of counting fluctuations, thereby enhancing sensing accuracy. These findings align with what’s seen in real-life cells and offer insights into cellular signaling processes and the development of new diagnostic tools.

Located in Glenbrook, within the City of Blue Mountains local government area of New South Wales, Australia, the Lennox Bridge – also called The Horseshoe Bridge – is a historically significant road crossing over Brookside Creek (formerly Lapstone Creek). Designed by David Lennox and constructed between 1832 and 1833 by James Randall and convict laborers, this heritage-listed stone arch bridge remains standing today, owned by Blue Mountains City Council. It was officially registered on the New South Wales State Heritage Register on April 2, 1999.

Prior to its construction, the initial road up the Blue Mountains’ eastern slopes, established by William Cox in 1814-15, proved problematic due to frequent washouts. This was subsequently replaced by the Bathurst Road (now Old Bathurst Road) in 1824, though its steep gradient posed ongoing dangers. Following Major Thomas Mitchell’s appointment as Surveyor General in 1828, he prioritized improving the Great Western Road, advocating for a more direct and less challenging route than the existing road, which required constant maintenance. He proposed building a new road in between the previous routes instead of relying solely on repairs.

Automatic Spine Segmentation using Convolutional Neural Network via Redundant Generation of Class Labels for 3D Spine Modeling

We present a novel approach to segment the spine of a 3D model using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a novel classifier. We use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate a set of class labels for each segment of the spine. We then use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to segment the segmented spine into the segments that are labeled by the class labels. We show that the segmented spine can be automatically segmented using the segmented spine classifier. We also show that the segmented spine classifier can be used to automatically segment the spine of a 3D model.

Min-cut clustering, based on minimizing one of two heuristic cost-functions
proposed by Shi and Malik, has spawned tremendous research, both analytic and
algorithmic, in the graph partitioning and image segmentation communities over
the last decade. It is however unclear if these heuristics can be derived from
a more general principle facilitating generalization to new problem settings.
Motivated by an existing graph partitioning framework, we derive relationships
between optimizing relevance information, as defined in the Information
Bottleneck method, and the regularized cut in a K-partitioned graph. For fast
mixing graphs, we show that the cost functions introduced by Shi and Malik can
be well approximated as the rate of loss of predictive information about the
location of random walkers on the graph. For graphs generated from a stochastic
algorithm designed to model community structure, the optimal information
theoretic partition and the optimal min-cut partition are shown to be the same
with high probability.

For this dish inspired by Pastis in New York City, start by heating a pot of water to boiling. Simultaneously, butter a baking sheet and broil halved English muffins until they’re lightly golden. Poach four whole eggs – create a whirlpool in the boiling water and gently introduce them one at a time. Meanwhile, melt 1 ½ sticks of butter in a saucepan until it sizzles. Blend the egg yolks with the melted butter, gradually adding it in a slow stream while maintaining a constant blend; finish by incorporating lemon juice and cayenne pepper. Arrange the toasted English muffin halves on a plate, topping each with a piece of smoked salmon and a poached egg. Drizzle generously with Hollandaise sauce and season with black pepper. For optimal temperature, briefly return the poached eggs to the hot water right before serving, and prepare the Hollandaise immediately prior to plating.

British Airways will discontinue its flights between London Heathrow and Saudi Arabian cities Jeddah and Riyadh starting March 27th, citing decreased passenger interest. The airline presently offers four weekly flights to Jeddah and three to Riyadh. Following a governmental concern regarding potential risks to British aviation in Saudi Arabia during autumn 2003, they previously paused operations for three weeks. Despite a longstanding connection between the UK and Saudi Arabia, BA’s director of commercial planning, Robert Boyle, acknowledged that these routes aren't financially viable at present. Flights will be continually assessed for future resumption, and passengers holding reservations beyond the suspension date will be informed about revised travel options.

Sandvine cautions that rising interest in online gaming poses challenges for internet service companies, citing a dramatic increase in traffic related to the Xbox game network’s launch of Halo 2. Following a fourfold spike on November 9th, this heavy traffic has persisted through December, highlighting the urgent need for improved network capacity. Halo 2’s popularity, alongside its connection to Microsoft’s Xbox Live subscription service, allows players to form clans and compete online. According to Sandvine CTO Marc Morin, this surge represents a critical alert for the industry, demanding enhanced network infrastructure capable of handling increased demand. Providers are implementing strategies like network intelligence – identifying bandwidth usage – and potentially introducing tiered pricing. Morin emphasized that ISPs should prioritize bandwidth for gaming to combat “lag,” a frustrating delay impacting online gameplay, and retain gamers seeking low latency connections. Analyst Lindsay Schroth from The Yankee Group notes that effective bandwidth management will be vital for broadband operators competing in a demanding market, urging them to tailor services specifically for live-play gaming experiences.

The fear the old man anticipates manifests with terrifying clarity when the young man discovers the mannequin and utilizes it as a centerpiece in a neighborhood Guy Fawkes Night bonfire. Now, this once respectable man must venture out seeking victims beyond a lifeless form.

Recent advances in deep learning based image segmentation methods have
enabled real-time performance with human-level accuracy. However, occasionally
even the best method fails due to low image quality, artifacts or unexpected
behaviour of black box algorithms. Being able to predict segmentation quality
in the absence of ground truth is of paramount importance in clinical practice,
but also in large-scale studies to avoid the inclusion of invalid data in
subsequent analysis.
  In this work, we propose two approaches of real-time automated quality
control for cardiovascular MR segmentations using deep learning. First, we
train a neural network on 12,880 samples to predict Dice Similarity
Coefficients (DSC) on a per-case basis. We report a mean average error (MAE) of
0.03 on 1,610 test samples and 97% binary classification accuracy for
separating low and high quality segmentations. Secondly, in the scenario where
no manually annotated data is available, we train a network to predict DSC
scores from estimated quality obtained via a reverse testing strategy. We
report an MAE=0.14 and 91% binary classification accuracy for this case.
Predictions are obtained in real-time which, when combined with real-time
segmentation methods, enables instant feedback on whether an acquired scan is
analysable while the patient is still in the scanner. This further enables new
applications of optimising image acquisition towards best possible analysis
results.

To make this cranberry brie tartlets, start by mixing 1 1/2 cups of sugar and 1 cup of cranberry juice in a saucepan and bringing it to a boil, stirring until the sugar is dissolved. Then, add the 4 cups of fresh cranberries, 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts, 1/2 cup of currants, 1/4 cup of orange juice, 2 tablespoons of cider vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon of ground ginger, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Simmer the mixture, uncovered, for 5 minutes until it thickens. Let it cool completely – it will continue to set up as it cools. Lay one sheet of thawed phyllo pastry on a damp towel, brushing it with melted butter, followed by two more sheets, also brushed with butter. Reserve the remaining three sheets, keeping them covered to prevent drying. Cut the layered phyllo into six squares, placing a piece of Brie cheese in the center of each. Gently gather the corners of the phyllo around the Brie and twist to form bundles. Arrange the bundles on a greased baking sheet. Repeat this process with the remaining phyllo, butter, and Brie. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 13 minutes, or until golden brown. Serve warm with cranberry chutney on individual plates. Leftover chutney pairs well with roasted meats like chicken, pork, or ham.

So who, if anyone, is playing politics with the security of the nation?
Michael Howard has no doubt it is the prime minister who, he claims, is "ramming" through Parliament the controversial new anti-terror measures without proper debate. He didn't say so, but the Tories believe the prime minister is playing the fear card on this one so he can look tough in the run up to the general election And they believe Tony Blair is using the issue to suggest the Tories are soft on terrorism. Why on earth will the prime minister not simply take up the Tories' offer to extend the existing powers temporarily to allow proper parliamentary debate of the laws, he demanded. The prime minister claims this is the clearest indication that it is the Tories who are playing politics with the issue by attempting to score cheap political points in parliament. Is not the opposition against to the proposed laws "in principle", in which case delaying a decision for further debate would be pointless?
What this is really about, believes Mr Blair, is the Tories spotting an opportunity to embarrass, maybe even defeat the government. And that is more important to them than national security. Liberal Democrat leader Charles Kennedy avoided suggesting anyone was playing politics with the issue. He preferred to state that, as with other issues like ID cards, the government's immediate instinct was authoritarian.
As is his habit nowadays, the prime minister was less rough with Mr Kennedy than he had been with Mr Howard - he prefers a more exasperated tone suggesting he believes the Lib Dems have, once again, just missed the point. Apart from all that, it was electioneering as usual. The very first question to the prime minister from Derby North's Bob Laxton asked him, in effect, if he would carry on the excellent policy of pouring more resources into schools. Later Birmingham's Sion Simon even went so far as to suggest the Tories were such a shower that we should have the general election now. The prime minister almost blushed. This was not the appropriate place to announce election day, he stammered. But can anyone be in any doubt that that announcement is just days away - an announcement coming in the week beginning 4 April for an election on 5 May is where the big money is in the Commons. And perhaps that simple fact alone means everyone is seen to be playing politics with just about everything at the moment.

We derive the general 5-dimension metric structure of the $Dp-Dq$ system in
type II superstring theory, and demonstrate the physical meaning of the
parameters characterizing the 5-dimension metric structure of the
\textit{holographic} QCD model by relating them to the parameters describing
Regge trajectories. By matching the spectra of vector mesons $\rho_1$ with
deformed $Dp-Dq$ soft-wall model, we find that the spectra of vector mesons
$\rho_1$ can be described very well in the soft-wall $D3-Dq$ model, i.e,
$AdS_5$ soft-wall model. We then investigate how well the $AdS_5$ soft-wall
model can describe the Regge trajectory of axial-vector mesons $a_1$. We find
that the constant component of the 5-dimension mass square of axial-vector
mesons plays an efficient role to realize the chiral symmetry breaking in the
vacuum, and a small negative $z^4$ correction in the 5-dimension mass square is
helpful to realize the chiral symmetry restoration in high excitation states.

1 whole 6-8 Pound Pork Butt (estimate 1 Hour Per Pound To Smoke)
1 cup Mango Nectar Or Apple Juice- For Injecting Into The Meat To Keep It Moist And Juicy
2 Tablespoons Olive Oil
1 container Your Favorite BBQ Rub, For Sprinkling
1 cup Mango Nectar
1/4 cups Guava Preserves
3 Tablespoons Lime Juice
1 Tablespoon Lime Zest
3 Tablespoons Honey
1 whole Jalapeno Pepper, Finely Chopped With Seeds
2 teaspoons Minced Fresh Ginger
Prepare your grill to 250 degrees F. Soak a fruit wood such as apple or peach for 30 minutes and then throw the wood chunks into your grill that is at 250 degrees. The wood is to create the smoke that will infuse the pork with great smoky flavor. Next, slice the fat layer on the top of the meat in a cross hatch direction so as to create cubes of fat on top of the meat (see picture). This is going to help get more rub rubbed in to the butt. Next, inject the meat liberally with the mango nectar or you can use apple juice or juice of your preference. Slather the pork butt with olive oil, and then generously rub the butt all over with your favorite BBQ rub. Place the pork butt (fat side up) on the grates of your grill or Egg with a piece of foil underneath to catch the juices. Make sure to also have the place setter in place as we are cooking indirect. (An Egg uses a place setter to cook indirectly.) For a regular grill, if you are smoking at 250 degrees, I recommend just wrapping the pork with foil all over so that the pork never comes into contact with the grill. (A regular grill will not use a placesetter). Meanwhile, combine all of you Mango BBQ sauce ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a simmer. After simmering for 5 minutes, remove from heat and divide into two bowls. (One bowl is for basting, the other one will be for serving with the meat for sandwiches.) Periodically baste the pork with one bowl of the BBQ sauce as it is cooking. Smoke the meat for up to 8 hours (estimate 1 hour per pound of meat) or until the internal temperature reaches 180 degrees F. Then it is ready to be pulled off of the grill. If you have the time, you can smoke longer at a lower temp 225F, but 250F worked fine for me. After you pull the meat off of the grill, let it rest under foil for 10 minutes. Then you are ready to pull it with a fork. You will shred the pork with a fork and it will be perfect for a sandwich or tortilla for pork sliders or tacos. I made sliders paired with my chipotle cilantro coleslaw and sweet potato fries. For the BBQ sauce: Combine all of the sauce ingredients in a sauce pan over medium heat and let it simmer for 20 minutes. Serve with your sliders.

Abstract:

Unsupervised pathology image segmentation is a challenging task that requires identifying regions of interest in medical images without the need for manual labeling or prior knowledge of the disease being present. Representation learning, which has emerged as a powerful tool in deep learning, has shown promising results in this domain by learning a low-dimensional representation of the input images that can be used for clustering and classification. In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised approach to pathology image segmentation using representation learning with spherical k-means clustering. Our approach is based on training a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn a representation of the input images by training the network in a self-supervised manner. We then use the learned representation to cluster the images into regions of interest using spherical k-means clustering. The performance of our approach is evaluated on a benchmark dataset of lung tissue specimens and shows significant improvement over state-of-the-art methods. Our work contributes to existing research on unsupervised pathology image segmentation by providing a novel approach that leverages the strengths of representation learning and clustering techniques for accurate and efficient segmentation.

Across the verdant hills of Wyre, the train sped past, shifting landscapes as it went,
And in the distant west, Clee’s peak slowly disappeared, my hand resting weightlessly upon my knee.
It bore a deep ache, that morning almost halfway across a county,
Having been gripped countless times by strong, honest hands.
“Hand,” I thought, “since our paths diverge from familiar fields and comrades,
To unfamiliar faces and foreign soil—hand, you’ve known loyal companions.”
“Cleanse yourself then,” I urged, “and let nothing dishonorable come from you,
Let us avoid disgrace in London’s bustling streets, proclaiming our Shropshire origin.
They mustn’t whisper along the banks of the Thames that the Severn produces harsher characters than those we leave behind.
Our friends overseas should remember the bonds we forged here at home.
I will become distant and numb when I lose sight of you, dear friends,
And the place where I’ll cease to think of you is the place where memories fade.
Should my feet never again tread the shores of the Teme, Corve, or Severn,
May fortune attend you always by flowing rivers and steadfast hills,
By church bells and rustling trees – the men who shaped my life.
You’ll shield my memory in town and on the farm,
And guide me safely, these hands that brought me friendship until death.

Gentle Homebody, tranquil Soul,
You’ve known no distant land’s control;
Your heart has never swayed with tide,
Nor tasted ocean breezes wide.
You haven’t journeyed to India’s shore,
Where fragrant winds forever pour.
You’ve lacked the sight of vineyards vast,
Stretching onward, holding fast;
Nor witnessed summer evenings bright,
With maiden’s sewing by candlelight;
Nor watched the North Sea’s springtime hue,
Like fleeting birds in icy blue.
You haven’t observed dark hands at work,
Picking white cotton, a floral perk,
Nor heard melodious voices blend,
Or rested where ancient boulders end,
Once towering high, now flat and low—
Gentle Homebody, sweet, serene flow,
You lack the sights that fill life’s grace,
A quiet beauty in this place.
Bless your peaceful, lovely face,
For kindness nurtures you with space;
My affection lies within your core,
More than in wisdom to explore.

If someone had nudged me about 15 minutes into 'Ray' and asked what I thought of Jamie Foxx in the title role, it would have been time for a blank stare. After all, what is this (fictitious) person talking' about? That wasn't Jamie Foxx up on the big screen. That was Ray Charles. This is one of the best performances by anybody in recent years. Like the soundtrack, Jamie as Ray is flat-out brilliant.

The blind Genius of Soul (who took a revolutionary step of mixing gospel with R&B) died during production. The movie about his troubled life is good, not great. Taylor Hackford's direction and James L. White's script follow the well-worn biopic outline. Super-talented youngster battles adversity, achieves greatness while also self-destructing, then picks himself up out of the gutter for a happy ending. The film shows Charles' flaws (heroin abuse, chronic womanizing, persistent bastard-fathering) even as it sucks you in with his beautiful music.

Kerry Washington and Regina King play the main women in Ray's life, one his long-suffering wife and the other his longtime mistress. Both actresses match Foxx stride for stride. What takes him to a different level, though, is his deep understanding and uncanny impersonation of the great musician. The entire cast is effective, especially Sharon Warren as his headstrong mother and Curtis Armstrong as a music exec. Hackford's stars are likely to be rewarded with trophies and---better yet---more starring roles.

I was not a Ray Charles aficionado before 'Ray'. Apparently, the film has left out a lot (as do all biopics), but this picture functions as both an old-fashioned crowd pleaser AND a dark investigation of a brilliant/troubled man. For those who whine that Foxx doesn't actually sing (as if that somehow diminishes his performance), take a hike. No mere actor can sing like Mr. Charles anyway. You can't have everything. What the talented star does in this picture is about as close to "everything" as we'll probably see for a while.

Image quality relies heavily on both color and brightness levels; clusters of pixels with matching colors or intensities provide valuable information for computer vision applications like identifying salient areas and suggesting potential objects. Yet, real-world colors can be altered by variations in brightness, leading to discrepancies between pixel values. This work revisits affinity matrices from traditional spectral clustering techniques for image segmentation, creating a new, color-distortion-resistant matrix designed for object identification. We also develop a Cohesion Measurement (CM) based on this improved matrix to quantify the unity of object regions. Utilizing this CM, a new object discovery approach is presented, leveraging eigenvector analysis to uncover hidden objects within images.  This method’s effectiveness was validated through experiments on standard datasets, showing significant improvements in saliency detection and object proposal generation.

1 medium, firm eggplant
1 clove garlic, cracked away from the skin
2 pinches ground allspice
Coarse salt and black pepper
1 handful flat-leaf parsley tops
A drizzle extra-virgin olive oil
1 whole grain baguette or other long crusty bread, sliced at bread counter
Preheat oven to highest setting, at least 500 degrees F. Cut 2 or 3 slits into whole eggplant. Place eggplant directly on the oven rack in the middle of the oven and roast the eggplant until it is tender, about 20 minutes. Keep the slits facing up so that the eggplant does not loose liquids as it roasts. The roasted eggplant will look like a flat tire when you remove it from the oven. Using a sharp utility knife, carefully peel skin away from eggplant flesh. Add cooked eggplant flesh and juice to food processor and combine with garlic, allspice, salt, and pepper and parsley. Pulse grind the eggplant into a paste, add a drizzle of olive oil. Transfer to a serving dish. The seeds of the eggplant will make the spread resemble caviar eggs, and so the name: poor man's caviar. To serve, surround a bowlful of spread with crusty bread rounds. Tidbit: Mixed olives and selections of Italian sheep's milk cheeses are suggested accompaniments to this menu to round out your buffet. They require no recipe or preparation and add something to the offering overall. Place them on the buffet near the eggplant caviar and bread.

Nils Holgersson, a young boy whose primary pleasures were eating, sleeping, and causing trouble, frequently tormented the animals on his family’s farm. He captures a tomte in a net during church when left alone to study the Bible. The tomte offers Nils a golden coin if he releases him, but Nils refuses, leading to Nils transforming into a tomte himself – a small, talking creature surrounded by furious and vengeful animals. Simultaneously, a domestic goose tries to join a migrating flock of wild geese, and Nils clings to its neck as it escapes, embarking on a journey through Sweden’s historical regions alongside them. This adventure allows Nils to grow into a responsible individual; he must demonstrate his worthiness to the geese, mirroring the goose's own struggle to match their flight skills. Throughout the voyage, Nils discovers that demonstrating positive change could potentially restore him to his human form. The narrative intertwines with several related stories, such as one focusing on a solitary young man in Stockholm who connects with an elderly resident learning about the city’s past—only to realize that the gentleman was actually the Swedish king.

Wife Swap makers sue US 'copycat'

The makers of the hit UK reality TV show Wife Swap are suing an American company, claiming it copied their idea.

RDF Media, which makes Wife Swap for Channel 4, says ABC's Wife Swap "brazenly copied" the programme.

It says the US version, which started in 2004, is "strikingly similar" to Wife Swap and is seeking unspecified damages.

ABC has not yet commented on the lawsuit, filed in a federal court in Los Angeles.

The British version of Wife Swap was first broadcast in 2003 and sees two mothers swap lives for two weeks.

'Substantial copying'

RDF says the US programme - which has similar rules and is shot in a similar style - breaches copyright and trade mark law.
