Ernest Leslie Konnyu (born May 17, 1937) is an American businessman and former Republican U.S. Representative from Silicon Valley, California, 12th congressional district, serving one term from 1987 to 1989. He had previously been a California State Assembly Member from the 22nd district, serving from 1980 to 1986. Early life
Ernõ "Ernie" Könnyű was born May 17, 1937, in Tamási, Kingdom of Hungary (present-day Tamási, Hungary) to poet, professor and cartographer Leslie Konnyu and his wife, Elizabeth, a bookkeeper and owner of a home secretarial school, and is the eldest of his two late siblings Gabriela (Helen) and Zoltan (Joseph). In 1949 the 12-year-old Konnyu, together with his family, immigrated to the United States from a post-World War II refugee camp in Ampflwang, Austria. He attended parochial and public schools in Jefferson City and St. Louis, Missouri. He attended University of Maryland, College Park and received his Bachelor of Science degree from Ohio State University in 1965. Konnyu served in the United States Air Force as a captain from 1959 to 1969 and as a major in the Air Force Reserve from 1970 to 1981. In 1959, he married Lillian Muenks of Loose Creek, Missouri.

To make this dessert, you’ll need 3 cups of self-rising flour, 50g of cold, diced butter, 1 1/4 cups of milk, 125g of high-quality milk chocolate (diced), and 2 (55g) Cherry Ripe chocolate bars (also diced). Preheat your oven to 200°C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Begin by sifting the flour into a large bowl; incorporate the butter, rubbing it in until the mixture has the texture of coarse breadcrumbs – you can also use a food processor for this step. Create a well in the center and gradually add the milk, mixing until a soft dough forms. Lightly dust a surface and knead briefly until smooth. Roll the dough out into a 30cm x 40cm rectangle, ensuring the shorter side is nearest to you. Melt the chocolate in a small, microwave-safe bowl at medium power (50%) for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently until smooth. Spread the melted chocolate evenly over the dough, leaving a 2cm border along the longer edge. Sprinkle the Cherry Ripes across the chocolate. Roll the dough tightly from the shorter end closest to you, forming a Swiss roll. Trim the ends with a knife and slice the roll into 9 equal pieces. Arrange the slices on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2cm apart. Bake for 25 minutes, or until they are lightly golden. Let them cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before carefully separating them. Serve warm.

Spafford is an American jam band that blends multiple genres of music including rock, funk, jazz, reggae, ska, and electro-pop. Members Brian Moss (guitar/vocals) and Jordan Fairless (bass/vocals) formed Spafford in Prescott, Arizona on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “Red” Johnson (keys/vocals) joined Moss and Fairless after meeting the duo at an open mic night. Nick Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined shortly after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The group self-releases its recordings, including studio albums, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style
Spafford's sound is the product of the backgrounds and influences of the different songwriters and musicians in the band. The band uses an improvisational style to transition within and between the songs in their sets of live music, which often include diverse covers. Spafford tours across the U.S., and each of their shows features a different setlist and approach to the songs in their catalogue of original music. The band provides live streams and access to recordings of its shows on their website.

Looking back on my youth brings me immense nostalgia. I recall it fully, embracing both its challenges and joys. It’s amusing how adults yearn for their younger days, while children strive for maturity and strength. Girls desired womanhood quickly, and boys sought manhood swiftly, often before mastering basic skills. Those were simpler times, marked by minimal wrongdoing and abundant laughter – we entertained ourselves with hardly any money. It’s quite a poetic thought, isn't it? My mother frequently called us for sweets and treats as we engaged in playful activities and learned through our errors. We eagerly headed to school, anticipating mischievous schemes. I was generally considerate and respectful, though I fondly remember being captivated by bedtime stories from my parents and gazing at the distant night sky. Like the excitement of holidays—Christmas and Easter—I treasured gifts, especially those small ones that brightened someone's day. My mother consistently emphasized this sentiment. I also cherished explorations within the forest.  My memories encompass everything included and excluded, and even now, certain aspects remain puzzling. 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs
6 Toulouse sausages (depending on the size of chook the thighs came from) or 6 chipolata sausages (depending on the size of chook the thighs came from)
250 g streaky bacon (6 or 12 rashers depending on how cut) or 250 g pancetta (6 or 12 rashers depending on how cut)
200 g orange duck pate
Preheat oven to 180C (350F). Cover a (rolled out) chicken thigh with a couple of pieces of cling film and clobber until flattened / slightly larger surface area (until the width of the chicken is about the same as the length of the sausage). Take a rasher/slice of bacon/pancetta and lay out on a copping board - if using streaky bacon you may need to run the back of a knife across it to make it wider and longer. Or you may need to use 2 rashers per thigh, depending on the product. Lay a boned thigh on the bacon (outside to the bacon, where the bone was, facing up). Spread 1/6 of the pate into the centre half of the thigh. Place a sausage across the pate and roll up tightly, ensuring that the bacon ends overlap each other over the 'join'. (You may need to secure with toothpicks). Repeat for the other 5 thighs. Place roulades on a tray/oven-proof dish and bake for 20-30 minutes or until browned and juices run clear. Remove from the oven and leave to stand for 5-10 minutes. Slice each roulade into 1cm thick slices and serve.

Recent advancements in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) have led to impressive results in complex visual recognition like image classification and object detection.  This research integrates DCNN techniques with probabilistic graphical models to tackle pixel-wise image segmentation – also known as semantic segmentation. Our findings indicate that the outputs from DCNN’s last layer lack sufficient spatial precision for effective object delineation, stemming from the networks’ inherent robustness. To address this limitation, we integrate the DCNN’s response with a Conditional Random Field (CRF). The resulting “DeepLab” system demonstrates superior boundary localization compared to existing approaches, achieving a new state-of-the-art 71.6% Intersection over Union (IOU) accuracy on the PASCAL VOC-2012 dataset. Furthermore, we detail an efficient implementation utilizing strategic network modification and a specialized ‘hole’ algorithm adapted from wavelet processing, enabling computations at 8 frames per second using contemporary GPUs.

We present a method for segmenting neuron membranes in 2D electron microscopy
imagery. This segmentation task has been a bottleneck to reconstruction efforts
of the brain's synaptic circuits. One common problem is the misclassification
of blurry membrane fragments as cell interior, which leads to merging of two
adjacent neuron sections into one via the blurry membrane region. Human
annotators can easily avoid such errors by implicitly performing gap
completion, taking into account the continuity of membranes.
  Drawing inspiration from these human strategies, we formulate the
segmentation task as an edge labeling problem on a graph with local topological
constraints. We derive an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces membrane
continuity, i.e. the absence of gaps. The cost function of the ILP is the
pixel-wise deviation of the segmentation from a priori membrane probabilities
derived from the data.
  Based on membrane probability maps obtained using random forest classifiers
and convolutional neural networks, our method improves the neuron boundary
segmentation accuracy compared to a variety of standard segmentation
approaches. Our method successfully performs gap completion and leads to fewer
topological errors. The method could potentially also be incorporated into
other image segmentation pipelines with known topological constraints.

State-of-the-art image segmentation algorithms generally consist of at least
two successive and distinct computations: a boundary detection process that
uses local image information to classify image locations as boundaries between
objects, followed by a pixel grouping step such as watershed or connected
components that clusters pixels into segments. Prior work has varied the
complexity and approach employed in these two steps, including the
incorporation of multi-layer neural networks to perform boundary prediction,
and the use of global optimizations during pixel clustering. We propose a
unified and end-to-end trainable machine learning approach, flood-filling
networks, in which a recurrent 3d convolutional network directly produces
individual segments from a raw image. The proposed approach robustly segments
images with an unknown and variable number of objects as well as highly
variable object sizes. We demonstrate the approach on a challenging 3d image
segmentation task, connectomic reconstruction from volume electron microscopy
data, on which flood-filling neural networks substantially improve accuracy
over other state-of-the-art methods. The proposed approach can replace complex
multi-step segmentation pipelines with a single neural network that is learned
end-to-end.

Built in the 1930s as the second of four fast battleships for the U.S. Navy, USS Indiana (BB-58) represented a new design emerging from the limitations of the post-Washington Treaty era. Utilizing an “escalator clause” to increase gun size without exceeding displacement limits, the ship remained relatively close to the treaty’s restrictions. However, this constraint led to a confined interior space, further complicated by wartime upgrades bolstering its anti-aircraft defenses and expanding the crew. Commissioned in April 1942 amidst World War II, Indiana swiftly deployed to the Pacific Theater against Japan, participating in the Guadalcanal campaign in late 1942. For the remainder of the war, she primarily provided naval gunfire support for landings and offered crucial anti-aircraft protection to carrier groups. Notably, she bombarded Japanese fortifications at Tarawa in November 1943 and Kwajalein in February 1944, sustaining damage during the latter battle when colliding with another battleship and requiring repairs.

Though ostensibly a love story—each man harbors feelings for Matari—their differing philosophies, codes of honor, and moral compasses ultimately lead to tragic consequences.  The novel follows a straightforward, conventional plotline, drawing upon Cockcroft’s deep understanding of Zen thought to offer nuanced perspectives on both Buddhist and samurai beliefs. To make 2 seedless cucumbers into a pickle, combine 4 cups of distilled white vinegar with 1 ½ 3-ounce containers of salt substitute (like NuSalt, Morton, or NoSalt), ½ cup of garlic pepper, and ½ cup of dill weed. Mix these dry ingredients thoroughly into the vinegar, tasting and adjusting the salinity if needed. Wash and slice the cucumbers thickly, setting them aside. Then, submerge the cucumber slices completely in the brine within a large jar, ensuring they’re evenly coated. Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 6-8 hours; longer marinating times result in a more intense flavor.

The glad birds caroled clear;
And I, of all the wedding guests,

The very grey rocks, looking on,

And we together sadly sank

Supervised semantic segmentation normally assumes the test data being in a
similar data domain as the training data. However, in practice, the domain
mismatch between the training and unseen data could lead to a significant
performance drop. Obtaining accurate pixel-wise label for images in different
domains is tedious and labor intensive, especially for histopathology images.
In this paper, we propose a dual adaptive pyramid network (DAPNet) for
histopathological gland segmentation adapting from one stain domain to another.
We tackle the domain adaptation problem on two levels: 1) the image-level
considers the differences of image color and style; 2) the feature-level
addresses the spatial inconsistency between two domains. The two components are
implemented as domain classifiers with adversarial training. We evaluate our
new approach using two gland segmentation datasets with H&E and DAB-H stains
respectively. The extensive experiments and ablation study demonstrate the
effectiveness of our approach on the domain adaptive segmentation task. We show
that the proposed approach performs favorably against other state-of-the-art
methods.

Deep learning’s effectiveness in image segmentation heavily depends on vast amounts of precisely labeled training data—a challenge compounded by the significant time and specialized skills needed, especially when dealing with complex 3D medical images. While self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution, current methods primarily concentrate on overall image consistency, neglecting crucial local details vital for accurate dense prediction like segmentation.  Our paper introduces a PriorGuided Local (PGL) SSL model designed to learn regional local consistency within the latent feature space. It leverages spatial transformations to establish relationships between different image views, aligning corresponding features from these views. A local consistency loss then minimizes discrepancies between these aligned feature maps. This process allows the PGL model to capture unique characteristics of local regions and preserves essential structural information, boosting its performance on segmentation tasks. Extensive testing across four publicly available CT datasets featuring various organs and tumors demonstrated that initializing a downstream network with our pre-trained PGL model yields significantly better results than random initialization or existing globally consistent models. Details and model weights can be found at: https://git.io/PGL.

Throughout the period leading up to World War I, Schloss Heiligenberg frequently welcomed the Russian Tsar and his family, alongside numerous other royalty, princes, and diplomatic representatives due to the family's significant royal connections.

I Chandra Chagoo is threatened by Abdul Khan, who believes Chagoo has been asking questions in order to gather evidence for the police. II Dr Gauri Subbiah contemplates confronting Chagoo and demanding exactly what he knows about her past. She fears he knows everything. The next day the Commissioner assigns Ghote to investigate Chagoo's death to prevent the scandal being exposed by another officer. Ghote realises that Chagoo did not have a key to lock the reptile room door and must have been murdered. Ghote interviews Dr Ram Mahipal, who left a reptile-room key in his old office at the institute when he suddenly quit his job. Ghote learns from the building manager that Mahipal returned in order to access his computer files on the night Chagoo died. Dr Subbiah, Professor Phaterpaker, Dr Mahipal and the building manager were all in the building at the time. Ghote suspects that the murder may be an employee at the nearby hospital. He enlists the inspector originally assigned to Chagoo's death to test this theory. Ghote tries to determine exactly why Mahipal left, but Phaterpaker is vague. Ghote concludes that Phaterpaker is trying to use Mahipal as a scapegoat to protect the institute. Dr Subbiah reacts badly when asked about her relations with Chagoo, however Ghote concludes she is not the killer. Ghote deduces that Mahipal misrepresented himself in order to get a university scholarship reserved for the lower classes. Mahipal confesses this is so. Ghote suggests Chagoo came to learn Mahipal's secret and was murdered because of this. Mahipal denies this and reveals that he left the institute because Phaterpaker was removing lab animals that gave undesirable results. At the police station, Ghote is dismayed when the inspector he is working with points out one of the three scientists must surely hang for the crime and expresses a preference that it be Dr Subbiah. At the institute Ghote accuses Phaterpaker of falsifying test results. Phaterpaker confesses his results are fake. He became aware that Chagoo was stealing drugs from the institute but was forced to agree to a truce because Chagoo knew Phaterpaker was removing lab animals. Ghote considers the reptile room and realises wooden stool must have been used to break the glass, so he decides to have it dusted for fingerprints. At the police station Ghote learns that Nicky D'Costa has murdered, her throat slit after asking too many questions of Abdul Khan. Ghote is angry enough to confront the commissioner, but learns Khan had arranged to be in hospital during the murder. The forensic tests do not find a match between any fingerprints on the stool and Ghote's three suspects. Nor can they prove it was used to break the glass of the viper's cage. Ghote goes home and argues with his wife, then inspiration strikes and he returns to the institute. There he searches the grounds for evidence someone could gain access by night. The security guard catches Ghote and he must call his fellow inspector to rescue him. Afterwards Ghote chances upon Dr Subbiah. The conversation between Ghote and Subbiah is interrupted when, by chance, they pass the funeral of Nicky D'Costa. The expert admits he only compared the fingerprints on the stool to the three suspects Ghote named; Subbiah, Phaterpaker and Mahipal. Without Khan's file in front of him, he could not identify the fingerprints. Khan's file is retrieved and his fingerprints are a perfect match. Ghote realises he can arrest and charge Khan with murder and recalls, with satisfaction, the words used by Commissioner's at the start of the case: "Frankly, Inspector, it will take a better man than you to put paid to Abdul Khan".

Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) holds considerable promise within the field of medical imaging. Traditional FSS approaches typically demand extensive labeled data, a limitation often encountered when working with medical images where annotation is scarce.  To overcome this challenge, we introduce several key innovations: first, a new self-supervised FSS framework specifically designed for medical imagery, eliminating reliance on labeled data; second, a superpixel-based pseudo-labeling technique to augment supervision; and third, an adaptive local prototype pooling module integrated into prototypical networks to mitigate foreground-background imbalances frequently seen in medical segmentation.  We validate our method’s effectiveness across diverse medical tasks – including abdominal organ segmentation from CT and MRI scans, and cardiac segmentation from MRI – demonstrating superior performance compared to standard FSS techniques requiring manual annotation.

This work investigates how finite element methods, specifically MINI and stabilized P1-P1 elements, approximate the Biot’s consolidation model within poroelasticity. We examine the convergence of this discrete model using spatial discretization and an implicit Euler scheme over time. Furthermore, we tackle oscillating pressure approximations that can occur when dealing with low permeability or small time steps. Image analysis frequently relies on precisely classifying pixels via segmentation, yet imaging imperfections like partial volume effects and sensor noise hinder this process. These distortions broaden the variation in pixel intensity across different classes, leading to overlapping intensities and obscuring clear boundaries. This is particularly challenging when dealing with materials containing multiple components, such as saturated soils. Our research introduces an image processing method designed to enhance segmentation precision in multiphase scenarios. Initially, unclear transitions between classes are detected and eliminated, enabling straightforward thresholding of individual classes. Subsequently, these transitional areas are categorized using a distance metric, followed by merging the resulting segmentations.  This workflow utilizes three distinct techniques for pinpointing transition pixels, validated through experiments on simulated images. Results show high accuracy in separating these ambiguous pixels from their respective single-class regions, with minimal misclassification errors (0.69-1.48%) and small area discrepancies (0.01-0.74%) within the synthesized images. Ingredients
• 8 each bone-in chicken thighs (about 3 ½ pounds)
• Kosher salt and black pepper
• 2 cups chicken broth
• 2 cups water
• ½ cup white vinegar
• 2 tablespoons olive oil
• 4 medium garlic cloves, peeled and smashed
• 1 large shallot, finely chopped (about ¼ cup)
• Leaves from 3 sprigs fresh thyme, plus 1 sprig
• 1 pound mustard greens, washed, dried, and torn into bite-size pieces
• ¼ cup heavy cream

Instructions
1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. In a large bowl, combine the broth, water, vinegar, olive oil, garlic, chopped shallot, and thyme leaves; set aside.
2. In a large Dutch oven or heavy pot, layer the chicken thighs, greens, and thyme sprig, alternating and starting and ending with the greens. Pour the broth mixture over the top and press gently on the greens to submerge them.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for about 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the greens are wilted.
4. Transfer the chicken and greens to a platter using a slotted spoon. Cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
5. Increase the heat to medium and bring the liquid to a boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by about half. Stir in the heavy cream and return to a boil. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes, or until thickened. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
6. Pour the sauce over the chicken and greens. Serve.

Ingredients:

- 1 cup apple cider vinegar
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1 bunch of kale, stems removed and leaves torn into bite-size pieces
- 1 bunch of collard greens, stems removed and leaves torn into bite-size pieces
- 2 tablespoons unsalted butter

Instructions:

1. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper on both sides.

2. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. 

3. Add the chicken, skin-side down, and cook until the skin is golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip the chicken and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.

4. In the same pot, add the sliced onion and cook until it's soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until it's fragrant.

5. Pour in the apple cider vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring the vinegar to a simmer and let it cook until it's reduced by half, about 5 minutes.

6. Return the chicken to the pot and add the chicken broth. Bring the liquid to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it cook for 20 minutes.

7. After 20 minutes, add the kale and collard greens to the pot, pushing them down into the liquid. Cover the pot again and continue to cook for another 10 minutes, or until the greens are wilted and the chicken is cooked through.

8. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the butter until it's melted and the sauce is creamy. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt and pepper if needed.

Greek communities have a long and proud history, out of which the modern Greek nation state emerged only recently, in 1830.

The Chancellor has announced a £1.8bn package to help households with the cost of living, in his spring statement.

Rishi Sunak said the measures would help people "get through the next few months" of higher prices.

It includes a cut in the energy price cap, and £500m for households in council tax bands A to D.

The BBC's Laura Kuenssberg said the chancellor was "stepping up to help millions of households".

But shadow chancellor Rachel Reeves said help "should have been sooner" and accused Mr Sunak of "playing catch up".

Here are the key points from the statement:

What's happening to the energy price cap?
The energy price cap, which limits the amount suppliers can charge customers, will be cut in April by £200 per year.

It means around 28 million households will pay less for their gas and electricity.

Earlier this month, supporting measures were announced, including a £150 council tax rebate for most homes in England and a £200 discount on energy bills owed by households who get financial help with their council tax.

Why are people getting money off their council tax?
Mr Sunak said £500m would be available to help those in council tax bands A to D.

He said around 80% of households would receive a £150 council tax rebate. But those in bands A to D - typically the least valuable properties - would receive a minimum £350 payment.

The rebate will be paid directly into bank accounts from April, the chancellor said.

How much is the help worth in total?
The chancellor said the support package would be worth £1.8bn.

On top of the help with council tax, Mr Sunak said the Energy Price Guarantee would be extended, so that all households would pay no more than £2,500 a year for their energy bills.

Without the help, forecasts showed average household energy bills could have been as much as £3,500 from October.

Why did the chancellor make the announcement?
Mr Sunak said the announcement was designed to help people "get through the next few months".

He said: "We have a responsibility to help those who are paying the highest price for global inflation."

What else did he say?
The chancellor said the government would also make a one-off payment of £1bn to help people with business rates and council tax.

> Adversarial patches are small patches that can be attached to physical objects to fool image classifiers. In this paper, we propose a new type of adversarial patch, called an IPatch, that can be used to fool image classifiers remotely. An IPatch is a small patch that can be attached to a physical object to fool image classifiers when the object is viewed from a distance. We show that IPatches can be used to fool image classifiers in a variety of settings, including when the object is viewed from a distance, when the object is viewed through a camera, and when the object is viewed through a camera with a zoom lens. We also show that IPatches can be used to fool image classifiers in a variety of domains, including face recognition, object recognition, and scene recognition.

We introduce a method that allows to automatically segment images into
semantically meaningful regions without human supervision. Derived regions are
consistent across different images and coincide with human-defined semantic
classes on some datasets. In cases where semantic regions might be hard for
human to define and consistently label, our method is still able to find
meaningful and consistent semantic classes. In our work, we use pretrained
StyleGAN2~\cite{karras2020analyzing} generative model: clustering in the
feature space of the generative model allows to discover semantic classes. Once
classes are discovered, a synthetic dataset with generated images and
corresponding segmentation masks can be created. After that a segmentation
model is trained on the synthetic dataset and is able to generalize to real
images. Additionally, by using CLIP~\cite{radford2021learning} we are able to
use prompts defined in a natural language to discover some desired semantic
classes. We test our method on publicly available datasets and show
state-of-the-art results.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), particularly Deep CNNs (DCNNs), are frequently applied to medical image segmentation and 3D navigation during robot-assisted Minimally Invasive Surgeries (MISs). Traditional DCNNs often employ downsampling layers to expand their receptive fields and extract high-level features. This downsampling reduces spatial dimensions, potentially hindering segmentation accuracy. Atrous convolution offers a viable substitute by enlarging the receptive field without altering the spatial size of feature maps. This paper introduces a technique for efficiently determining atrous rates to maximize receptive field coverage using fewer atrous convolutional layers.  Additionally, a novel DCNN – the Atrous Convolutional Neural Network (ACNN) – is presented, utilizing stacked atrous II-blocks, residual learning, and Instance Normalization (IN). Experiments on MRI and CT images show that the ACNN outperforms U-Net and Deeplabv3+ in terms of segmentation Intersection over Union (IoU), while requiring fewer trainable parameters.

US Open champion Svetlana Kuznetsova has tested positive for a banned drug, according to Belgian authorities.
Belgian sports minister Claude Eerdekens said that the Russian world number five tested positive for the stimulant ephedrine on 19 December. Kuznetsova was playing in an exhibition event in Charleroi at the time. Eerdekens said: "There is a problem. Ephedrine was discovered. She remains innocent until proved guilty. She can ask for it to be tested again." The situation remains unclear as the tournament was not commissioned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the International Tennis Federation (ITF) or the Women's Tennis Accosiation (WTA). The test was carried out by regional Belgian authorities and Kuznetsova has not yet been able to have a B sample tested.
Speaking at the Australian Open on Monday, before Eerdekens identified her, Kuznetsova said: "I'm not worried. I'm not using anything to push myself. "I have not been notified of any positive test, and I think it is unfair that it's come out the way it did." Eerdekens said that confirmation of the findings was sent last Friday to the player's address in Spain, as well as to the Belgian prosecutors' office and the Belgian and Russian tennis federations. He conceded Kuznetsova might have taken a medicine which contained the banned substance. "We have simply stated a fact," he said. "It is for the federation concerned to impose the disciplinary measures after a procedure that respects the defence.
"Either the ephedrine was taken to improve her performance or it is because she took some medicine legitimately to cure an infection." However, Kuznetsova's naming was condemned by Russian tennis chief Shamil Tarpishchev. "First of all, this Belgian sports minister has broken every ethical rule in the book by naming a player without any proof of wrongdoing, without any basic evidence," Tarpishchev said. "We all know the basic principle in doping cases. Ingredients:
- 8 ounces of pasta (fettuccine, penne, or your choice)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 pound Italian sausage, casings removed
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 ounces mushrooms, sliced
- 1/2 cup black olives, pitted and halved
- 1/2 cup white wine (optional)
- 1 cup tomato sauce
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Cook the pasta according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
2. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the Italian sausage and cook until browned, breaking it up into smaller pieces with a wooden spoon.
3. Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until translucent. Then, add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, until fragrant.
4. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they are soft and release their moisture, about 5-7 minutes.
5. If using white wine, pour it into the skillet and let it simmer until it has reduced by half.
6. Stir in the tomato sauce and black olives, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Let the sauce simmer for about 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream. Let the sauce heat through, but be careful not to let it boil.
8. Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss it with the sauce until it is well coated.
9. Divide the pasta amongst serving plates and garnish with fresh parsley.
10. Serve hot and enjoy your delicious Pasta Alla Boscaiola!

Preheat your oven to 425°. Rinse and thoroughly dry the chicken; discard the giblet packet or use it later. Trim any extra fat from the cavity opening. Let me start off by saying that I was introduced to the films of Terrence Malick in 1998 when I watched and was blown away by 'The Thin Red Line.' It is one of the best war movies ever made and while I can rant about it at length, that review belongs on a different page. It was with great anticipation that I waited for 'The New World.' I was lucky enough to get tickets to an advance screening and the theatre was full of people like me. Their take on the film was almost as interesting as the film was.

'The New World' is a film that will draw out one of two very powerful emotions: Love or Hate. I really don't believe there is a middle ground in this case. I think it is quite possibly the most beautifully photographed film I have ever seen. It is astonishing. The score from James Horner is, in my opinion, his greatest work. He's a wonderful composer but he has exceeded himself on every level. This is a movie that can be watched like art (because it is) and listened to as a symphony (it might as well be one). Very few movies leave me stunned and 'The New World' is so luscious that I think it is worth the journey, even if it is only to look at how beautiful it is and listen to how glorious it is. Is that a superficial way of looking at things? Perhaps, but they are the film's two most brilliant qualities.

'The New World' does have problems and I think it falls very much into a 'buyer beware' category. Malick's movie is long -- very long -- and feels every moment of it. I don't mind these things because I found it enchanting; many in the audience with me did not. These are not people who are 'dumb,' or who 'don't get it.' They are people who are used to 99% of the films that you will see. 'The New World' is very self-indulgent at times. No one can reasonably defend the pace of the film. I want to and I can't. This is a movie so full of substance that it is detrimental. It is so rich and textured that it would be hard to say where things could have been improved, but aside from the first forty minutes which deal largely with the question of whether or not the Europeans can survive the first winter or not, the dramatic 'action,' that is, the engine of a script that pushes one scene into the next, is idling at best. 'The New World' has a plodding pace and it took me on a nice quiet stroll that I enjoyed immensely. I can not, in good conscience though recommend to the man on the street that he go to see it. If less than a third of the theatre I was in walked out, I'd be stunned. I lost count because so many people left. Mostly the middle hour and a half of the film is to blame. Scenes drift from one to the next -- they're stunning and textured and personally I enjoyed them -- but they involved a lot of hanging out. Two people hanging out in the woods. I understand that the film has deep meditative and philosophical meanderings about man's relationship with nature and how one impacts the other. I get it. But a lot of the love story is about two people hanging out in the woods. All the time. If one of them had said 'Let us go watch the grass grow for the afternoon,' it would have been the most honest line in the entire film. It is the only thing I will fault Malick for here because it really does kill the film for a lot of people. His intelligence should not be questioned. I wish only he'd tried to focus the script a bit more and been specific rather than general. Can two people from different cultures be together? We get it already. We got it an hour ago. Oh, more grass growing ... must watch ... ha! Forgive my little joke.

The argument to be made though is that this film has not been made for everyone (the studio is no doubt surprised to learn this and will be scrambling to recover their money -- they did a good thing in making it but they're going to lose their shirts). It was made by Terrence Malick for Terrence Malick. I'm glad to have seen it but I spoke with twenty people who were not. There will be constant arguments on the user boards here at the IMDb. The film is going to have rabidly fanatical supporters who think everyone else is just too stupid to get it. And it is going to be criticized by many, many others who died a thousand deaths just trying to sift through the movie.

Two final thoughts: the first is that I hate myself for having to say anything negative about Malick or his film. He's a special film-maker and his films make it worth going to the theatre. 'The New World' is great but flawed and it is dishonest for anyone to pretend otherwise -- such behaviour is deceitful and pretentious.Thought number two is that although the film is equal parts challenging and rewarding (as great movies should be) it is especially important in the case of 'The New World' to see it in the theatre. It is so majestic in scope that I don't believe the greatest home theatre can do it justice. It is truly epic in its cinematography and score. If it doesn't win Oscars for both we will have witnessed a massive artistic injustice. NOTHING this year, NOTHING has come close to being a threat to 'The New World' for either of those two categories. Appreciate them as they were intended to be seen.

Spaghetti with Pan Fried Chicken and Cherry Tomato Puree
 
Serve up a quick and easy pasta dish that's perfect for kids and adults alike with this pan-fried chicken and cherry tomato puree recipe. Both the chicken and the tomato puree can be prepared well in advance, making this a great choice for busy families.

Ingredients 
300g cherry tomatoes, halved
1 garlic clove, chopped
1 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp red wine vinegar
6oz spaghetti
1 small chicken breast, cut into strips
1 tbsp plain flour
1 egg, beaten
30g breadcrumbs
30g grated parmesan
1 tbsp olive oil
freshly ground black pepper

Method
1. To make the tomato puree, place the tomatoes in a small pan with the garlic, olive oil and red wine vinegar. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft.
2. Season with pepper, then blend until smooth. Pour into a bowl and wipe the pan clean.
3. Bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the spaghetti according to the packet instructions.
4. Meanwhile, prepare the chicken. Place the flour, egg and breadcrumbs in three separate bowls. Dip the chicken strips first in the flour, then the egg (allowing any excess to drip off) and then the breadcrumbs.
5. Heat the oil in the wiped-out pan and fry the chicken strips for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden-brown and completely cooked through.
6. Drain the spaghetti and either stir into the tomato puree or serve with the tomato puree poured over. Serve with the chicken strips and a grating of parmesan.

The Polyglot Petition for Home Protection was the first world-wide proclamation against the manufacturing and international trade in liquor and drugs as well as the prohibition of legalised vice. It served as a first major campaign to raise public awareness of the need for international agreements on controls for opium and its derivatives. Description of the petition
Addressed to all rulers and nations of the world, this petition to adopt prohibition was written by the American Woman's Christian Temperance Union (WCTU) president Frances Willard in 1884. It was carried across the world by at least four World WCTU missionaries who gathered signatures of nearly eight million people in more than fifty countries. The signatures can be categorized in three basic sections: signatures of individual women, written endorsements of men, and attestations of leaders of groups that had endorsed the petition. The signed petitions from the U.S. (over 750,000) were sent to Mrs. Rebecca C. Shuman in Evanston, Illinois who trimmed and mounted them on white muslin, one-half yard in width and bound with red ribbon on one side and blue ribbon on the other. Signed petitions from Great Britain (350,000 signatories) came in already mounted on cloth in time for presentation to the U.S. president in February 1885. The Polyglot Petition is archived in the Woman's Christian Temperance Union Administration Building in Evanston, Illinois, United States of America.

Conservative proposals would empower local communities by allowing them to directly elect their own police commissioners, replacing current, less transparent police governance structures. Party leader Michael Howard asserted this new position wouldn’t diminish the role of chief constables. However, the Liberal Democrats expressed concern that such changes could enable extremist groups to influence policing, while Labour deemed the initiative “excessive.”  The Police Federation emphasized the importance of maintaining operational autonomy, warning against turning policing into a politically driven issue. Chair Jan Berry cautioned that electing commissioners could lead to individuals with strong political agendas controlling day-to-day operations. Mr. Howard argued that commissioners would offer greater public accountability than existing councils composed of councillors and magistrates, highlighting the relative obscurity of these latter bodies. He stated that commissioners would retain the same powers as current authorities, noting their lack of visibility. Critics worry that this shift might concentrate power in the hands of campaigners focused solely on specific issues, potentially neglecting broader community needs. Lord Harris from the Association of Police Authorities voiced opposition, arguing that it risked undermining established policing practices and subjecting chief constables to political direction.

Despite seeing this film three times, I maintain it’s a masterpiece, though its brilliance isn’t universally appreciated. It’s understandable why some find it tedious and lengthy, although I personally found it perfectly paced. Many viewers fail to connect with the film’s core theme—a profound exploration of spiritual growth from self-centeredness to selfless love, essentially charting a genuine Christian path—because of our current era’s emphasis on secularism and material reduction.

This film uniquely depicts this journey of self-overcoming, linking it to the early days of Christian missions in Japan. The Japanese exhibit a subtle cruelty, yet possess a greater depth of understanding than the largely oblivious Portuguese missionaries who often projected unwarranted cultural dominance. Achieving this complex narrative and culminating spiritual experience required nearly three hours of exceptional filmmaking. 

For those familiar with the true path of self-transcendence towards humble love, this is undoubtedly a remarkable work. However, others might perceive it as a slow and unproductive expenditure of time. Fans of this film could also appreciate “The Assassin” by Hsiao-hsien Hou, which explores a related Taoist perspective on this internal transformation.

To make this dish, start by combining 100 grams of peeled Kabocha squash with 90ml of water and bring to a boil before simmering until tender. Blend the cooked squash and liquid mixture using a hand mixer, then stir in 50ml of milk and 2 tablespoons of sugar. Heat gently, adding 1 tablespoon of white miso and dissolving completely. Adjust sweetness with additional sugar if needed. Simultaneously, prepare the dumplings: soften peeled Kabocha squash in plastic wrap before microwaving until pliable; mash thoroughly while warm. Mix 75g of shiratamako with 100ml of water, kneading until it reaches a soft, earlobe-like consistency. Form the mixture into 2cm balls, creating a small indentation in each. Gently drop these dumplings into boiling water and cook until they float – about one minute. Drain and serve immediately in bowls, ladling generously with the warm broth. We present approaches for the study of fluid-structure interactions subject
to thermal fluctuations. A mixed mechanical description is utilized combining
Eulerian and Lagrangian reference frames. We establish general conditions for
operators coupling these descriptions. Stochastic driving fields for the
formalism are derived using principles from statistical mechanics. The
stochastic differential equations of the formalism are found to exhibit
significant stiffness in some physical regimes. To cope with this issue, we
derive reduced stochastic differential equations for several physical regimes.
We also present stochastic numerical methods for each regime to approximate the
fluid-structure dynamics and to generate efficiently the required stochastic
driving fields. To validate the methodology in each regime, we perform analysis
of the invariant probability distribution of the stochastic dynamics of the
fluid-structure formalism. We compare this analysis with results from
statistical mechanics. To further demonstrate the applicability of the
methodology, we perform computational studies for spherical particles having
translational and rotational degrees of freedom. We compare these studies with
results from fluid mechanics. The presented approach provides for
fluid-structure systems a set of rather general computational methods for
treating consistently structure mechanics, hydrodynamic coupling, and thermal
fluctuations.

Dean Cornwell (March 5, 1892 – December 4, 1960) was an American illustrator and muralist. His oil paintings were frequently featured in popular magazines and books as literary illustrations, advertisements, and posters promoting the war effort. Throughout the first half of the 20th century he was a dominant presence in American illustration. At the peak of his popularity he was nicknamed the "Dean of Illustrators". Background
Cornwell was born in Louisville, Kentucky. His father, Charles L. Cornwell, was a civil engineer whose drawings of industrial subjects fascinated Cornwell as a child. He began his professional career as a cartoonist for the Louisville Herald. Soon thereafter he moved to Chicago, where he studied at the Art Institute and worked for the Chicago Tribune. In 1915 he moved to New Rochelle, New York, a well known artist colony, and studied in New York City under Harvey Dunn at the Art Students League of New York. Eventually he traveled to London to study mural painting as an apprentice to Frank Brangwyn.

Collapse theories offer interpretations of quantum mechanics where the wave function's collapse represents a genuine physical event. These theories specify detailed mathematical rules governing this collapse, moving beyond the ambiguous idea that it happens only when an “observer” performs a “measurement.” A core aspect of these theories is the “primitive ontology”—the fundamental variables representing matter within spacetime—and there’s debate regarding whether such an ontology is essential to their formulation. My discussion addresses this issue, suggesting that certain contradictions within collapse theories can be resolved by incorporating a primitive ontology.

To prepare this dish, you’ll need 1 1/2 pounds of boneless, skinless chicken breasts cut into 3/4-inch cubes, alongside 1 1/2 cups of 1/2-inch diced potatoes, 1 cup of 1/4-inch sliced carrots, and 1 cup of frozen peas. Combine these ingredients with 1/3 cup plus 2 teaspoons of unsalted butter, 1/3 cup chopped yellow onion, 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon of sea salt, 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon of celery seed, and 1/4 teaspoon of dried thyme. Add 1 1/2 cups of unsalted chicken broth and 2/3 cup of 1% milk. First, simmer the chicken, vegetables, and seasonings in water until the carrots and potatoes are tender – about 10 to 15 minutes. We develop families of stable states for the Einstein-Vlasov system with a spherical symmetry, defined by a central redshift value. As this redshift approaches zero, these states closely resemble steady states within the Vlasov-Poisson system – effectively establishing a Newtonian limit where the speed of light remains constant. The resulting behavior is examined using a parameter connected to the specific characteristics of each solution. Carl Beam (June 30, 1935 – July 1, 2021) was an American physicist who made significant contributions to the field of elementary particle physics. He was born in Huntington, West Virginia, and received his Ph.D. from the University of Illinois.

Beam was a professor of Physics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and spent a sabbatical at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) in Switzerland, where he made the discovery of the W and Z bosons, which are particles associated with Weak force interaction. For his discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1969, along with Richard P. Feynman and Jack Steinberger.

In addition to his work on weak force interaction, Beam made important contributions to the development of the quark model of matter, which is a fundamental theory of physics explaining the nature of matter.

Beam passed away on July 1, 2021, at the age of 86. He was widely regarded as a pioneer in the field of particle physics and his work continues to inspire students and researchers today.

Procedures: Select twelve unblemished organically grown small lemons, preferrably Meyer (a small type). Wash and dry the lemons. If using store-bought lemons, scrub them carefully to remove any pesticides. Cut a thin slice from the top and the bottom of each lemon. Set one lemon on end and make a vertical cut 3 quarters of the way through the fruit, so that the 2 halves still remain attached at the base; do not cut it in half. Turn the lemon upside down and rotate it so that you can make a second vertical cut down the center, crosswise to the first, leaving the bottom Fill each cut with as much salt as it will hold. Carefully place the lemon at the bottom of a hot, sterilized, wide-mouthed quart glass jar. Proceed in this manner with the remaining lemons, compressing them in the jar until no space is left and the lemon juice has risen to the top. Seal and set aside at room temperature. More lemons may be added in the following days as the lemon rinds begin to soften. Make sure the lemons are covered with juice at all times, adding freshly squeezed lemon juice if necessary. The lemons are ready to use when the rinds are tender, in 5 to 6 weeks. Rinse them lightly before using. Once opened, refrigerate preserved lemons for up to 6 months.

To make this cheesecake, you’ll need 450g of softened cream cheese, 1/4 cup of caster sugar, 3 teaspoons of cornstarch, 3 eggs, 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract, 3 teaspoons of powdered sugar, 1 1/2 tablespoons of fresh lemon juice, 2 cups of sour cream, 1 cup of heavy cream, and 220g of melted and slightly cooled white chocolate. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and line a 20cm (8-inch) springform pan with parchment paper, then wrap the outside tightly with two layers of aluminum foil. Blend the cream cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until smooth. Gradually add the eggs while the processor is running, scraping down the sides as needed. Incorporate the vanilla, lemon zest and juice, creams, a pinch of salt, and pulse until everything is mixed. Stir in the white chocolate until smooth. Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and place it in a larger baking dish. Carefully pour hot water into the dish until it reaches about halfway up the sides of the pan. Bake for 45 minutes, then remove from the oven and let it sit, covered, inside for an additional hour. Once cooled, remove the pan from the water bath, discard the foil, and allow the cheesecake to cool completely on a wire rack. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Before serving, gently loosen the base with a warm, damp cloth and run a knife along the edges. Invert the cake onto a serving plate, decorate with fresh fruit arranged artfully, drizzle with passion fruit pulp, and slice with a warmed, dry knife.

Neil Kennedy O'Donnell (born July 3, 1966) is a former American football quarterback who played in the National Football League for 14 seasons (1990–2003) with the Pittsburgh Steelers, New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, and Tennessee Titans. He played college football at Maryland. Early life
O'Donnell grew up in Madison, New Jersey, and played high school football there at Madison High School. Neil Kennedy O’Donnell was born July 3, 1966 in Morristown, New Jersey. Neil's four older brothers played for local coaching legend Ted Monica and won state championships. Stephen O’Donnell was an All-State quarterback who went on to play for Duke. Coach Monica had retired by the time Neil enrolled at Madison High School, but mentored him throughout much of his young football life. In this paper, we review and extend a family of log-det divergences for
symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices and discuss their fundamental
properties. We show how to generate from parameterized Alpha-Beta (AB) and
Gamma Log-det divergences many well known divergences, for example, the Stein's
loss, S-divergence, called also Jensen-Bregman LogDet (JBLD) divergence, the
Logdet Zero (Bhattacharryya) divergence, Affine Invariant Riemannian Metric
(AIRM) as well as some new divergences. Moreover, we establish links and
correspondences among many log-det divergences and display them on alpha-beta
plain for various set of parameters. Furthermore, this paper bridges these
divergences and shows also their links to divergences of multivariate and
multiway Gaussian distributions. Closed form formulas are derived for gamma
divergences of two multivariate Gaussian densities including as special cases
the Kullback-Leibler, Bhattacharryya, R\'enyi and Cauchy-Schwartz divergences.
Symmetrized versions of the log-det divergences are also discussed and
reviewed. A class of divergences is extended to multiway divergences for
separable covariance (precision) matrices.

A close associate of former Yukos boss Mikhail Khodorkovsky has told a court that fraud charges levelled against him are "false".
Platon Lebedev has been on trial alongside Mr Khodorkovsky since June in a case centring around the privatisation of a fertiliser firm. The pair claim they are being punished by the authorities for the political ambitions of Mr Khodorkovsky. Mr Lebedev said there were "absurd contradictions" in the case. Opening his defence, he said he could not see the legal basis of the charges he faced, which also include allegations of tax evasion. "To my embarrassment, I could not understand the file of complaints against me," he told a Moscow court. Mr Lebedev headed the Menatep group, the parent company of Yukos.
Mr Lebedev and Mr Khodorkovsky, who each face a possible 10 year jail sentence if convicted, will be questioned by a judge over the next few days. Mr Khodorkovsky began his testimony last week, telling the court that he objected to the way that the "running of a normal business has been presented as a work of criminal fiction". The charges are seen by supporters as politically motivated and part of a drive by Russian President Vladimir Putin to rein in the country's super-rich business leaders, the so-called oligarchs. Yukos has been presented with a $27.5bn (£13bn) tax demand by the Russian authorities and its key Yugansk division was auctioned off to part settle the bill. The company's effort to gain bankruptcy protection in the US - in a bid to win damages for the sale - were dismissed by a court in Texas.

“Paint It Yellow.” Oops—that’s supposed to be “Rang De Basanti.”  Essentially, that’s what the director aims to express. It explores today, our present, alongside echoes of pre-independence India. It depicts a generation familiar with modern technology like McDonald's, yet still appreciating traditional foods such as Dhaba parathas and sweet lassi, often limiting their patriotism to just these experiences. This isn’t a typical Bollywood film filled with six love songs, brief foreign trips, and predictable melodrama. Instead, “Rang De” is a powerful cult movie; it’s an invitation for deep reflection and intellectual engagement, prompting questions about how we truly honor our freedom. The concluding lines spoken by the narrator – “I thought there were two kinds of people in the world, one who dies weeping and another who quietly depart, but today I’ve learned there’s a third kind – those who laugh” – perfectly encapsulate its message.

Rangi De Basanti is undeniably a bold and inventive effort by the director, showcasing a remarkably well-chosen ensemble cast. While seasoned actors like Om Puri and Anupam Kher appeared somewhat detached, every character develops organically throughout the film, allowing them to convincingly articulate their perspectives. Rakesh Omprakash Mehra is a rising voice in Indian cinema, consistently pursuing unique approaches. I was particularly struck by his earlier work in 2001’s “Aks,” and he has successfully crafted another exceptional achievement. A key element of the film is its masterful use of cinematography, notably pioneering the effective juxtaposition of scenes. The gradual immersion of characters within historical moments evokes a sense of wonder at the meticulous preparation involved, both visually and through the performances. The film begins with considerable energy and optimism.

Adapromine, a Russian-marketed antiviral medication belonging to the adamantane family—similar to amantadine, rimantadine, and memantine—is used to treat and prevent influenza. As an alkyl derivative of rimantadine, it shares antiviral activity but demonstrates efficacy against both influenza A and B strains. In the 1980s, resistant strains of influenza A, alongside those resistant to rimantadine and deitiforine, emerged in Mongolia and the Soviet Union. Animal EEG research indicates that adapromine and related adamantanes, such as amantadine, bromantane, and memantine, exhibit psychostimulant and potentially antidepressant properties linked to catecholaminergic pathways. However, these effects are distinct from typical stimulants like amphetamine; alternatively, these compounds are often characterized as “adaptogens” or “actoprotectors.”

Ngangom Bala Devi (born 2 February 1990) is an Indian professional footballer who currently plays as a forward for Rangers Women in the Scottish Women's Premier League and the Indian national team. She is also the first Asian to play and score in a professional league in Scotland and also the first South Asian to sign a professional contract.

Early Life and Career

Devi was born in Manipur, India. Her interest in football was sparked by her father, who played the game at a local level. She began her professional career as a footballer in 2005 with Manipur Police Sports Club in the Indian Women's League (IWL). After five years in this team, she moved to New Radiant SC of Maldives, where she spent just one season before returning to her former club.

Bala Devi has also represented India at the international level, playing in the SAFF Women's Championship and the Women's Asian Cup qualifiers. Over the years, she has been an integral part of the Indian national team and has scored several crucial goals.

Move to Rangers F.C. 

Bala Devi signed an 18-month contract with Scottish club Rangers F.C in January 2020, making her the first Indian woman to be signed by a professional club in the United Kingdom. This move was facilitated through a partnership between Rangers and Bengaluru FC. Devi made her debut against Hearts, scoring in the final two minutes of the match. Her consistent performances have received widespread recognition and commendation.

Style of Play and Legacy

Devi is known for her strength, agility, and precision in front of the goal. She is capable of playing as both a forward and attacking midfielder and has earned comparisons to her male counterparts in Indian Football.

Devi's move to Rangers was a landmark moment in Indian football history, particularly for women in the sport. Her career demonstrates the possibility of Indian talent finding opportunities in prestigious international leagues; a fact that has been acclaimed as instrumental in fostering ambition and aspiration among young Indian women interested in football.

Honours and Awards

Among her many accolades, Bala Devi was crowned AIFF Women's Player of the Year twice, in 2014 and 2015. She was also the top scorer in the Indian Women's League in three consecutive seasons, from 2016 to 2019. Achievements at international level include being part of the SAFF Women's Championship-winning squads of 2010 and 2016.

Sure, here's a recipe for bow ties with sausage and leek sauce:

Ingredients:

* 1 pound bow tie pasta
* 1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
* 2 medium leeks, chopped (about 2 cups)
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1/4 cup white wine (optional)
* 1/4 cup chicken broth
* 1/4 cup heavy cream
* 1 tablespoon tomato paste
* 1 teaspoon dried thyme
* Salt and pepper to taste
* Grated Parmesan cheese for serving (optional)

Instructions:

1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the bow tie pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water and then drain the pasta.
2. In a large skillet, cook the Italian sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the sausage from the skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, add the chopped leeks and minced garlic. Cook until the leeks are softened and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
4. If using white wine, add it to the skillet and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
5. Add the chicken broth, heavy cream, tomato paste, and thyme to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring the mixture to a simmer.
6. Add the cooked sausage back into the skillet and stir to combine.
7. Add the cooked bow tie pasta to the skillet and toss to combine, adding some reserved pasta cooking water if the sauce is too thick.
8. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Serve the bow ties with sausage and leek sauce hot

Crude oil prices surged back above the $47 a barrel mark on Thursday after an energy market watchdog raised its forecasts for global demand.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned demand for Opec's crude in the first quarter would outstrip supply. The IEA raised its estimate of 2005 oil demand growth by 80,000 barrels a day to 84 million barrels a day. US light crude rose $1.64 to $47.10, while Brent crude in London gained $1.32 to $44.45.
The Paris-based IEA watchdog, which advises industrialized nations on energy policy, said the upward revision was due to stronger demand from China and other Asian countries. The fresh rally in crude prices followed gains on Wednesday which were triggered by large falls in US crude supplies following a cold spell in North America in January. The US Department of Energy reported that crude stockpiles had fallen 1m barrels to 294.3m. On top of that, ongoing problems for beleaguered Russian oil giant Yukos have also prompted the IEA to revise its output estimates from Russia - a major non-Opec supplier. "I think that prices are now beginning to set a new range and it looks like the $40 to $50 level," said energy analyst Orin Middleton of Barclays Capital.

Acton House is a mansion in Acton, West London, that was formerly the home of Napoleon III, Emperor of France, and his wife, Empress Eugénie. It was built in the 1870s by Richard Norman Shaw for the Scottish economist and historian William Hewett. In 1883, it was bought by the architect Richard Shaw, who designed the nearby St. Barnabas Church.

In 1904, the house was acquired by the Welsh businessman Sir John Williams Bt., who lived there with his wife Frances (née Cornwallis), daughter of Colonel Charles Cornwallis of Abermarlais, Carmarthenshire. The couple's eldest daughter, Ursula, married Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg, the son of the Austrian ambassador, in 1919.

In 1928, Acton House was acquired by Baron Melchior de Polignac, who rented it to King Zog of Albania from 1936 to 1938. It was then acquired by the Turkish-born Hüseyin Jawdat, who used it as a training center for the Muslim World League.

Since 1958, it has been the home of the International Youth Hostel. In 1985, it was Grade II* listed by English Heritage.

To make Vanilla Bean Rooibos Ice Cream, combine 1 cup whole milk (avoiding ultra-pasteurized), 2 cups heavy cream (also avoiding ultra-pasteurized), 2 tablespoons organic rooibos tea leaves, and the split Madagascar vanilla bean with its seeds scraped in a medium saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a bare simmer and remove from heat. Steep the mixture with the rooibos leaves for one hour – this step is crucial for flavor development. Stir in one cup of cream and warm it without boiling. Strain out the rooibos leaves and vanilla bean, discarding the former and retaining the bean. Keep the remaining one cup of heavy cream in a bowl with a strainer. Whisk the egg yolks until light, then slowly incorporate the warm cream mixture, tempering as you go. Return the combined mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and reaches 170-175°F. Strain this into the reserved cream, return the vanilla bean, and chill in an ice bath for 30 minutes. Refrigerate the mixture for 4-8 hours until it’s 40°F or colder. Remove the vanilla bean, transfer the chilled mixture to an ice cream maker, add one teaspoon of amaretto liqueur, and churn according to instructions.

To make this sourdough bread, begin with 1/2 cup of sour bread starter and 2 cups of warm water. Combine with 3 1/2 cups of rye flour, 1 packet of active dry yeast, 1/4 cup of warm water, and 2 teaspoons of salt in a large bowl. Gradually mix in the water until blended, followed by 1 cup of rye flour. Cover loosely and allow it to ferment in a warm environment (around 85°F) for 20-40 hours, adjusting for desired sourness. In a separate small bowl, dissolve the yeast in 1/4 cup of warm water before adding it to the mixture. Incorporate the remaining salt and slowly add the rye flour, beating continuously. Gradually add the white flour, ensuring each addition is fully combined. Once a stiff dough forms, let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then turn it out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth. Place the dough in a greased bowl, coating all sides, cover, and allow it to double in size – approximately 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Divide the dough into two portions, saving about 1/2 cup for later use, and store the remaining pieces in a covered container in the refrigerator. Prepare a greased and floured pan, let it rise slightly, and bake at 375°F (190°C) for one hour.

In an era where technology is constantly evolving, it's hard to imagine that something as ubiquitous as mobile phones could only be celebrating its twentieth birthday. Yet, it was on December 3rd, 1991 that British telecommunications company Vodafone sent the world's first SMS text message - marking the beginning of a revolution in communication and ushering in the age of mobile phone usage.

Since then, mobiles have become ingrained in our daily lives, transforming how we communicate with one another both domestically and internationally. Microfluidic devices and portable diagnostic chips rely on numerous interconnected parts, including nanosensors needing internal communication. Molecular communication offers a potential solution, leveraging kinesin-driven microtubule (MT) movement to transport data between elements. Determining the ideal channel geometry presents difficulties. This study develops a mathematical optimization model to identify suitable channel shapes and sizes across various transmission durations. Specifically, we formulate three distinct models for rectangular, regular polygonal, and regular polygonal ring channels. Our results indicate that the square channel is best for rectangular designs, while circular channels perform optimally in the other geometries. Ultimately, we demonstrate that among two-dimensional shapes, a circular channel provides the highest information transfer rate.

Despite deep convolutional neural networks achieved impressive progress in
medical image computing and analysis, its paradigm of supervised learning
demands a large number of annotations for training to avoid overfitting and
achieving promising results. In clinical practices, massive semantic
annotations are difficult to acquire in some conditions where specialized
biomedical expert knowledge is required, and it is also a common condition
where only few annotated classes are available. In this work, we proposed a
novel method for few-shot medical image segmentation, which enables a
segmentation model to fast generalize to an unseen class with few training
images. We construct our few-shot image segmentor using a deep convolutional
network trained episodically. Motivated by the spatial consistency and
regularity in medical images, we developed an efficient global correlation
module to capture the correlation between a support and query image and
incorporate it into the deep network called global correlation network.
Moreover, we enhance discriminability of deep embedding to encourage clustering
of the feature domains of the same class while keep the feature domains of
different organs far apart. Ablation Study proved the effectiveness of the
proposed global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Extensive
experiments on anatomical abdomen images on both CT and MRI modalities are
performed to demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our proposed
model.

Recent semantic segmentation relies heavily on the U-Net architecture, utilizing an encoder-decoder structure. However, standard U-Nets with basic skip connections often struggle to capture comprehensive, multi-scale contextual information – this is due to issues like mismatched feature representations between encoder and decoder stages, and sometimes, skip connections can actually hinder segmentation accuracy. To address these limitations, we introduce UCTransNet, a novel framework incorporating a newly designed CTrans module within the U-Net. This approach focuses on channel relationships and utilizes an attention mechanism. The CTrans module employs a Channel Cross Fusion with Transformer (CCT) and Channel-wise Cross-Attention (CCA) sub-modules to effectively integrate multi-scale channel data. These components intelligently link fused channel information to decoder features, resolving ambiguities and enhancing segmentation precision. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that UCTransNet surpasses existing methods across various datasets and established architectures—including those employing transformers or U-shaped designs—providing improved segmentation accuracy. Code available at: https://github.com/McGregorWwww/UCTransNet.

Serves 4 as leftovers

Ingredients (for 2 servings):

1 tbsp butter, softened

1 medium butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and diced

1 onion, diced

3 garlic cloves, finely diced

1 (14.25-ounce) can chopped tomatoes

½ cup water

½ cup milk

1 cup butternut squash puree (about 1/2 pound)

salt

1 teaspoon ground black pepper

1 cup dry white wine

2 cups chicken stock, or water

1 cup fresh baby arugula, washed and chopped, and torn leaves for garnish

½ cup chopped fresh dill

4 cups fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves, plus more for garnish

Directions:

1. Heat a 15-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add butter and sauté until it reaches a depth of 10 inches (about 3 minutes). Remove from the heat and set aside.

2. When the butter is gone, add the butternut squash and onion. Cook for 5 more minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes, then the water, milk, and stir vigorously until the sauce thickens, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper, to taste. Transfer the mixture to a food processor and pulse until it separates and starts to form a smooth puree. Transfer the puree to a large saucepan.

3. Bring to a boil. Add 2 cups of the stock (or water) and reduce heat for 2 minutes. Stir in the baby arug. Reduce the heat for 10 seconds, then add the wine and remaining stock. Lower heat to a simmer and cook until the wine has reduced by almost half and the soup is thick, about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.

4. Stir in the parsley, drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve. Garnish with fresh dill and parsley leaves.

Image segmentation remains a prominent area of investigation within computer vision, continually driving the demand for enhanced methods. Clustering, a widely utilized unsupervised technique across various scientific disciplines, frequently features in image segmentation techniques; however, further advancements are needed. This work introduces a new clustering-based image segmentation approach, prioritizing color spaces and selecting Lab. We employ the K-means hard clustering algorithm, utilizing cosine distance due to its sensitivity to distance metric selection. Subsequently, a Sobel filter refines the resulting image, which is then processed using a marker watershed algorithm to achieve the final segmentation. Performance evaluation relies on measuring Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) values.

4 large eggs
4 large egg whites
1 cup nonfat milk
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, minced
1/4 teaspoon fresh ground pepper
5 cups chopped spinach, wilted (see Tip)
4 cups whole grain bread (cut into 1-inch cubes, crusts removed if desired)
1 cup ham steak, diced
1/2 cup jarred roasted red pepper, chopped
3/4 cup shredded gruyere cheese or 3/4 cup swiss cheese
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a 7-by-11-inch glass baking dish or a 2-quart casserole with cooking spray. Whisk eggs, egg whites and milk in a medium bowl. Add mustard, rosemary and pepper; whisk to combine. Toss spinach, bread, ham and roasted red peppers in a large bowl. Add the egg mixture and toss well to coat. Transfer to the prepared baking dish and push down to compact. Cover with foil. Bake until the custard has set, 40 to 45 minutes. Uncover, sprinkle with cheese and continue baking until the pudding is puffed and golden on top, 15 to 20 minutes more. Transfer to a wire rack and cool for 15 to 20 minutes before serving. TIPS. Tip: To wilt spinach, rinse thoroughly with cool water. Transfer to a large microwave-safe bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and punch several holes in it. Microwave on High until wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Squeeze out excess moisture before adding the spinach to the recipe. MAKE AHEAD TIP: Prepare casserole through Step 2; refrigerate overnight. Let stand at room temperature while the oven preheats. Bake as directed in Step 3.

Overall, the way people treat me has definitely varied. I'm extremely lucky to have plenty of supportive and loving people in my life but the negative reactions and comments still sting. The first four British men to be released from Guantanamo Bay are expected to return to the UK within weeks.

The men - Shaker Aamer, Jamil El-Banna, Richard Belmar and Omar Deghayes - will fly to Britain on private jets, the BBC understands.

They are among nine British residents held at the US detention camp in Cuba.

The four men are due to be freed after being cleared of any involvement in terrorism by a US military review panel.

The BBC's Caroline Wyatt in Washington says it is not yet clear when the other five men will be released.

She says the four men due to be freed will fly to a military base in the United States before boarding private jets for Britain.

The Pentagon is expected to make a formal announcement later on Thursday.

The four men have been held at Guantanamo Bay since 2002.

Shaker Aamer, 39, from London, has already been cleared for release by the US authorities but remains in detention.

Jamil El-Banna, 45, from west London, was seized in Afghanistan where he had gone to help with relief efforts.

Mr Deghayes, 37, from Brighton, is originally from Libya. He went to Afghanistan to fight against the Soviet Union's occupation in the 1980s.

Richard Belmar, 24, from north London, is of Jamaican descent.

To prepare this dish, begin by gathering 1 pound of trimmed green beans, one small red bell pepper (seeded and sliced), two baby bok choy (sliced lengthwise), twelve thin ginger slices, 1 teaspoon of ground coriander, 2 teaspoons of seafood seasoning (Old Bay is suggested), and freshly ground black pepper. You’ll also need four 6-to-8 ounce black bass or sea bass fillets, 1/2 cup of hoisin sauce, 1/4 cup of orange juice, 2 scallions (finely chopped), and 2 tablespoons of fresh cilantro leaves. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Create four large rectangles of aluminum foil, each 16-18 inches long. Layer 1/4 of the beans, peppers, and bok choy in the center of three pieces of foil on a baking sheet; place the remaining foil piece aside. Top each vegetable pile with three ginger slices. Mix together the coriander, seafood seasoning, and black pepper, then sprinkle this blend over the fish fillets. Place the fillets on top of the vegetables. Whisk together the hoisin sauce and orange juice, and pour this mixture evenly over the fish. Garnish with scallions and cilantro, then fold the long edges of the foil up around the fish and roll tightly along the shorter sides to seal the packets. Bake for approximately 15 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure the fish is cooked through but still slightly translucent. Remove from the oven and serve directly from the foil packets.
